Its nice to have more PCU limit for both Online and Offline play, and with the addition of experimental mode building has gotten a little better.  Scripting is still missing, atleast from what I have seen. Basic/Intermediate scripting capability is still needed and atleast the addition of some already made scripts such as automatic LCDs. There is always the possibility. But overall there has been improvements since last time. It is still more of a creative builder than a survival, would like to have wildlife on planets or Spiders for survival mode to actually make it interesting and to have more of a reason to play survival other than just worrying about oxygen and power. Also still needs controller friendly improvements. So far so good, but only time will tell. Original Review on Ultimate edition.

title: Rage Swarm: Complete Edition
review_title: Two huge flaws ruin it all
review_text: Good game. NOT a survivors genre like others say. Autoshooter ARPG clearly made to be a mobile game, which is where the flaws come in.  Stats are linear unlocks, no real choices, just move forward in a straight line if you have required level and currency. You can't play previously beaten levels to grind, all you can do is play one of three challenge "survive 60 seconds" maps over and over for a miniscule amount of xp and gems. Gear is progressive unlock except from chests bought with gems. 1600 gems for 10 pulls of the best chest, or 200 for one pull. 15 gems per Challenge victory. See the issue? You get some from achievements, daily and weekly tasks, but they never reset. I.E. After done once they won't change and you never get more. Ever. So, not really daily or weekly  Also, having to replay the same level you died on means if it was a boss you literally cannot get in-stage upgrades as those drop from enemies at random upon kill. Gear upgrades require designs, also from chests.

There's roughly 11 or so heroes, with 6 individual hero specific achievements. Each hero is functionally unique, w/dif perks/cards. Basic run-down: The maps consist of 14 battles & 1 boss battle. You're awarded gold at B5, 200 diamonds at B10, and 2 epic chest keys at B15 - each stage. So if you fully clear 10 stages, boom-2k free diamonds. There's a seasonal "battlepass" you progress via daily and seasonal quests - it awards chest keys, gold, hero unlock progress, hero upgrade tokens, and diamonds. There's 6 pieces of gear across 5 sets, each piece/set gives dif buffs. DO NOT SPEND DIAMONDS on revives or pass skips.  Always have the Collector set equipped. Buy the 2x battle speed for 1k diamonds. Play two seasons.

title: Coloring Book: Complete Bundle - 396 drawings
review_text: There are 64 achievements worth 1,630 GS of which 22 are base game totaling 1,000 GS achievable within roughly 45min or so. The remaining 630 GS & 42 achievements are locked behind the 62 USD dlcs or 30 USD Complete Edition. The game suffers from being SUPER imprecise due to choosing a graphical floating brush averse to an actual pin-point cursor. You can use the base pallete or click on the pallete for a larger range. There's a fill/paint bucket, around 5 brushes, spray can, and eraser. The base game has 4 chapters with 3 pages each, totalling 12, and 2 full chapters: Jungle & Space, 6 pages each, totaling 12 together. There is also a free-draw whiteboard. The DLCs offer 29 additional pages per chapter type, so chapter 1 would have 90-120 pages IF you buy the DLC. I think with all DLC you get like 540 pages & some whiteboards. Overall, great for AH'ers and parents with younger kids but the coloring is unfulfilling, in my opinion.

review_text: Its a tough sim that is very rewarding and fun. However, its quite buggy and th graphics are not good. These things i can overlook cause the core mining is great. Also, loans are extremely expensive, the game in the beginning and middle is too grindy to a point that you realize youwont be able to afford a new claim unless you put in countless hours. For example, 1 cleanout on first claim will give you max 65oz gold. On avg 50ish. The next claim is 1.2 mil. Thats 24 cleanouts even before the way too pricey equipment and vehicle anywhere between 250k to 1 million. I avged 36oz gold per hour at the end so thats 33 hours of gameplay for new claim at least. title: Injection Ï€23 'Tabula Rasa'
review_title: Anticipated Finale to a Great Psychological Trilogy
review_text: I am one of the only Xbox players in the entire world ranked as 100%ing the entire trilogy, and Abramelin Games' work became some of my favorite survival horror I've played. This obscure series caters to the most niche of veteran horror fans, who desire punishing, rewarding gameplay and cryptic puzzles and story that have to be deciphered with heavy thought, with lite-ARG elements that push the envelope. If you are experienced in this genre and can overlook the edges of the games sometimes being rougher, they are an unforgettable experience. The Injection series is some of the most genuinely imaginative and stylish psychological horror I've seen, turning classic formulas into something truly it's own. Tabula Rasa shows the creator's gained experience, with new features added and use of MetaHumans tech for cinematics, delivering a content-filled finale fans will love, and newcomers will find more accessible.

review_text: First thing's first: you 100% will not unlock another hero within 15-20min as one reviewer said, let alone 2hrs, UNLESS you spend money. Cup Heroes isn't terrible for a free game but it also isn't best-in-class either. It's not an idle game but it is an auto-battler. There's roughly 11 or so heroes, with 6 individual hero specific achievements. Each hero is functionally unique, w/dif perks/cards. Basic run-down: The maps consist of 14 battles & 1 boss battle. You're awarded gold at B5, 200 diamonds at B10, and 2 epic chest keys at B15 - each stage. So if you fully clear 10 stages, boom-2k free diamonds. There's a seasonal "battlepass" you progress via daily and seasonal quests - it awards chest keys, gold, hero unlock progress, hero upgrade tokens, and diamonds. There's 6 pieces of gear across 5 sets, each piece/set gives dif buffs. DO NOT SPEND DIAMONDS on revives or pass skips.  Always have the Collector set equipped. Buy the 2x battle speed for 1k diamonds. Play two seasons.

review_text: You haveto be willing to think and observe, but once it all comes together, it's intensely immersive. Just get in there, don't worry about what the game expects u to do next, and just be you in that world. You'll figure it all out. The only downsides i've encountered, and the reason it's a 4 for the moment, is the lack of non-game options. It runs at 30 fps only (on X) with no performance mode or blur options for softening the frame flicker. You could normally counter this by speeding the R stick way up, but there's no aim specific sensitivity slider. Just the one. So you're kinda stuck optimizing for aiming. But if you're not an FPS snob or senstive to frame flick, none of this should stop u buying this game. It is a unique and intense experience with a game that assumes the best of you, rather than assuming you're a lazy, incurious moron, and i respect the hell outta that. Good hunting.

review_title: One plus one plus two plus one
review_text: Fantastic rendition of Clue! I have loved the board game for ages, playing it often and even buying the SNES game. I'm glad to say this version surpasses that version thanks to better presentation and game modes. Ultimate Detective and Clue Cards are both wonderful additions to the classic option and keeps the game from getting stale. There is DLC already available giving new boards with more promised. You also have the benefit of unlocking lore by completing certain tasks. I love this game! Developers: Any chance of getting movie skins as a DLC?

review_text: Pros + Dark, vibrant visuals + The Mimic is a great stalker enemy + The story and setting have so many layers to uncover and theorize + Honorable mention: Designed for fans and critics alike! I highly recommend playing with a Secret Ending guide, and make sure to find the Vacuum Pet at 5AM and store it in your inventory before starting New Game+. title: Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon - Excalibur Edition
review_text: Knew it was indie. But felt that, given the demo and footage, this game at least had potential. It really is much better than the standards I'd set for it. It does just a little bit of everything; fishing, scavenging, blacksmithing/gear crafting, cooking, has a great variety of play-styles to toy with thanks to all the dual-wielding possibilities and weapon types. Music, atmosphere and art direction are all above-average. There are slow-mo kill animations, varying landscapes and enemy types. And on that note I want to mention there's a cool feature involving a sketch book that you can take out pretty much whenever, and draw a sketch of whatever is in front of you. Overall there's a fairly large amount of content as well. This is a game I'd so far put on the same level as Oblivion (for the first time playing it), in terms of "a really cool, new dark fantasy RPG I can actually sink my teeth into." It's not perfect; there is some jank here. But what a breath of fresh air.

title: Medieval Dynasty - Complete Edition
review_title: FPS is not a review of the game.
review_text: Played this game for quite a while on Steam and am very glad to finally see it's console release. This is a city builder/town management type game with light survival mechanics. You'll be building a settlement and starting a new life for yourself after escaping war. It'll include raising crops, livestock, and ultimately a family. You are the overseer of your settlement and will have farmers, blacksmiths, tailors and such living and working within your village. This game is one of those types of games that many people find relaxing, as you hunt, gather resources, and tend to your village. I hope this proves to be a positive experience for Toplitz and they bring Wild West Dynasty over here as well. Medieval Dynasty is a well loved game on PC with a great community. Let's hope it continues here.

title: Medieval Dynasty - Complete Edition
review_text: This is a slow-build up type of game. You will be hungry, you will be thirsty, you will be poor. After the first year, you may have a few people in your town, but not many. They wont be skilled, and they have their own needs. Taxes suck, but not really. You have ample ability to make money by hunting, crafting, and prioritizing what your people do. Build 3 woodsheds, and 2 excavation sites. Build 10 houses and the worker areas. Know that this will skyrocket your taxes, which are due in the spring. When you notice how prices work, you notice that meat and simple crafted tools are easily produced and sell well. Also hunting bandits for coin and loot is not hard at all. You can change the difficulty and game options mid-play, which means you can turn off stamina, or get infinite carry weight. Really, if you set up your villagers well, you can sell firewood for a living, and slowly go from hunting to having a merchant empire. Clunky in a survival sandbox way, but fun and replayable too. GG

review_text: I appreciate what the game is trying to achieve. I'm a huge fan of art the clown and I'm old enough to appreciate the style. Unfortunately it's unplayable. The original alien movie is a good example of this. Sure the style builds tension, but it also difficult to navigate. I realize that I can turn off the film grain, but i don't want to have to sacrifice a part of the experience just to navigate. Just elevate the lighting just a bit and tone down the film grain a bit. review_text: TLDR: The game isn't really that bad. Aside from that, the only real issue is the AI, which has been improved recently- it's still not super great, but you're not getting rear ended every time you stop anymore. The other biggest complaint is about the rolling at pick-up/drop off spots and stop lights, truthfully, this can easily be avoided by enabling your parking break when at a pick-up/drop off and at stop lights you can just hold the break button down..like you do in real life, and your car will not roll. Ultimately, the game isn't top tier, but it's also not really as bad as some of the reviewers make it out to seem- of course there have been some updates since some of these reviews, if you're not super bother by no wheel support, i'd give the game a try you might enjoy it.

review_text: Beginning to end, this game was a lovingly crafted treasure. I loved the themes of compassion, mercy and restoration, mostly done without dialogue. Bosses were challenging and a little rough around the edges, but still fun for the most part. The devs NAILED the atmosphere. I wish I could explore this island in real life! Some short freezes that usually resolved themselves after a few seconds, only had to restart twice in 24 hrs of play. Devs are actively engaged with players on their Discord and looked into a bug I reported quickly. No spoilers, but I loved the ending. Overall, an absolute delight!

title: Death Howl: Deluxe Edition
review_text: Very addictive and very challenging until you get the hang of deck building and knowing enemies attacks. When I saw "soulslike" my initial thought was that it was going to not be good but I was pleasantly surprised. Music is great as well as the rest of the sound design. Art and card arts are cool especially the Gloom cards. I thought it was too short but that's probably because I have to find a new game now; 100% in 24h. Deck balancing could use work, Plains and Gloom deck are WAY better than Forest and Wind. The game almost forces you to stick to one type in each area except one and the Realmless cards are lackluster. Quests were an added challenge; most either put a special card in your deck or give you a boss fight. Very solid game. Ending made me cry a bit.

title: Death Howl: Deluxe Edition
review_text: Just cleared the first zone and it's been a while since a deck builder held my attention for this long. The pegan aesthetic is done very well and the soundscape has an ancient/isolated texture to it. The gameplay is challenging at first but you're encouraged to farm materials, teardrops (skill points), and exp. So it doesn't take long to start crafting a propper deck. The story itself is an examination of grief. You play as a mother who chases after her deceased son accross the realm that rests between life and death. As someone who enjoys brewing janky themed decks in MTG arena, I think Death Howl is a playground for mechanical experimentation and synergy hunting. I look foreward to chipping away at it over the coming weeks.

review_title: Brings A lot More To The Table
review_text: I've played a few survivor-likes, this one felt more unique. After the first area, game got way more intense and I understood what I'm supposed to be doing. You go through a dungeon like map, pick your pathway the spawn in an arena with just a few minutes to loot it. Being fast and uncovering the map is key along with getting all the gold you can for buying rewards. It's usually a pain to collect xp while moving through the map in these games but thankfully a magnet spawns in each arena and I usually head to it when I have about 30 seconds left. Thats what you mostly do in this game, but there's a lot more to it that makes it really cool. I feel like there's some more randomness to run which I appreciate. Was also surprised to see quest in my runs that even have cutscenes. There's a lot to progress, explore, soundtracks great, artstyle is great, all at half the price of a fortnite skin bundle. I definitely recommend this 1!

title: ROUTINE
review_title: This Is Why I Play Videogames
review_text: ROUTINE is the first game I've ever reviewed. I absolutely loved it. This is the first game in a very long time that not only held my interest from beginning to end, but also genuinely scared me. The retro world design, the tone and atmosphere were PERFECT. iC bots were great There were only a few things I wish were a little different. SPOILER I really enjoyed the designs of the Type 05s. I thought they were amazing and terrifying at the same time. They unfortunately were nowhere to be found in the second half of the game. They were however replaced by something much scarier. Some of the game's mechanics never came back either. In the second half, I never had to use the bullet projectile feature on the C.A.T. again. Same with the finger print puzzles. I still used the UV function a lot, but I enjoyed the idea of thinking outside the box to learn codes. Although there were parts of the game I wish were different, I still loved it. ROUTINE is a prime example of why I play videogames.

title: Against the Storm - Complete Edition
review_text: This charming City builder isnt a slow and easy process. It has a dark and slightly anxious overtone and relies on you having already known or played a few builder before hand. It holds your hand a gentle bit and guides you as it should, but overlooking and the map you realize you truly will figure it out alone. Thats a good thing! Its cozy and creepy, with a clean and sharp ps2 xbox era grim art. graphics are cool, the weather system is fun, and the overall objective will keep your returning till you succeed. Not a dev here, just another fellow player tired of these moronic review bombers. Play the game and make a decision on your own. Hope this helps.

title: Against the Storm - Complete Edition

title: OCTOPATH TRAVELER 0
review_title: Great Addition To The Octopath Traveler Series
review_text: Well designed JRPG that has great storylines, with fun challenging turn based combat in a beautiful created world to explore. The environments are unique with that 2.5D artistic style graphics. The variety of jobs, and skills really adds to the overall gameplay, the addiction is strong with this JRPG once you start playing. There is a lot of replay value with this JRPG. The characters you meet and add to your town are unique with each having their own background story. The town rebuilding is done really well for a JRPG, many props and features to add to your town simple design, but you can place buildings where you want, you unlock props as your town population increases. Octopath Traveler 0 is well worth the price to play.

title: SLEEP AWAKE
review_text: When people talk about video games being art, this is the sort of game they are referring to. Sleep Awake is dripping with unique style and oppressive horror atmosphere. The visuals, art direction, sound and music is among some of the best I have ever experienced in a video game. Unfortunately, as you might expect, this seems to come at the expense of the actual gameplay design, as it is mainly very simple stealth and puzzle solving, with very straightforward exploration. Still, the incredible aesthetics, worldbuilding and immersion more than make up for this shortcoming. It is more of an art horror experience, and less of a game, so have suitable expectations going in.

review_text: If you've ever wanted a realistic police sim where you play as an everyday patrol officer doing mundane things like writing tickets, towing cars, responding to traffic collisions, DUI checkpoints, and on occasion intervening in crimes like robbery or drug dealing, then this game is for you. Keep in mind, this is NOT L.A. Noire, a True Crime game, or any action-oriented cop game. This is an accurate procedural law enforcement game where you are assigned tasks during your shift and are held accountable for any and all mistakes. Also, keep in mind this is a low budget indie game, so don't expect AAA quality. There is nothing else like this on console right now, and I'm glad the devs released this game. The devs confirmed they will keep updating and adding new content as well.

title: Young Suns
review_text: To The Players: I highly urge you all to ignore all the negative comments about the games current lack of content and potential bugs. This is an Early Access Game and these things are to be expected, we are in the position to potentially help in the growth of these games and the comments should be used to do just that, by hopefully drawing the developers attention to the games problems so that they can be fixed and not just review bombing the game because it's unfinished. To The Developers: I think this game has a lot of potential and I'm excited to see how you continue to build and expand on this going forward. That being said, there are two main issues I've encountered while playing your game; Firstly, a lot of things seem to require the need of a specific material (Zips) that I have found to have a rather small drop rate. Secondly, the prices in the shops need to be balanced better, the ratio of how much favor you earn to how much things cost is a little ridiculous. Thank You

review_text: As someone who loves space and scifi, I think the setting is pretty sweet, especially since it takes place in our own solar system (Would love to be able to visit jovian moons like Europa, Io, and others further into development). Premise so far is good too, helping people recover from some revolution from a corporation (also would love to know more about the state of Earth, other planets, and why people are living in space in the first place). Theres some bugs here and there, but its been fine so far. Would recommend more customization options, like male and female presets, and other similar things. Some places also feel pretty empty and dead, so maybe adding in some more people doing things and some details would help make some places feel more alive. In other words, it has some good potential, and definitely needs time to improve.

title: Project Motor Racing: Year 1 Bundle
review_text: For starters even ACC as well as iRacing were rough at launch. That being said the day 1 patch helped enormously. As far as the bad comments on the handling, if you try to run a lap full speed while your tires\tyres are cold your gonna eat the wall. Put 3 or 4 medium speed laps in and the second your wheels heat up I swear the handling is great. Im an avid ACC player and all in for realism and Im saying this really does and certainly will end up rivaling ACC in realism.Its hard to explain because the ffb really feels nothing like ACC. Its almost in this you can feel the uneveness of the grid and it almost pulls/persuades you into a line. The more used to it I became the more it grew on me and I honestly really like it. I think this game is gonna slap!!  The hypercars are very difficult and super floaty though thats my only complaint. Have not tried them since I figured out the tire warmth trick we'll see. Its nice to have something to switch from Ac and ACC though......

review_text: This is worse than a toxic relationship, hear me out.  Now the penalty system is actually pretty good. If I cut a corner, I'll have to slow down unless I get a penalty. That I like as you won't get a penalty right away. Now you also can't rewind, which I don't hate. I'm actually quite fond of it. Unless you go wide and lose 2 places and now slower than everyone and then get the message to slow down or get a penalty. The penalty system is more stupid than a 4 year old. The kid would know that I shouldn't get a penalty, but apparently I should. That why I want to be able to rewind so I won't go mentally insane. Now if the penalty system was actually smart, this would never happen. I wouldn't even be writing this review. This feels like a toxic relationship because this game ain't that bad. I'll love to continue to play this game, but these type of stuff always happens to me. I love this game, but it will keep treating me like this. It's actually torture.

review_text: I really like the driving physics in this game. The graphics are great.   I cannot race the career, it will not save the game. It does not save any settings I put in, my bio, controller settings or anything.  Every time I start, It is from scratch.   The NPC drivers are ridiculous.  They don't break for corners, if they run you off the track, if you happen to be in front of them, and are immovable.   If you touch them, you are spun out, or over penalized.  I will play more and more if they Dev's fix these problems.

title: Project Motor Racing (PC)
review_text: Don't get me wrong this game shipped with bugs and poor optimization and should have been labeled an early access game, however I am only recommending this game as I feel the developers will make the necessary changes to make this a good racing game in the future. I think all the negative comments are a result of the hype behind this game which I get as I felt the same way with AC Evo on release. Overall the bones for a good racing title are there but there needs to be significant changes. AI: The AI is in an atrocious state. Racing single player is unplayable in its current state as AI has no awareness of the player or other AI for that matter. The AI remain on a single line and don't deviate much. When trying to bump them off line they are like rocks and don't move one bit. When going to make a pass on a turn or straight in some instances they well collide into you sending you off track giving you a time penalty.

title: JDM: Japanese Drift Master
review_text: Time played: 22 hours 38 minutes Console: Series X Price paid: Free Play Days Achievements: 26/26 TLDR; If you're a fan of drifting and/or japanese car culture, this is a must own. Wait for a sale. I started this game with pretty low expectations, but was quickly taught just how much love was poured into this title. Cars look, sound and feel great to drive. The world is interesting and beautiful. The story is engaging and interesting, with characters that I came to enjoy and wanted more of. (Please do a sequel!) On to the bad; Framerate is inconsistent even in performance mode. The world, though beautiful, is completely devoid of any life. Some objects around the map cannot be broken when driving through them while others can. This makes for a confusing experience. Lighting is inconsistent across the board. Driving in cockpit view is hard to see due to a "tint filter" on the windshield, making everything near impossible to see around midday/night. Wait for a sale!

title: JDM: Japanese Drift Master
review_title: An Absolute Must Buy For Any Initial D Fan!
review_text: This is basically the best Initial D game I have ever played. The only one that really captures the feel of the anime. The setting is very similar, it has the story explained in manga comics that have sound effects to go with them, and overall it just feels like a love letter to that franchise and setting. The graphics also strike an attractive art style that's somewhat anime inspired, sort of reminds me of the newer Persona games. The car selection is great, half are officially licensed, the other half are obvious and well represented, all Japanese modern classics. You have 3 competition classes, drift, grip racing, and drag racing, and they remind me of the better Need For Speed games. Physics are fun to play with, music totally hits the Initial D animes, overall I am very satisfied with what I got.

title: The Tomb Raider & Soul Reaver Remastered Bundle
review_text: They work fine,you just have to understand how Lara works. When you want to do a running jump make her walk to the edge then draw her guns then she'll do the hop back and hold jump right after she starts moving forward and she'll jump like shes supposed to,she needs at least two steps before she can do a long jump. You can also do her back and side flips with guns drawn, its easiest to reset the camera behind her while doing the flips. And for the camera remap the look button from RS to RB and double click it to reset it behind her when it gets funky. RT gets her out of the water and will make her grab ledges while stepping off of an edge, you have to slightly step off instead of full force running off. I hope this helps those wanting to use modern controls, it took a lil bit to figure this out but i have absolutely no issues with them after learning this myself.

title: The Tomb Raider & Soul Reaver Remastered Bundle
review_text: Some remasters are total overhauls, and some are borderline remakes. This is admittingly a more modest approach to remastering the original classics from the PS1, but I appreciate how faithful this is to the original trilogy I grew up with. The design on the levels, the controls and Lara's design is very suitable to how we remember her back in the 90's. Modern controls is very much welcome and the ability to switch between the moden visuals and the classic graphics is such a treat, I wish every remaster had this. The Tomb Raider Remastered Trilogy feels like I am coming back home to something I have been without for a very long time, and I am glad it is back.  Good job Aspyr! - A 25 Year Fan.

review_text: To get comparisons out of the way: Cry of Fear, Condemned 1, Stalker, Resident Evil 4. Resource management heavy, but nothing too restrictive. The combat has some jank but is quite fun and very tense. In the earliest part of the game you have to run from common enemies, but this is only for few sections in the first 20 minutes. It's got amazing set pieces, some extremely tense moments, and very few jumpscares. The few puzzles are easy. All melee weapons break, but there are an abundance of them, and the crafting system lets you repair and upgrade certain weapons. Use your equipment, don't get attached, if it breaks, improvise new weapons. Itâ€™s not a shooter, there are guns, but they're more of a panic button than something to use in every situation. I wouldnâ€™t consider this game difficult, itâ€™s challenging without feeling unfair. No handholding, no yellowpaint. I disliked a few short sections but overall I really enjoyed it, good story, good gameplay, really cool horror moments.

title: Monsters are Coming!
review_title: 53/62 14hr early review: Will be a 5 star without bugs
review_text: I say "early review" as I rarely review a game until I fully beat it (all achievements), but as of right now, I don't think it's possible on Xbox. Bugs holding it back on Xbox: -Tower upgrades. There's a glitch where, typically after an Endless run or just randomly, towers won't upgrade when you place their duplicate on them. It's not visual as I was able to consume 5 of the same tower before the Ark and it remained at level one. There's a number of unlocks tied to upgrades, and obviously as a TD game I NEED strong towers so, pretty bad. A restart only sometimes fixes it. -Poor optimization/crashes. MaC! suffers the Soulstone Survivors effect where, because it's pretty, it's more resource intensive. By Endless Ark 6 I was stuttering and had to quit, with a score of just 20k. There's a cheevo for 100k/1mil score so it needs to be fixed as it also causes crashes. -Shrink tile function is broken. Freezes your game until you hit B but doesn't stick. Devs, please fix. Love it otherwise.

title: Kiosk
review_text: I got this game on sale for $2.50. For the price this is a good game. The story mode offers 3-4 hours of gameplay. This is basically a cooking game with a little mix of scary. Despite it being a scary game there was actually only a handful of jump scares. Seriously. 3 of the scares got me which was funny.  This game sometimes felt stale to the point where i actually felt as if this game were a real job because all you're doing is cooking the same foods over and over.  There's 3 game modes. First is the story mode, then endless and then relax mode. In endless mode you cook continuously, but if the timer runs out you lose. In relax mode you simply just cook people's order until you just get bored. Like I said for the price this is a good game, but I can't see myself playing this after beating the story mode and I think many will agree with that.  Also 10 achievements to obtain. They are really easy to get if that's your thing.

review_text: Not bad, not great but good. If you're bored with time to fill and have a few bucks to spend, play it. As a heads up for what you're getting into, this game is nowhere near scary, you never leave the kiosk and you have around 2hrs of storymode gameplay. As for why its a 3, the plot kinda falls flat when 90% of the game is spent cooking the food, and bc that majority only leaves 10% left for the plot/horror it's hard to care abt why you're actually there at the kiosk. Additionally, the restricted setting and repetition of the game make progression feel more like a chore rather than effort spent to unlock a greater purpose. If there were to be a kiosk 2 I'd love to be able to explore more, that'd make room for new tasks to help spice up the gameplay. As for the plot, make orders less tedious in exchange for longer cooking time and let me talk to npcs as I cook to better understand whats goin on! review_text: I'm no stranger to difficult run n gun games. I've played Cuphead, multiple Contra games, and Hard Corps: Uprising. This one took it a little too far. "We wanted the hardest difficulty to be considered the standard." Well, fine, but with extremely stingy check points and low health, it felt like you were asking for a near perfect run as the "expected" difficulty. Normal should've been just that, "normal, the intended". The background shooting could've used a more modern dual stick setup that was toggled rather than forcing you to stand still while firing. Upgrades were also disappointing. Limited Ammo, can't stop it once active, and you can only hold one at a time. This isn't a BAD game. But its expectations are a little high of itself.

title: Demonschool
review_text: Demonschool has everything I wanted in a game, plus stuff I didn't know I needed.  Faye and her crew hunt demon between classes and homie hangouts, to stop the impending apocalypse. title: Disney Dreamlight Valleyâ€”Ultimate Edition
review_text: I am completely enchanted. It's the best of Disney blended with the fun crafting and gathering experiences of Harvest Moon, the simulation and customization experiences of the Sims, and the amazing friendship and neighborly joys of Animal Crossing. It's easily one of the best games I've ever played. That being said, there's a lot of bugs. The game crashes frequently -- especially if I am editing the neighborhood. Spend too long adjusting things and the game will crash. Do too much crafting and the game will crash. Spend too long without manually hitting the save button and the game will crash. There's a lot that needs work, but somehow, the bugs don't take away from the game play. There's a reassurance that playing will reveal the bugs and developers will take notice and make the necessary fixes to keep the gameplay fresh and fun. Fingers crossed.

title: Goat Simulator 3 - Starter Edition
review_title: Legendary sequel to awesome sandbox game
review_text: If you like sandbox games, loved and/or played the original Goat Simulator, or both, then you need to play Goat Simulator 3. This sequel takes everything great with the original Goat Simulator and cranks it up to 100. The map is huge and way bigger than the maps from the first game. In fact, the entire map is one large island separated into different cities or areas. The game doesn't fall short of funny gags or references, and you're sure to find something that references another game or film. You can now also customize your goat with the Wardrobe, where you can pick different gear or goat/goat skins. And now, for the first time ever, Goat Simulator goes online with online multiplayer with 4-player co-op, and you can either mess about or participate in some of the special mini-games scattered around the map. Goat Simulator 3 is a vast improvement over its predecessor in various ways. Definitely get this if you're a Goat Simulator fan or like sandbox games. It's worth your time.

I had extremely high hopes for this game when it got announced. I can assure you, they did not disappoint. Goat Simulator 3 is a solid sequel. It still has the same feel as the original, just modernized and upgraded. Rather than having multiple maps, you have one large map to explore. It still has the same whacky-fun the original game provided, but only better. There are plenty of places to explore. Plenty of collectibles to get if thats your thing. Lots of items to unlock. Hilarious NPC dialogue as always. Tons of little easter eggs, which i really enjoy. And of course, TONS of chaos! More than the original for sure. Coffee Stain did not disappoint with this game. Highly suggest this! Much better with friends too.

title: Disney Dreamlight Valleyâ€”Wishblossom Ranch Edition
review_text: I am completely enchanted. It's the best of Disney blended with the fun crafting and gathering experiences of Harvest Moon, the simulation and customization experiences of the Sims, and the amazing friendship and neighborly joys of Animal Crossing. It's easily one of the best games I've ever played. That being said, there's a lot of bugs. The game crashes frequently -- especially if I am editing the neighborhood. Spend too long adjusting things and the game will crash. Do too much crafting and the game will crash. Spend too long without manually hitting the save button and the game will crash. There's a lot that needs work, but somehow, the bugs don't take away from the game play. There's a reassurance that playing will reveal the bugs and developers will take notice and make the necessary fixes to keep the gameplay fresh and fun. Fingers crossed.

review_text: I have a 7.2.4 media room with two 13 inch subs and this game's bass pressurizes the room. The bass response is subterranean and easily dips below 20hz. This is not only bass you can hear but feel. As for the game, this is Gen 9 Geometry Wars. It's more difficult with the changing zones and more enemies onscreen. There are roguelike elements like choosing powerups mid batlle and a recharging super blast. As great as the audio is, it is 2.1 front channel stereo only with no surround or Atmos. Also there is no HDR and the neon explosions and particles would greatly benefit from a wider color gamut. No 120hz VRR but it maintains a solid 60hz even when the screen is filled with effects.  Buy this game, your subwoofers will love you and your neighbors will hate you.

review_text: This game is good. As the title suggests, it is short (around 20 hours) and slightly difficult at times (some areas and bosses being challenging) with a color loot system like popular looter shooters. Thematically, this game is the kitchen sink of other top games: feels like a mix of Cyberpunk, Doom, Metro, Titanfall, Dead Space and so on...  I was pleasantly surprised for 3GB and under $20. It also has a new game plus feature so you can carry all your gear and stats over when going for another ending (there are several endings tied to achievements). There is a skill tree to cater to your playstyle that you unlock halfway through the game. There are "totems" in the world that add some rogue-lite elements. Only complaints are the lack of descriptions in the stats menu (mostly related to gear), and the ending being abrupt without elaborating on your specific ending. It isn't an RPG, but does have a couple RPG elements. Refer to the title of this review...

review_text: This is Dead Cells set in a bleak somewhat banal sci-fi setting. The art style is excellent with the damp lighting and neo noir color grading. The melee and gunplay feel weighty and significant, you can feel every pull of the trigger and sword swing. But this game has shortcomings. Like DC, the movement is floaty and imprecise and the controls seem off like they programmed in an extra frame of input lag. Like other small indie games, there is no support for HDR10, 120hz VRR or Dolby Vision or Atmos. The audio is mostly confined to the front stage with little surround but if you're a bass head, this game has deep tight punchy LFE that will test your subwoofers.  Overall a decent game that I'm glad I didn't pay full price for. A solid B-.

title: Atari 50: Game + DLC Bundle
review_text: Going in, you should know that this is not just a collection of Atari games, it is a playable museum and piece of history. Many people will hit the "X" button to play the games collection, but they are missing out on the main product. The UI for the timelines is very well done, as are the interviews, restored pictures of history such as cabinet descriptions and art, and more. Digital Eclipse went above-and-beyond in showing how video games got their start and why they are still around today.

title: Atari 50: Game + DLC Bundle
review_title: New high bar for retro collections
review_text: This is such a lovingly consructed piece of software. Somehow they made a collection of games where playing the actual games is frequently the least compelling part. It is both a documentary and a museum. The interviews are terrific and edited really well. There's 3D-rendered product boxes and high-res scans of arcade flyers, development planning documents, and even business cards. I have no personal nostalgia, much of this happened well before I was born, so this is covering a bit of a blind spot for me. What a fantastic way to learn about the origins of popular video games.

title: Atari 50: Game + DLC Bundle
review_text: Interviews and history are great of how it all began and to play it in order as you go along is awesome. We've all had our share of ''old atari games'' with all the rereleases and such but with addition of some ''newer'' never before rereleased (Jag and Lynx,+) made the purchase of this collection worth it for me. Got a Jag at Kaybee toys back in 95 on the cheap! Had a nice collection, gathering it all back is too much $. Would love to see more Jag and Lynx games, especially the ones that are hard to get or expensive to grab. Jag: Iron Soldier, Flip out, Kasumi ninja, White men can't jump, Ultra vortek, and IWar. Lynx: Dirty Larry, Battle Wheels, Bubble trouble, power factor and Electro cop.  (just to name some games I would enjoy seeing added as DLC). Maybe Jag CD?

title: Strike Pack
review_text: An enemy force threatens thousands of innocent lives with its army and It's your job to take them down before that happens. In your ready for battle hellicopter, you'll use a machine gun, missles and strafing maneuvers across seven missions to take down the enemy. Every mission does take place on the same map but it's different areas each time. If you fly by an area that gives you an on screen danger warning, you're not meant to be there yet. Just fly by because those enemies are extra strong on purpose until it's time to go there. You'll have three lives across all seven missions so engage the enemies carefully. You do get full health, fuel and ammo upon respawning. Be sure to double check those stats when starting new missions because they sometimes auto replenish. Even so, if you manage resources well enough, there's plenty for all the missions. Albeit short, Strike Mission is fun to play. It has easy achievements and a few missions that do offer a good challenge.

review_title: Fans of Chambers will really appreciate this one
review_text: The King in Yellow isn't just a plot allusion here - the world this takes place in fits right into the anthology, like a modern dystopian take on some setting elements from The Repairer of Reputations mixed with the art focus of The Mask. The creators clearly love the source material. In a world oversaturated with Lovecraft, this deep focus on Chambers is refreshing indeed. Gameplay is standard horror walking sim fare, but just dripping with atmosphere and done right in nearly every way. If you get a chance to read the actual book, do so first as you'll appreciate this so much more.

review_title: A tight concept spread too broad
review_text: A cRPG with minimal (and I would argue, disingenuously framed) character choices, skills, and progression needs an impactful narrative, compelling story, and realized characters to justify its minimal roleplaying. The narrative could work, but the story (the written scene to scene narration and dialogue) is stretched too thinly. I see a world where this could have been a great 2 hour experience that is instead 10 hours, manufacturing game mechanics that are only executed perfunctory or are abandoned soon after introduction. I think the narrative (and especially the flat characters, player character included) is just not crafted well enough, and rather than tighten scope to polish its flaws to create a stronger story, the scope was widened in hopes those writing flaws are obfuscated by, to be blunt, dishonest time wasting and false gameplay promises. I wouldn't be this bothered if I didn't think there was potential for better work in the future.

Just as an example, I have made Voldemort leading the goblins and Sauron leading the orcs as direct competitors trying to take over Narnia. I've made countless D&D characters from my Tabaxi wild magic sorcerer to my dwarf gunlinger and my dragonborn druid. Every single aspect is customizable. Want to make an army of ratmen who ride velociraptors and have orc strength? You can! Want to make Elsa from Frozen leading the Hobbits on a conquest of Faerun? Knock yourself out! title: Suzerain Expanded Edition
review_text: The game is set in a fictional world with a lot of choices that have long game consequences. It's essentially a "choose your own adventure story" for politics on steroids.  The game has a pace that's a little slow by design to build tension and weight to your decisions, and those decisions aren't like Telltale where they're meaningless.  Even "casual" decisions leave you second guessing something that was very beneficial previously, and who you can and can't trust. Biggest con:  No tutorial wouldn't matter so much except it's fairly clunky as you struggle with accessing information in the visible UI, but it's not **** or frustrating enough to walk away. Definitely worth $10.  Can't recommend at $20+ if you're expecting more than compelling text. The more I play, the more nuanced many of the choices are such as when politeness matters, and when being a jerk is beneficial.  Easily 20 hours or more worth of play in this Machiavellian masterpiece. 9.5/10 for the genre

review_text: So excited to be HUNGRY. In the two days that i've played this game after release i've gotten my a*s kicked by another peasant (Gave me PTSD from KCD 1), used a sheep named Ignacius as bait for wolves, got eaten by wolves, Ignacius was also eaten by wolves, reloaded save to save Ignacius, killed wolves, Victory Baaa'd with Ignacius. I have also relearned new combat mechanics, they've changed since the first game but overall feels better and more fluid (Combo's are much easier, but master striking is much more risky but so damn satisfying). I've done a variety of side quests such as, fist fighting, hunting wolves, brewing potions, plenty of combat, stealing items for people, saved a guy from wolves just to get jumped by poachers, and etc. Great side missions that didn't feel like fetch quests. title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance â€“ Saga Bundle
review_text: This game is epic, pure and simple. The main story could be a blockbuster movie, and has it all for a medieval adventure: romance, swordfights, revenge, gigantic battles, betrayal, castle sieges, grand heists, court intrigue, and so much more, all set against the backdrop of an authentic recreation of 1400s Bohemia. Aside from the main story, the side quests are brilliant. There are no "go here, fetch this and come back" style quests. Every single side quest has some kind of interesting storyline full of twists and turns. I enjoyed every minute of this game, and can't wait to play through it again once hardcore mode comes out, not to mention the DLCs they have planned. This is a must play if you want an RPG worth sinking 100 hours into.

review_text: Forced update that coincides with a $40 "upgrade" in the form of an anniversary edition and now it crashes in the main menu. I never had issues before. Half the creations are dependent on the unofficial patch, which is now exclusive to the anniversary edition, making things you BOUGHT useless because THEY SHARE A CREATION STORE. review_text: I haven't been able to get into many games recently. None really held my attention long enough. This game, however, made me accidently do a near 10hr session without even realizing on my first time booting it up. Expect a learning curve (maybe an hour or two) but afterwards it is just difficult enough to make me think and to make some genuine danger for the whiskers, but not so much that I feel as though I can't salvage a bad situation (winter can be rough but also quite thrilling to surmount). The level of verticality you can use is amazing. I've built towers of buildings and very deep hidden mineshafts and mushroom farms. It makes the building so much more engaging (I don't recall the tutorial telling you but you'll really want to use layer mode for building vertically and for mining [z to enter, x to exit, f go up layer, v go down layer]) Can't recommend enough! If you're on gamepass just try an hour. If not, I still think it is worth the price given what I've played so far.

Unfortunately, the modernization can be as much a detriment to the original experience as it does bolster it. I feel like some of the original vision was lost in translation and sometimes the game suffers for it. On the other hand, the pre-rendered 90s cutscenes are begging to be updated because the difference between OG and modern Kate is extremely jarring, almost to the point where they feel like different characters. Highly recommend picking up OG Syberia first if you are new to the series, it runs on basically anything and you can easily upscale the resolution yourself. Basically freeware. Buy this on sale

title: Farming Simulator 25: Highlands Fishing Edition (PC)
review_text: Quick PSA on how to install a mod on this version no worries if you already bought it or use Game Pass. First, the mod folder wonâ€™t be there until the game creates it. The best way I found to trigger that is by launching the game, go to the internal mod browser, and install one mod from there. After that, youâ€™re free to grab mods from anywhere. The mod folder will be located at: \Users\(yourusername)\AppData\Local\Packages\GIANTSSoftware.FarmingSimulator25PC\LocalCache\Local\mods Not in the XboxGames folder. Note that the AppData folder is hidden by default in Windows. To make it visible, go to the top of File Explorer, click View, then hover over Show, and select Hidden items. Just drop .zip files into the mods folder, and the game will recognize them. Make sure to open the .zip file you downloaded sometimes it contains another .zip inside. Youâ€™ll want that inner one for it to work. Use an app like WinRAR to extract it directly into the mods folder.

review_text: As far as retro-like games go, this one is great. Jump scares have variety and avoid being too predictable. Escaping house 13 was fun, a good mix of exploration and simple stealth. I particularly like the little details. Each house is different, not just some copy/paste job, each one has a little story to it and they collectively tell a narrative that ties in with the final house. Calling the stealth "simple" is generous. These cultists are paid by the hour at minimum wage. You walk about twice their speed (and you can even sprint). They literally have tunnel vision, are near-sighted and are deaf. Dang, you even have to get caught at least 6 times for an inconsequential game over.  If you skip deliveries (they don't effect ending/story) you'll back in under 5 minutes. All of that considered, this was still very fun well worth the time and money. If you're after achievements, you'll get them in a few hours, even without a guide.

title: Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection
review_text: I'm happy to have this Kollection on a modern konsole, but I have a few koncerns. I think the menu interface is a bit excessive; instead of cycling between each version of every title it would be simpler to pick a title and then choose which version of that title you'd like to play. The fatality training isn't available for each version. Also I'm very glad MK4 is here, but why not add MK4 Gold also? You have different versions of each game but not for MK4? Deadly Alliance handheld, but not a konsole version? Lastly, each game could have been remastered instead of ported and this might have fixed a lot of the original issues. Ex: MK1 SNES has a big input lag, and MK Trilogy looks dull and loads very slow as it did on PS1. In konclusion, it's a great kollection, but it's not perfect and there's room for improvement.

title: Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection
review_text: While I can't speak to online play, anyone giving this less than 5/5 stars just for the fact of what all we get in this package, are some ridiculous spoiled modern gamers!!! Put online gaming aspect aside and just look at what all we get here, how well it all is done and looks! Unless you had an Xband modem for you Genesis or SNES, you didn't play any of this online in it's time (definitely not the arcades). That should be just bonus to have at all here. Take me back to the 1990's, back to my teen years, and hand me this collection just like this (along with hardware that would play it, lol). My jaw would had been on the floor with my pants full of what I had for dinner. Never would I had been able to imagine having what we have here, not this well done and definitely not everything added to enhance the fun.  I was happy to just have blood in my Sega port and to sometimes be near a machine without a line & some quarters in my pocket. The documentary timeline is it's own treasure!

Menu button works for some games but not others (for which = block instead?), view button is a long hold (?), motion jutters when playing in "wide" mode, I could go on, but it all points to one question: WHY? Why were these obviously bad choices made for the UX? Believe me, I hate to complain, and while I do love these games, none of these executive decisions make sense! title: ARC Raiders - Deluxe Edition
review_title: From a Casual Gamerdad (and general PvP disliker)
review_text: Right off the bat, I want to let anyone reading this know that I generally do not like PvP games. I'm a 35 year old dad with limited gaming time and my reflexes are not what they used to be or at the level of the younger kids that play these kinds of games. That being said, I absolutely love this game and I hope this review can convince you why the $40 price tag is worth it, even if you are on the fence, or like me, do not have a lot of time to play, or generally do not like extraction shooters or PvP. The team at Embark did a fantastic job of creating a world with threatening AI that it naturally forces player cooperation and has created some of the most memorable gaming moments for me in recent memory. Moments where (in a PvP game), nearly the entire map came together to kill the ARC enemies and extracted together. Not a single shot fired at the other teams.  Embark did such a great job of making this such an accessible extraction shooter. Get this game.

title: RoboCop: Rogue City - Collection
review_title: Almost perfect. Update: NG+ added, and it's AWESOME!
review_text: Sure, there are some little AA jank issues, mostly having to do with human facial and body animations, and there are a few audio issues I hope they can fix with a patch, otherwise, these devs figured it out. They started from the end of the 1st sequel, and continued on from there. And it's pretty great. They actually kind of invented a new genre of FPS game here: things like ammo and cover are trivial when you're Alex Murphy! And that is ultimately who you ARE in this game, if you choose, because, for the 1st time I think, you actually get to explore the psychology of being RoboCop in a videogame! But the action never gets boring, new abilities keep things fresh, and the writing is sometimes sharply funny, and heartfelt when needed. I could've used more music during downtimes, of which there are many, but they are filled with great moments of being a beat cop serving the public trust, solving mysteries, filling cop quotas; decisions you make actually affecting the world down the road.

review_text: My first and biggest complaint...i would have bought this on steam but i expected this to be playable on xbox cloud like dq3. Lots of little side content and mini bosses have been added...the addition of physical abilities in particular gives you a lot more versatility in DQ1, and promotes the prince of midenhall from the dumb brute that he was into a weakness shredding brute at least. The grind is still there, especially on the draconian difficulty...some bosses are a little gimmicky, i beat the knight abberant in Damdara by wearing spiked armour and healing/boosting def every round, two other bosses were beaten by spamming the counter attack skill Cop Out and hoping for the best.  DQ2 still feels like a grindfest (no complaints here) with certain bosses on higher difficulties basically requiring that you have certain skills (magic barrier, insulatle) or you'll watch your team get fire breath-ed to death really quick.

review_text: Maybe I'm in the minority, but the first was better. The first few hours of gameplay feel empty, boring, and the story just takes itself too seriously. title: The Outer Worlds 2
review_text: The story and gameplay trump the first title. But there are features from the first game missing. You can't rest or skip time. The visual upgrades to armor are now gone. Which is odd considering we now have a 3rd person camera. And the companions all have unique looks that if upgraded sport a visual change. There are still features missing that were requested in the first game. Notibly the lack of a barbershop and a FOV slider for your weapon. I'd like to see faction disguises added.     Also, the game has graphical issues. It suffers from pop in and out. Screen tears along the sides and bottom of the screen. It gets grainy the longer the play session and also has ghosting too.     The story this go around is more thought provoking and grounded. The companions feel alive and interact not just with the world, but the story. Its clear they focused more on story telling this go around and I look forward to future updates.  At the end of the day, this game is great. GOTY

review_text: Do not get this game if you are looking to kill aliens because you will not get that chance you will however get to fight the invaders, hunt animals, and learn to live the life of a Na'vi warrior. Eat, cook, harvest, hunt & craft > All the systems are easy to use just find the appropriate bench > This game does have co - op you can play with friends > This game incorporates the movies in the back story only it is its own entity > Combat plays alot like Call of duty, with the exception that you can climb trees and jump like a maniac > Stealth is in this game as a mechanic (the people in comments stating their is not stealth are just bad at it) Speaking from experience here people literally took out a whole outpost with stealth.  > The games Physics are incredible you move with the water, you take fall damage and you have to harvest plants like a forager > weakpoints are your friend The only bad part is that i got lost getting through the prologue Navigation needs better explanation.

title: Complete Edition - Avatar: Frontiers of Pandoraâ„¢
review_text: I've never played a game where I felt like the world was truly ALIVE like this! The sound design when you're exploring the forest is incredable. The graphics are stunning too! I've seen some people say they get lots of blur when running but I have performance mode on (with motion blur off) and it looks amazing. I've also had very very few frame drops, most of which have happened when loading up the game from the instant game response thing on Xbox. The only thing I wish was better is the gunplay, but I think they may have made it intentionally wonky because you're a Na'vi, so using the bows feels great but the gun play is sluggish. Overall I am really really enjoying this game FOR WHAT IT IS and I think many people fail to do that. It doesn't do anything groundbreaking that we've never seen before, but what it does SO WELL is make you FEEL like a real Na'vi warrior. So if you decide to get this game, try to go into it with an explorer mindset and less of an "FPS" mindset.

review_text: *Fair warning: I backed this game on Kickstarter* The art is delightful, perfectly serving up an atmosphere and aesthetic further augmented by the music. The gameplay has been super tasty to me thus far, and I can't quite decide if I like the exploration or the cooking more - which might sound like a bad thing for a game with "Chef" in the title, but far from it. While a bit slow to open up at first, I'm already impressed by the scope, and am eager to progress and discover more! On the down side, this game is clearly made for PC first. While the console port appears exceptionally well done, things like the Inventory (similar to games like Stardew Valley), and some lack of context sensitive commands are indicative of these roots. Not at all a deal-breaker, but your mileage may vary. Worth a try for fans of cozy, cooking, and more!

title: Wreckreation
review_text: As a longtime Burnout fan, and Burnout Paradise Pervert, I am loving this game. There's so much in it already and so much potential for creativity. It feels, looks, and sounds incredible. I'm loving the soundtrack. It is not a polished as the Criterion games, but it was never promised to be. This is not 2008 and this is not a $60 AAA release. This is 2025 and Wreckreation is an incredibly ambitious indie game from a tiny team. I'm so glad it's out and I hope it will be a success. I fear that with this niche genre, no cross-platform multiplayer (which I never expected), and the dire state of global politics, success will be elusive, but the game is absolutely worth $40. This is what Three Fields Entertainment has been building towards since Dangerous Golf, and I'm so glad to finally have my hands on it. It has crashed on me twice in LiveMix mode but all my progress was saved when I booted it back up. I really hope this game gets a few little updates, and the community it deserves.

review_text: To manual save just quit to main menu. At first a bug in crashing and losing progress as only issue I had with the game until manual save. After completing it I have changed my mind. Multiple endings due to choices throughout on a morality spectrum of selfish or compassion in choices. Only negative would be lack of invincibilty frames on dodge rolls but its only an issue against the wolves. title: Atomfall Complete Edition
review_text: I love exploration so this game was perfect for me. There isn't a clear direct quest line so taking your time to explore the world is satisfying and rewarding. I played on Survival so combat was a bit challenging early on, but you're not meant to take on mobs that early in the game. Just save often, pick your battles, play stealthy, and don't be afraid to run away or run past enemies. They will not chase you far and will lose sight of you quickly. The inventory is EXTREMELY limited but but on top of using the pneumatic tubes, you can use almost anything for storage. BARD crates, metal detector caches, crates, backpacks, dead bodies (not enemies), etc.  The story was interesting and after playing this game for 60 hours, I got every achievement, every ending, and pretty much did everything.  I loved it and this game easily gets 5 stars from me.

title: Atomfall Complete Edition
review_title: Extremely bad start, but gets much better.
review_text: It was a mistake for the devs to give you so few options for survival at the start.  You're meant to avoid and run from combat at the start which does not make for a fun time.  Stealth starts out terrible because of loud stealth kills and enemies that give you almost no openings.  Having to buy skill trees was also a dumb decision.  Once you find some decent guns and have a nice stack of ammo it gets better.  There is a much larger emphasis on survival than something like base Fallout.  You are a weak and pathetic loser at the start, so focus on the main story, explore, avoid combat and look for recipes/trade items.  You'll unlock cooler stuff later on.  Only glitch I've had is the sound one(series X).  You can have fun with the game, but you have to play a very specific way.

title: Super Fantasy Kingdom (Game Preview)
review_title: It's yet another Hooded Horse game...
review_text: And like every other Hooded Horse game I've ever played, it's a fantastic idea implemented as poorly as possible.  To the point that I wonder if HH deliberately backseat drives games until they're painfully tedious and unfun.  Like...  On purpose.  For reasons beyond my kenning. Anyway, SFK.  It's a very boring puzzle game masquerading as a wave defense, masquerading as a city builder, masquerading as a roguelite.  But the only kind of game it actually is, is a puzzle game.  And more in the escape-room vein than the jigsaw.  You have to do everything in exactly the right order, at exactly the right time, or you lose.  And if you lose, you get to start all over again from the very beginning.  Yay. The first five or six days of play are a twenty minute long, absolute yawning snoozefest in which you do nothing except micromanage your incredibly limited workforce in order to grow your incredibly limited resources so that you can maybe survive to day twenty.  It is agonizingly unfun.

title: THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD 2: Remake
review_text: Get your trigger fingers and reflexes ready for the undead have returned to wreak havoc in The House of the Dead 2. This remake brings back everything I missed from originally playing this on the Dreamcast along with some upgrades. This on rails arcade shooter runs smooth from start to finish. Sure the voice lines have been redone by different actors and some of the boss creature sounds have been tweaked but if you lower the nostalgia glasses a little bit, it's still the same campy dialogue and a blast to play since 98. Graphics and character models have been vastly improved with everything being more gritty and detailed. Achievements have been added and unlock even with cheats active. Which btw, cheats can only be active by first acquiring the code from beating the game. It'll take several playthroughs to get them all but each run is short with multiple paths to take for replayability. A friend can join in the fun as well. So a great remake and I hope to see the third one rise again.

With a graphic style from decades ago, limited ammo supply and a mysterious story, it has the right setup. Which it does execute well because I did like how the story and events are fleshed out. It's just what happened when it came to the controller layout? RT for aim and B to shoot was a terrible idea. However, if you can get past that, the only other real negative is getting stuck on everything. Thankfully there's a generous jump feature that overcomes getting caught on everything, especially when running from dinos. In the jungle, they're nonstop, you have to run. With easy achievements, good dino design, dino sounds and a decent story; I liked it. Mostly devs, improve upon the controls for the sequel please.

title: Pacific Drive
review_text: First of all, i have over 100 hours of playtime on PS5.  This is a survival/roguelike with spooky atmosphere. This game has one of the coolest survival mechanics. Your car is what keeps you alive. its a mobile safe zone. Well.... almost, you have to keep it up and running and the doors intact. Every part of the car adds to its ability to shield you from the hazards in the zone. You start with a simple station wagon and eventually beef it up to a mobile fortress.  There are so many awesome upgrades you can customize your car with, spotlights, extra storage, decals and paint. Heck why not add a huge tank of gas to the roof? You can do this and much more, how you customize it is up to you.  Your real safe area is the garage. it is where you return with all of the goodies you collected to create upgrades for your car and yourself. To make it even better, you can upgrade the garage too. Oh and don't pass on the radio, the soundtrack for this game is absolutely amazing. 5 Stars

title: Tormented Souls 2 Digital Deluxe Edition
review_text: Update (3/2026): game has at least one busted achievement (for good ending even after several tries). Easy 5 star when fixed. This game has stunning environmental design - often I'll pause to soak in the small details. Combat controls and positioning can be a bit wonky. I opted for controller Type C layout to aim/shoot with the left/right triggers. It's a bit weird that, in order to dodge (x button), you have to have to switch to your weapon, press aim (left trigger), then press x. The puzzles are great and I'm glad I resisted the urge to google through some sticking points where I wondered, What the hell do I do next?  Some of the dialog and cutscenes are delightfully hammy. The game isn't taking itself seriously 100% of the time. Facial animations are often odd. For full immersion, I recommend watching the 1993 film Dark Waters at some point during your playthrough. The game is a bargain even at full price. Very happy with the purchase and will be keeping an eye out for TS3!

review_text: I really wanted to love this game. I have been a total TTRPG geek since the 90s. And have been a fan of VTM for just as long. But this game dissapointed me quite a lot. It is in one word, boring. The story is weak. The characters, your PC and all of the NPCs, are bland. I cant create my favorite Clan vamp as the selection of Clans is lacking, leaving out my top 3 fave Clans namely Gangrel, Malkavian and Nosferatu. The customization options are practically non existant. The combat is boring and repetive. The game world is smaller than my apartment. Your limited choices in how the, again boring, plot unfolds dont actually matter much in the end.  I cant think of any aspect of this game that hasnt just let me down. So if you are a VTM ttrpg player or fan, save your money and avoid massive dissatisfaction.

title: Insurgency: Sandstorm - 4-Year Anniversary Edition
review_text: This game adds a unique and also a hint of logical sense to it with their mag and ammo system.  The issues I have found is when playing multiplayer, you might run into rubberbanding issues. Could be fixed if you choose to play within your current region, but might in turn, slightly increase the time it will take to find a match. Lots of character customization, but of course most of the customizations is pay walled.  The game does start you off with a couple of currency to buy a few things. After that, you are on your own. The game lacks a story mode. Currently can play multiplayer CO-OP against AIs or against each other via various game modes. People that are giving this game a bad review are upset that there isn't infinite stamina for running across the globe, special abilities like a magic dog spawning from thin air to hunt enemies, unlimited ammo, or killing an enemy with a throwing knife to the foot like COD.

title: Insurgency: Sandstorm - 4-Year Anniversary Edition
review_text: I've been playing Insurgency for the past few years on PC and it is one of the few games I have consistently kept coming back to. Cooperative matches are the best. Enemy AI is outstanding and relentless in co-op. Sound design is excellent, the most realistic weapon audio of any game out there. Every player has access to every weapon in the game right off the bat. The only microtransactions are for clothing and weapon skins. This game has a small but passionate fan base and I would encourage any FPS enthusiast who hasn't to try this game. Call of Duty is for little boys. Insurgency is where the men are.

title: SEDAP! A Culinary Adventure
review_title: Great game, but causing overheating on Series X
review_text: The couch co-op is great. My wife and I are having a lot of fun playing the game - when it doesn't cause the Series X to overheat. Almost straight out the gate of launching the game you can hear the XBox fans kick on high gear, and every other launch or so it will end up overheating and shutting down the game to protect the hardware. The XBox has plenty of breathing room and has been cleaned out with an air duster sufficiently. We experience screen tearing within the game, so I suspect it is something to do with uncapped framerates causing too much GPU workload. If the dev fixes this, the game is an easy 5 star and I will update this review.

There is only like 5 weapons to choose from which you can customize but no skills or powers to be had. Just guns......only guns. The movement is fast paced and fun but can also be annoying. I dunno, if you like mechs and are here to have a good time, I'm pretty confident you'll do so. I'm having a grand ol' time with this game. On the flip side, if you're looking for something to be mad about, you'll be able to do that too. review_text: Purchased the bloodline edition to discover multiple wrestlers are still locked by modes I have no interest in playing. Universe mode is the same with only promos added. title: Pax Dei
review_text: The games graphics are beautiful.  And that's where the beauty ends.   You have to have a subscription to have a house. Don't be fooled by the game letting you start a plot.  You get a free month (which is barely mentioned) of premium that gives you that first token.  Unless you pay or a friend pays or you join some one that pays, your progress is severely hindered.  in 4 hours I started hitting walls that would require me to have to build a house and start building work benches to progress.  And that progress is tied to a real money transaction that you have to make next month or you get locked out of it.  Unless as I mentioned you have a friend or join a clan that's willing to basically support you playing the game by providing the things you need to use to progress.  Oh and all this progress is just crafting.  That's it.  The whole game is pay to craft stuff everyone else can.  No wonder this game was mired in controversy on launch.   Makes C.I.G. look good.

title: Pax Dei
review_title: Some more gneiss rocks would be nice
review_text: I ran around aimlessly for two hours and failed to find enough gneiss rocks to build a proper foundation for a dwelling. Without a foundation, there's very little I could do in the game. I quit out of boredom and frustration. The developers saying that players don't need to pay for a subscription to have the full game experience is a joke. Yes, you get 31 days free with your first plot, but beyond that you have to pay a subscription to maintain that plot. Without a plot there would be absolutely nothing to do in the game. review_text: The game just released and focuses on building, crafting, and exploration. It takes a looooong time to skill up, but that's the intent. This isn't a game with a 60-hour completion. It's something you continuously play and build community around. This game has just released 1.0 and has several continuous releases planned. If you're just starting, you have the opportunity to level up and build your home and marketplace or choose your own adventure before the expansions introduce battle. There are PVP and PVE areas. The building system is fantastic, and is definitely the game's standout feature. I've run across many amazing builds, from cozy roadside inns to elaborate cities and castles. title: Pax Dei
review_title: You can play with a plot for free
review_text: I don't get the whole "hate this game cuz it's not free" - but I've been playing for 3 months, with a plot, and never had to pay.  There is in-game currency called Grace.  Logging in every day gets you grace, or killing NPCs earns you gold, which you can use to buy grace.  If you play fairly regularly, you can play for free, including a plot. You can't build giant castles with one plot, but it's big enough to build a multi-story building with plenty of room.  Game is beautiful.  It IS very grindy.  A lot to craft and build amazing looking buildings - takes a loooong time to unlock the more interesting stuff. Relaxing for me, but may be too much grind for many people. The world is also huge, and while player buildings are everywhere, I'll see 4-5 people at most in a session.  Either bring friends, make them, or plan solo. Community has been very friendly.  The combat is pretty basic and repetitive, and the NPCs are fairly obtuse.  For me, they are means to earning gold.

title: BALL x PIT
review_text: This game took me by surprise. Wanted to just try it out and ended up completing it  A unique pinball roguelite. The only Roguelite I've completed 100% besides vampire survivors.  The combinations of balls and character quirks make for unique and satisfying runs.  There is also a base building/resource gathering aspect I've never seen before in a Roguelite that upgrades your characters and abilities. It takes some getting used to at first but once you get the hang of it it's easy. You'll find yourself completing levels faster because of these buildings. Gets even better you can use more balls, passives and 2 characters for your runs. Highly recommended for those who like Roguelites, pinball or both. Even if you don't this is a chill game to play with Spotify in the background! Tip for base building. When harvesting,create a "closed area" for your harvest so your harvesters (all your characters) don't go all over the map. Use the buildings, and the map wall, as borders.

review_text: It took me years to get around to this game. The main game was short but very cool. Creepy atmosphere and sound design and memorable enemies. However, all of that wears off from the amount of trial and error it takes to progress puzzles or chase sections. I never had issues with puzzle games. Rarely do I have to look up solutions. Didn't know that you could interact with this random part of the background? Dummy. Oh does the evil guy always get you, didn't you know he can't reach you in this little spot? It only takes about 50 tries! And then when you KNOW the solution, you still have to redo the section because of the clunky controls and the weird camera angles. The DLC was the final straw for me. Completely new ideas that weren't alluded to at all, constantly had to look up a guide which I didn't need for the main game. Then, when I'm finally about to be rid of this game, I suffered a known bug literal moments before the end. Uninstalling and never looking back. I want my time back.

review_text: It took me years to get around to this game. The main game was short but very cool. Creepy atmosphere and sound design and memorable enemies. review_text: I picked up the demo when I saw this release, and lost several hours in the best way. I don't want to over sell it, but this game checks all the boxes for me: tactical combat with strategic environmental factors, good writing and VO, meaningful choices with risk and reward (banes & boons), and a progression system that, so far, is NOT a ridiculous slow drip.
