title: Lost Eidolons: Veil of the Witch
review_text: I was skeptical about the combination of these two seemingly incompatible genres, but the result is actually great fun! The overrall runs will last 1-3 hours depending on your progress, but the individual battles are short and engaging, lasting only 5-15 minutes. The battles have a variety of fun objectives and are further supported by non-combat events that have you training your units, buying items, or making skill checks. The meta-progression is great, enabling further progress each run with lots of perks to choose from. The characters are good and have all the build archetypes you would expect from a game in this genre. I'd recommend this game to anyone, especially fans of other SRPGs like Fire Emblem. Also, I had no experience with crashing at all on the Series X.

review_title: Tactical RPG Roguelite w/ Solid Story (so far)
review_text: I picked up the demo when I saw this release, and lost several hours in the best way. I don't want to over sell it, but this game checks all the boxes for me: tactical combat with strategic environmental factors, good writing and VO, meaningful choices with risk and reward (banes & boons), and a progression system that, so far, is NOT a ridiculous slow drip. If you're on the fence, try the demo.

title: Lost Eidolons: Veil of the Witch - Deluxe Edition
review_text: I was skeptical about the combination of these two seemingly incompatible genres, but the result is actually great fun! The overrall runs will last 1-3 hours depending on your progress, but the individual battles are short and engaging, lasting only 5-15 minutes. The battles have a variety of fun objectives and are further supported by non-combat events that have you training your units, buying items, or making skill checks. The meta-progression is great, enabling further progress each run with lots of perks to choose from. The characters are good and have all the build archetypes you would expect from a game in this genre. I'd recommend this game to anyone, especially fans of other SRPGs like Fire Emblem. Also, I had no experience with crashing at all on the Series X.

title: Carpathian Night Starring Bela Lugosi
review_title: A for effort, C- for execution...
review_text: A Castlevania clone with the OG Dracula - sounds like a dream, and... Sadly it underdelivers, massively. The good:  - It looks like Castlevania - Officially licensed by Bela Lugosi's estate The bad: - A bareboned experience, right from the starting menu that has two options - Play or Quit, and no settings - Vast and empty locations, paired with a small character sprite. I get the idea and the limitations, but it's sub-par - Sluggish controls. Yes, I get the Castlevania 1-3 blueprint, but at least add a Metroid-esque "stop to aim" button if you're letting us whip in 8 directions - Poor and straight up baffling level design. There's a difference between hard and deliberately unfair. This one falls into the latter category. And exploration is limited to tiny detours on mostly bite-size maps through breakable walls - There are hearts in almost every light source, like in Castlevania, but they're supposed to be health... Yet they barely heal.  - Ridiculously easy bosses $5 tops

title: My Horse Stories: Complete Edition
review_text: As a owner of a purebred Arabian mare for 30 years I am always on the lookout for horse games where the emphasis is on caring for the horse and not having to worry about it dying. I feel like this game is finally what I have been searching for all these years. Not only do you take care of the horse like feeding and grooming it but being a game designed for children I never have to worry about my horses ever crossing the Rainbow Bridge because having had to deal with it in real life I didn't want it in my video game. Caring for your beloved horse is not all that you do there are also things around the stable that need fixing so in order to do that you can enter competitions. These are just timing your jumping so you don't knock down bars. After awhile you are able to train your trusting steed to improve and enhance both of your abilities. I give this game five stars because it to me is the best game you can get if you just want to relax with horses.

review_text: I'm surprised this didn't go on Game Pass, so much stupid fun. I got lost in it for several hours on first boot, couldn't put down the controller. It's just like the demo.  I played single player mostly but did try multiplayer for a bit which is still the campaign. Says will reset level (any progress reset?) if you connect up. You can play with strangers if you find an ethernet cable statue in the level or you can pause and select to invite a friend or start co-op. Game doesn't mention it but you can roll around if you hold in the dash button. Rolling will also smash things plus you move a little faster. You have unlimited lives but it's expensive, dying takes half your loot. Things will often get in the way of the camera and while it can be annoying it is tolerable & doesn't cause problems. It would be nice if the game had some sort of map we could place markers on. Everything else about the game has been awesome. Played on Xb1X This is a gem, I don't recommend holding off.

I hit a bump though, it seems you can only do so much progress before you have to wait a day supposedly. The in-game time matches console time so I'm assuming you actually have to wait a whole day before continuing quests. You can still fish, harvest, use the store, and craft; just no more story progress till the day after. It's a fun whimsical game that is perfect for stress relief, and the music is calming, so it's worth every penny. I'll for sure be spending time in this game plus it'll make an amazing game for Xbox Streaming!

title: Car Driving School Simulator
review_title: Pretty good learning sim but also a reminder
review_text: Pretty decent learning sim for basic rules of the road, I do have a couple issues I'm not a fan of.  Firstly rules are little too strict, if i turn on a blinker just a little too far back for the games liking it deducts points although in my opinion it's within reason to turn on a blinker that far back in some cases for other drivers.  My second issue is the AI is relentless which is fine sometimes for learning but EVERY AI acts like you aren't even there and just pulls out in front of you. Also right of way doesn't exist in this game. Lastly a reminder that this teaches basic lessons, depending on where someone lives these lessons aren't helping completely. For example I'm in the USA in a smaller major city and most drivers ignore these rules, like everyone in my city regularly goes 10-20 over the limit and they really don't care if you are following the rules or not they will hit you. Again a good learning tool, but I wouldn't say this game will work for every situation.

title: My Horse Stories
review_text: As a owner of a purebred Arabian mare for 30 years I am always on the lookout for horse games where the emphasis is on caring for the horse and not having to worry about it dying. I feel like this game is finally what I have been searching for all these years. Not only do you take care of the horse like feeding and grooming it but being a game designed for children I never have to worry about my horses ever crossing the Rainbow Bridge because having had to deal with it in real life I didn't want it in my video game. Caring for your beloved horse is not all that you do there are also things around the stable that need fixing so in order to do that you can enter competitions. These are just timing your jumping so you don't knock down bars. After awhile you are able to train your trusting steed to improve and enhance both of your abilities. I give this game five stars because it to me is the best game you can get if you just want to relax with horses.

review_text: I pre-ordered this game months before its release, as well as Sonic Frontiers and Sonic x Shadow generations. review_text: I LOVED the original Slime Rancher, so when the sequel was announced I admit that I was HYPED. And now that the early access is out, was that hype warranted? Yeah I say it was! Plus, the bugs are few and far between, which is a breath of fresh air for me considering the industry today. Though they should be mentioned regardless. I also do feel the brightness of the Phosphor slimes should be toned down a bit, I found myself mistaking a phosphor plort for a cotton plort many a time. Overall, I'm optimistic for the future of this game! If you're a fan of the first game I highly recommend this game.

review_text: As a Civ 5, and Civ 6 lover Civ 7 just leaves me asking "why". So first things first the Good on the Game. The Graphics are an upgrade from Civ 6. The new animations are a nice touch. One thing I am really enjoying is the new Army Commander system. The ability to control your armys in a new and unique way brings a nice twist to domination focused players, and expands the strategy aspect of the game. Now onto the bad stuff. The age changes in my opinion are aweful to the game since its more of you play 3 mini civ matches instead of 1, because every time the age changes you borderline get set back to having nothing. you keep your cities and SOME of your military units, but your economy and science get reset and you start over. Go back to the normal trading and Sc sytem. The Ugly of the game is that there are so few civilizations and NO TRUE START EARTH MAP. Which I imagine will be set behind a pay wall later. So in conclusion WHY change so much from civ 6 which was perfect and trash it.

title: Sid Meier's CivilizationÂ® VII Settler's Edition
review_text: The Fear of being a "one trick pony" has caused one of the saddest letdowns for the playerbase. An incredible amount of money has been made off of Civ6 alone, so why change it? If "passion" is no longer the motivation for developers anymore then i will talk logically in terms of making money. Why release a title that belongs to a different game entirely, and come to expect success? Call of Duty is still alive because of this one money-hungry rule. Civ7 is not worth the money. Absolutely no passion or business sense. I have no malice for Firaxis, but they need to be the "one trick pony" everyone loved. I genuinely feel for everyone that waited years for something they didnt want, and feel worse for the die hard fans that want their overpriced pre-order refunded. Civ7 will probably not be fixed in the eyes of 90% of the fans, but Civ8 has so much to live up to now.

title: Labyrinthine - Console Edition
review_text: So there was a decent bit of jank at release. Despite that, I had so much fun, both with buddies and even solo; both in story mode and in the case files. Since release, though, the swift patches have improved and fixed jank and UI bugs, making the whole experience more fun, smooth, and accessible. Would recommend this to anyone who even just likes puzzles and exploration. 100% this might be the best maze game out there in terms of both ambience and replayability. It's charming on it's own, and hilarious with friends. There are sooo~ many maps and monsters, each with their own aesthetics and mechanics, and even loads of drip to unlock and wear. Even just exploring the maps in custom case files with no monsters is so immersive and fun. I can only hope they continue to update the game and potentially add even more in the future. It's not perfect, and neither am I. But hot damn it feels close.

Not only does it go full 80's sci-fi anime type of zany, but the game's filled with special cards to signify locales, items, even IRL dev cats (all of which, yes, are cute). It's all very admirable to me. Don't get me wrong, the premise is still simple, and your time will inevitably be short with this one. But in a world full of VERY involved, complicated franchises... little ones like these? They're nice. Pick this up if you need a break between games. Can't hurt. review_text: Waking up in a bathtub at a dirty motel with no recollection as to why, you must first figure out how to escape the room you are in. After that, it's all about escaping the horror you find yourself in with nightmarish creatures roaming about. If you die, you do start over but in a more clever way. With each restart, items are moved around, more monsters are added and the path to the end can even change, taking longer to get to it. Plus, there's four different endings and "restarting" after dying is how to get them. Don't die too much because there is a set number to it. All found documents do carry over. Now voice acting isn't the greatest but the gameplay is good. It does have a bit of a resource management element with limited carrying space. There is a slight issue with achievements unlocking. I liked how some of the weapons from the first game were a bit different from other kart racers and gave you unique abilities that really played into the mechanics of the game. The weapons in this game are all basically just reskinned from Mario Kart. (No, I didn't buy this expecting the same quality experience and I don't recommend anyone does that.) review_title: A must play for Remedy & Kojima fans
review_text: The title says it all. This would get five stars easily if it weren't for the stutter that many people mention. On series S it really only did it at a couple of major cutscenes, but this game is so beautiful that it feels heartbreaking when it happens. Challenging puzzles that, once solved, are quite satisfying. Good game length for a game like this, doesn't overstay it's welcome. That said, an expanded rpg-esque game in this universe would be absolutely incredible.

title: 9 Lives To Defend
review_title: Decent Survivorslike With Room For Improvement
review_text: Overall it's a competent survivorslike, which puts it above a lot of the VS clones out there, however it just doesn't have enough content/variety as of now. The unlocks don't feel too meaningful and the meta progression is weak. I tend to try most of the survivorslikes that come out on xbox, and I think that with some work the devs could have a good game here, it just needs more content, meaningful unlocks, variety, better metaprogression (like a variety of permanent stat boosts, not just medals you only can have 3 active of) and some evolutions for weapons. Again, its not a bad game, especially for the asking price.

title: Firefighting Simulator: Ignite
review_title: I like this game very much.
review_text: I've played 100% of the main missions. Firefighter Simulator Ignite is a good game. Most importantly fighting fires is amazing. There is a lot of player freedom on how you tackle each fire. Blazes spread dynamically with some limits (fires can't burn down whole buildings... yet). Airflow & ventilation matter. Certain floors and stairs can collapse. A+ on this aspect. NPC pathfinding still needs work, there's a reset button for your team, but civilians often get lost when traversing ladders on trucks. The graphics suit my realism craving and the game performs well. If anything the Player animations are a little stiff. Also, you can drive the trucks (how well depends on you). 5 out of 5 for me.

review_text: Played this game for quite a while on Steam and am very glad to finally see it's console release. This is a city builder/town management type game with light survival mechanics. You'll be building a settlement and starting a new life for yourself after escaping war. It'll include raising crops, livestock, and ultimately a family. You are the overseer of your settlement and will have farmers, blacksmiths, tailors and such living and working within your village. This game is one of those types of games that many people find relaxing, as you hunt, gather resources, and tend to your village. I hope this proves to be a positive experience for Toplitz and they bring Wild West Dynasty over here as well. Medieval Dynasty is a well loved game on PC with a great community. Let's hope it continues here.

title: Medieval & Sengoku Dynasty Bundle
review_text: This is a slow-build up type of game. You will be hungry, you will be thirsty, you will be poor. After the first year, you may have a few people in your town, but not many. They wont be skilled, and they have their own needs. Taxes suck, but not really. You have ample ability to make money by hunting, crafting, and prioritizing what your people do. Build 3 woodsheds, and 2 excavation sites. Build 10 houses and the worker areas. Know that this will skyrocket your taxes, which are due in the spring. When you notice how prices work, you notice that meat and simple crafted tools are easily produced and sell well. Also hunting bandits for coin and loot is not hard at all. You can change the difficulty and game options mid-play, which means you can turn off stamina, or get infinite carry weight. Really, if you set up your villagers well, you can sell firewood for a living, and slowly go from hunting to having a merchant empire. Clunky in a survival sandbox way, but fun and replayable too. GG

title: Cronos: The New Dawn - Deluxe Edition
review_text: Review from a Survival Horror Fanatic. Is it gonna scratch the Dead Space itch? A bit, it honestly makes me want to play DS again. Is it as good as Bloober's Silent Hill 2 Remake? No but that's okay! It's a great step in the right direction for Bloober Team and it could be an awesome series. The Horror aspect for me personally needs improvement and that's with my headset loud enough to cause hearing loss. The combat 8/10. Setting 9/10. Atmosphere 8.5/10. Horror 7.5/10. It really shines with keeping the situation tense but falls a little short on the scares. Resource management for survival horror experts will be easy but for casual players decently difficult. Overall I'm enjoying it and I can't wait to see where Bloober Team goes from here. 9/10 for me.

title: Cronos: The New Dawn - Deluxe Edition
review_text: Brutal? Absolutely. Visually and narratively interesting? 100%.  Post-apocalyptic Poland, crawling with grotesque and horrifying abominations, low on resources, and full of intrigue and mystery. You'll probably die, a fair bit, but each time, pick up a bit of info about your foes and environment, and you'll see results when you use it to your advantage. Conserve ammo, but don't rely on melee, it's a last resort, unless you're skilled enough to make use of it. Don't panic, don't get cornered. Highly recommend for fans of Resident Evil, Dead Space, and Metro type games.

review_title: The "There's not enough resources" is a lie.
review_text: There's a TON of reviews claiming the game doesn't give enough resources, and it definitely does. They're more than likely not looking around enough or spamming/not charging shots, but there's 100% enough if you use your surroundings, properly manage resources, and don't spam every shot. - With that out the way, the game is fun and interesting. At first you'll be lost about the plot/story, but after reading the files you find and just by playing, it will unravel itself and you'll get the picture.  - The gameplay is pretty similar to The Callisto Protocol (the enemies mutating, resource management, etc) just without a dodge mechanic (the movement helps save this). - The combat is fun and keeps you on your feet. The atmosphere keeps you on edge. The enemy designs are awesome. I've played alot of survival horror (every Resident Evil, Dead Space, etc) so maybe my review might count for something.  If you love survival horror, this is worth grabbing. 100% recommend.

review_title: This is NOT an action game
review_text: Do not go into this game thinking it's some kind of arcade off-road racer. SnowRunner is a slow-paced offroad SIMULATOR. You are tasked with completing deliveries or recovering lost supplies and vehicles. The challenge and fun comes from besting your adversary - the ground. You WILL get stuck in the mud and snow, and you WILL spend 10 minutes kicking yourself while you struggle to winch yourself out. Once you reach your destination, you're given some money as a reward - money that can be used to buy and upgrade your trucks. Rinse & Repeat. Is SnowRunner slow? - Yes Is SnowRunner boring? - A little bit Is SnowRunner fun, rewarding, and addictive? - ABSOLUTELY Final Note: I really hate most of the menus and the Garage/vehicle storage system is just awful, but those are really my only complaints.

Zero regrets as a fan of PSX horrors and DOS/Win9x adventures. If you like survival horror, the 90s aesthetic, or the idea of a cyberpunk Lovecraftian mystery adventure, this is 100% up your alley.

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre - PC Edition - Content Pass Edition
review_text: They clearly pulled off what they were going for. High tension asymmetrical multiplayer. That's wonderful if you're looking for.. well, online multiplayer asymmetrical gameplay. You either play as a victim, alongside 3 other players, or a member of the "Family", including the coveted Leather Face. The victims are struggling to escape, so to a degree the game boils down to hide and seek, with death. It's very cool, very well done. I'd give it 5 stars if there was an option to play a bot match. While that may sound crazy, games like Unreal Tournament nailed that 20 years ago. If you're excited for this game and down for multiplayer only, hop onboard, it's everything it's advertised to be.

review_title: Poor PC port, and no onboarding.
review_text: In the PC version, you can't change your key bindings, nor can you change your mouse sensitivity.  These were common features in games from the 90s.  It also frequently crashes. Additionally, the onboarding is uniquely terrible.  The tutorials are dozens of short films, sometimes lacking narration,  there are almost no in-game clues as to what you should be doing, the three maps included look very similar to each other which mostly serves to confound new users, and some mechanics are not explained at all.  The onboarding strategy seems to be "find an influencer that made some tutorials and watch those." Other than that, the game looks and sounds great.  It really captures the feel of the 1974 film.

title: Hell is Us
review_text: The game is fun, yet odd. It isn't a souls-like and it isn't ametroidvania. It's not real open world either. Some areas are larger than others, and combat is fun, granted I'm not really struggling. You can kill enemies fairly quickly. You don't level up, or allocate skill points. You instead level up your weapons through battle. The story is unique and interesting to me and there is a lot of lore to learn. I must warn people that there is A LOT of PUZZLES in this game. I personally don't care for puzzles, but these aren't super difficult. There is also a lot of backtracking to open new areas later on with newly acquired keys or codes, just about EVERY door or chest needs a key or code to open. There are no "free" chests in this game. There is also NO MAP or guide holding your hand either. You must think, remember, and observe everything. It is a bit annoying, but overall I'm enjoying the game.

title: Hell is Us
review_text: First point, there is a lot of memorizing (or pen and paper), running back and forth between areas multiple times, creative puzzles requiring outside the box thinking, and storytelling. A lot of attention is needed in the dialogue, letters, recordings, and other findings if you want to successfully complete everything. Next point, combat is very repetitive. I ran the entire game with one set of weapons, but there are a few different types to try out. You can upgrade the weapons as well as apply three perks. You're equiped with a sidekick as well that provides up to four different supports. There are a few consumables that will help you. Ironically, I only needed to use consumables at the very beginning and very end of the game. It took 37 hours for me to complete. The ending cutscenes were nice twists. Finally, performance was pretty good. One crash, one odd ladder traversal, and some minor graphics and audio glitchs. Overall, I enjoyed this game. Not everyones cup of tea though.

review_title: Excellent game, beautiful, with its share of flaws.
review_text: This is the truest example of an action adventure game, honestly close to a gold standard. Game is highly polished, with few bugs to speak of, some areas have geometry issues where the lack of jumping can force you back to the main menu. Speaking of which, this is not a souls like or roguelite, death doesn't halt progression, and enemies dont respawn unless you leave the location. This game's main plot is nothing to write home about and the combat can grow stale by the late game, but there is something so compelling about everyone you meet, help, and talk to, that makes this game feel human. The world building is astounding, how they were able to fit millennia of background and story into each location seems highly difficult, even if  the game isn't super ambitious. Graphics wise, just gorgeous, from dark hazy forests to wide open vistas, ancient castles and even a war torn city, each location is hand crafted and unique. Im out of words, buy this game. The VA for Adam Jensen is Remi.

title: Friends vs Friends
review_title: Overall pretty good but there are some big issues
review_text: The game itself is very fun to play, with or without friends. The only problems I have with the game are, the performance issues, the aim assist, and the lack of the customization the pc version has. During certain points in the game, the game's frame rate will all of a sudden tank even with the graphics setting turned to "performance favorable." Most notably on Tabletop, Museum, and Reality. The most common spots where the frame rate drops seem to be the middle of the map. The issue with the aim assist is that it will lock on to random enemies if they're close together, and when I say lock on I mean it. Multiple times I have aimmed at someone with their teammate nearby, the aim assist will lock onto the other enemy even if I was already shooting the other enemy. Now the lack of setting customization, more graphic, video, audio, and just basic setting options are very much needed. The game is still very fun but I recommend either not buying this until it is fixed or getting it on pc.

title: Goosebumps: Terror in Little Creek
review_text: A sudden curfew has been issued in the small town of Little Creek. It's not normal, nor will the night be as Sloane and her friends sneak out to find out why. It's not long before you'll be exploring the town, solving puzzles and dealing with monsters. The town itself is set up well with many paths blocked off until you acquire keys or tools to get past a specific type of obstacle for example. While playing through it, it felt like a Goosebumps version of Resident Evil. Puzzles aren't overly complicated and some will have you sneaking, running away and hiding from monsters as you explore interior locations, gathering pieces for their solutions. You're also not totally helpless as you'll get a sling shot with different types of ammo to fight back or distract with. This was surprisingly longer than I expected and all characters are fully voiced. Achievements are very easy but there are two endings so two playthroughs for them all. The $40 is a bit high so grab on sale and have fun.

title: The Knightling - Deluxe Edition
review_title: Just like the good ol' days
review_text: Feels like a classic from the PS2 days, for better and for worse. Traversal is a blast, between surfing on your shield and gliding through the air, mastering movement is very rewarding. Combat is mid. You have a reasonably robust set of tools, but most of them either aren't rewarding enough when you compare it to just blocking to build super bar and nuking everything, or just aren't functional enough to bother with. Music is overall very pleasant and fitting. Lots of jank. Shield throw feels awful which is a huge shame since the animation in general is so fun and expressive, but the lock-on barely works and the frustration is compounded with it being the only way to incapacitate what is already the most annoying enemy in the game, who also happens to be unkillable for seemingly no reason. The story isn't anything too deep but the writing and scenarios were usually pretty funny and always charming. Definite mixed bag but overall positive experience. If there was a sequel I would play it

title: Carnival Survivors The Parade
review_title: Boring IF you have to play twice - 10/10 45min review:
review_text: CStP is basically missile defense with a splash of space invaders. There are rogue elements here like 3 skill choices after every wave (60 waves in total) and a skill tree you can buy buffs in, via coins you pick up in the run. There are 4 levels to choose from each with their own biome/environment . The way the HP works is 2-fold. The truck has hp and the conductor does as well (less than the truck) and you'll get HP pickups as you kill enemies. I did not die nor need to buy buffs, and got all 10 achievements by finishing ghe first level, having had bought each band member through the run. While CStP isn't bad at all and frankly I like the art style, it's just a bit easy, and given its manual shooting due to the Left-to-Right formula it get tedious holding left stick up constantly for such little impact. It's a slightly above average achievement game with custom art. At ToR I got it on sale for 1.74 USD and I'd say that to upwards of 3 USD is a fair price range for AH'ers.

I LOVE THE SPREAD GUN though, best weapon ever!  I would definitely recommend to get on sale for $1.99 or  $0.99 for it, but no more than this. review_text: I may be in the minority when it comes to this, but something that's always bugged me about Contra and Contra-clones alike is the fact your dude can only take one hit. Crushborgs however gives you health-bar right off the bat and vertical-platforming stages don't kill you when you drop down a platform; you just land! I realize this game is just a quick little BGM experiment for Darkman007 and Xitilon and an Achievement Hunter cashgrab, but just playing a Contra clone with a health-bar is a wish I've always wanted since I played the first Contra. Maybe this isn't the only Contra clone to do that and maybe this review will get 'actual-ied' and down-voted into oblivion, but I don't care: this game proves to me there is some hope left in this nostalgia-blinded corner of the industry. Damn good soundtrack, too; it all just makes ME happy.

title: Space Adventure Cobra - The Awakening - Gold Edition
review_title: A nostalgic blast from the past!
review_text: This gem of a game needs more love as it truly pays homage to the late Buichi Terasawa (RIP). A majority of the story is based on the 1982 anime. Even the cutscenes from in-game are taken from the anime as well. Space Adventure Cobra's story is very rich sci-fi fantasy during its time period. Anyway, this game really focuses on run & gun gameplay. A good tip would be to continuously shoot your psycho-gun ahead of you off screen. The music also sounds awesome and reminiscent to the anime. Though my only complaint would be trying to manually direct Cobra's psycho beam. Even with aim assist turned on/off it can sometimes veer into a nearyby enemy/switch when you're trying hit another enemy/switch. Which can be a little annoying. Though I wish the end boss in mission 13-1 got a cooler death animation (or anime cutscene) by getting blasted into space just like in the anime, as the in-game one felt anti-climatic. Now I feel like re-reading the mangas and rewatching the movie, anime & OVA's!

title: Particle Hearts
review_text: Put on headphones, helps mood & finding chimes. Chimes aren't required but definitely necessary for the story & experience. Finding all in each level before moving on is difference between having a good experience & a great one by the end (mopping up later = ruined & missed experience). I was hooked early in. You find out right away this is gonna be something cool with curiousity being piqued for what to expect & what's going on. I highly recommend this if you like chill games with a minimal ambience to go with the mood, exploring around environments, easy (real) puzzle solving and you like the creative approaches to 3D game ideas that often landed on 6th gen consoles (Xbox, GameCube, Dreamcast, PS2). The few reviews I could find on YT & Steam were all positive and now that I've finished it, I see why all were so. I sure hope this doesn't end up being one of those gems that go largely unnoticed.  Go into it blind or as spoiler free of experiences, story, & mechanics as possible.

review_title: A Contra Clone with a Health-bar!
review_text: I may be in the minority when it comes to this, but something that's always bugged me about Contra and Contra-clones alike is the fact your dude can only take one hit. Crushborgs however gives you health-bar right off the bat and vertical-platforming stages don't kill you when you drop down a platform; you just land! I realize this game is just a quick little BGM experiment for Darkman007 and Xitilon and an Achievement Hunter cashgrab, but just playing a Contra clone with a health-bar is a wish I've always wanted since I played the first Contra. Maybe this isn't the only Contra clone to do that and maybe this review will get 'actual-ied' and down-voted into oblivion, but I don't care: this game proves to me there is some hope left in this nostalgia-blinded corner of the industry. Damn good soundtrack, too; it all just makes ME happy.

review_text: I usually save reviewing a game until I feel I've gotten everything out of it/I'm done, or if it's broken, but I wanted to exempt Roundguard because it's a game I feel I can keep playing. There are some lulls in gameplay like when you get stuck in a bouncing loop or you just want to finish the level, but otherwise everything feels satisfactory. There's more player control than you'd expect from what looks and plays like a rogue-like pachinko game. Relics are a great addition, the trinkets feel worthwhile, and the combat is surprisingly rewarding. There is an accessible easy mode from the start, and varying degrees of difficulty for a challenge. Overall, I wouldn't regret the 20 MSRP, and definitely don't regret the 8 USD sale price. review_text: This game has immediately become a fixation of mine. As other reviews have mentioned there's a bit of a difficulty spike at chapter three, but after a few swings at it I finally broke through. I followed this up immediately with an unstoppable run in chapter 4. I felt powerful, like God must feel when he's holding a gun. Unfortunately when I set the game down at level 9 to grab dinner and watch Hulu, I came back to find the game completely unresponsive at the shop screen I left off on. I tried all the button mashing my caveman brain could muster to try and get it going again, with no luck. I had no choice but to quit and relaunch the game and lose all my progress. My RNG on subsequent attempts has paled in comparison to that god run. It's unfortunate because I'm otherwise really enjoying the gameplay loop, but a game like this should feel like you can safely put it down and pick it back up on a whim for long sessions or just a level or two. Hopefully this is fixed.

review_title: A Must Play For Souls Combat Enthusiasts
review_text: This is one of the better souls-like games if you're a fan of Bloodborne's combat mixed with Sekiro. There are 3 types of Blocking, one is your normal hold LB to negate all damage at the cost of stamina. Second is tapping LB the moment an attack lands to deplete the enemy's posture slowly, whereas the third block is a RIPOSTE which happens if you hold LB and attack at the same time an enemy hit lands, causing you to straight up rip their guts out. That visceral feeling of combat, combined with the fact that you have a Pistol that can also parry enemies is straight up from Bloodborne which I love so much. The level design and enemy variety isn't anything extraordinary, but for a $30 title it is pretty solid. The bosses are not easy, however they do not have any crazy AOE spam attacks so if you're any good at souls-games then you won't have much trouble with them. All in all, a great game to play if you love Fromsoft Titles. ðŸ‘Œ

The flourish might work on paper but in reality costs you precious time. Time you don't have as there is sometimes HORDES of enemies on your screen. review_title: Good but not like the first
review_text: This game doesn't really have the same feel as DL1, less of a horror game and more of a standard RPG feel, that is somewhat dissapointing. Overall though not terrible, there are some bugs with the audio and visual but a lot of that's being fixed. Story isn't quite like the first but the voice acting is a bit better and the amount of actions you can take that change the course of the story makes for better replayability than DL1. The vs zombie combat feels worse than DL1 but, their recently updated weapons system is slighty better than DL1. The vs human combat on the other hand is improved from DL1, guns also feel better. Their are some good and bad things they added to parkour and whether you like that or not is largely personal preference. Overall, I think the biggest con in this game is it doesn't have that DL1 horror feel we all know and love. All in all, I would wait for a sale but still worth a playthrough or two, just don't expect the DL1 feel.

title: 9 Kings (Game Preview)
review_text: I think I'm qualified to review this as I've gotten every achievement - which means I obviously enjoyed the game. But it's not without major issues. Pros:  Easy to understand Fun to play while doing something else Lots of fun combos to discover and each king plays differently A lot of content between the base gameplay and the quests; I haven't even bothered with the multiplayer Cons: Repetitive: once you know a strat you can repeat it over and over Easy: yeah...it's really easy, even at the highest difficulties, mostly because of the former point Slow: A run only takes ~10 minutes but those 10 minutes have never felt longer, the 3x speed should be the default option and increase from there Quests: While they're great to have, the difficulty is all over the place and many can only be won with rainbow cards - no matter how much you bang your head against the wall trying the "intended" strat. So yeah, fun game in short bursts but with problems that can be fixed.

review_text: I put in like 25 hours before I gave up so I enjoyed my time with it. But after awhile I found some things I didn't love. The actual battles feel borderline pointless, the idea that its even playable outside of 3x speed is a joke. Even if using your main tower manually played any real part, it would be so tedious as to be not worth your time. Also found the 3x3 grid system to be very claustrophobic after a while. It made it so strategy was very obvious. Anything with the tag "surrounding tiles" goes in the middle, corners for buildings with passive effects, etc. And this is probably just a "git gud" scenario, but the quests are like stupid hard, some off them I genuinely never even saw how they were possible. Anyway, still a solid 4/5, the "King" system was super fun and it was enjoyable to discover a combo that was just broken as heck.

review_text: New review: I reviewed this almost a year ago, and heres my thoughts now. I like the changes made, and bringing the final king. I appreciate the quest mode, I feel it can be a bit frustrating, you have to initially play the cards correctly, and then the RNG ramps in and hecks you up, causing you to restart. Not a bad thing, I would probably modify it a bit to say an adventure mode style where you continuously get differing challenges, instead of each king has 9 scenarios and you unlock additional as you progress. Its moot, and I can still appreciate what it is. I have been focusing on that and enjoying it. The rainbow cards are all strong, as well as the introduction of chaos cards is pretty near, I would probably consider having more trade off chaos cards, like gain 9% troops, but surrounding buildings lose one level and get locked at that level. Or something to that effect, make them more risky to take. 999gold for the stat increase is broken. Great job Devs, cant wait to see more!

review_title: Should've been called Gates, Bridges, and Platforms
review_text: I don't mind puzzles, but these are not puzzles - they're simply exercises. The same mundane 'raise platform' 'unlock door' routine again and again and again. And the game tells you exactly what to do, so you're not even solving problems. It's dull, plain and simple. I thought these 'flip the door switch' games went out of style in 2005. As far as the narrative, kudos to the voice acting. It's all very well-done. Unfortunately, there isn't much of a 'story' being told, because you spend your time walking a straight path a raising platforms. Combat. While not dreadful, this isn't a game that has great collision physics, making combat (as well as other basic movement in the game) feel janky and not precise. The game looks pretty, although it's often hard to tell where you can and cannot go. The boundaries look the same as the environment - just gotta stumble around and get lucky. Echoes isn't the worst game you could play, but not all that good.

review_text: A decent game as long as you aren't expecting too much. Older setting is neat but feels like that was done as an excuse to cut out the urban environment and police system. Very scaled back from the other Mafia games, which is worrisome. Extremely (and I mean EXTREMELY) basic gameplay and mission design. Doesn't build on its predecessors and instead actually regresses quite a bit. If it weren't for the graphics I'd swear Mafia DE was the newer game. The strength of the game is supposed to be the story, but the story is pretty predictable. If you played Mafia DE you'll likely know exactly where the story is going long before it gets there. Still a very cinematic experience, but wish they focused more on making sure their video game was fun to play instead of just fun to watch. This one is a forced 10 hour journey that you have very little freedom from for exploration or decision making.   Imagine you'll be playing a 10 hour on rails movie,  and not enjoying a typical Mafia game experience,  and you won't be disappointed.   That being said,  I'm very disappointed in how short and shallow this journey was,  and really regret dropping 60$ on a 10 hour game with no replay value.   Save your money on this one,  or wait for it to go on sale or join gamepass.   Not worth the money!

Until these games, the plots to FPS were very limited in both in game and supplimental material. There was a lot of back story to them compared to even DOOM. Also the games gave proper names to the playable characters. Sure there was BJ from Wolfenstein, but the Heretic/Hexen games had a full named playable cast. The Heretic isn't just Heretic, he is Corvus. The playable classes in Hexen also have names and fleshed out back stories in ways that DOOM and Wolfenstein didn't have until more recent games. So instead of complaing just enjoy the games and the ability to play these important parts of gaming history. . .also if the devs try to remaster Heretic 2. . .please don't. . .instead remake the game from the ground because I for remember what a nightmare and slog that was to play 'cause the control layout for keyboard was that horrible no matter what.

title: Ship Graveyard Simulator 2: Complete Edition
review_text: Just bought the Steel Giants DLC and started playing the game again. I could not be happier! The problems I was having back in February have been fixed, like pieces of the ship hanging in mid air. It is so satisfying taking a big ship apart from the bottom and watching the whole thing crumble like a house of cards!! The physics are just incredible. I can tell that the Developers really care about delivering a great experience. I have no further issues with the game on my Xbox Series X. However, the button assignments have changed for tool selection and Contracts. For tool selection, you need to press "LB" button and NOT D-pad up (which is assigned to Contracts). It took me over an hour to figure this out with trial and error. Other than that, the game plays fantastic. Thank you Devs for the fixes and two new DLCs! I want the Cruise Ships DLC next.

title: Life Sim Bundle
review_text: I have been in the medical field for six years and counting. Started as a combat medic in the Army, and after leaving the service, become a civilian provider on an ambulance in a rural county as an Advanced EMT. Our ENTIRE ambulance crew is excited to play this, even between the real calls we run. Finally there's a simulator (yes with some bugs) to show people just a fraction of what we do! Messaging back and forth with devs on Insta, if this game continues to gain support from us as a community, they have many plans ahead, including more treatments, meds, and calls we see in our IRL job. Give em a chance! The traffic PURPOSELY won't move for you sometimes (trust me that's realistic) and sometimes patients simply cannot be saved even when we do our best! 5/5, thank you Aesir for doing your research. title: Dark Steel Legends
review_text: Let me start by saying that I don't mind the graphics. It's clear that it's a low budget game and that's fine. There's zero story, it's just an arena combat game, which is fine. The menu and user interface is horrible. I spent way too much time moving a cursor around trying to navigate menus. I can get past those things. But when the entire game is based around arena combat, you'd think they would get the combat part right. That's the part I can't get past. The enemies are so erratic, you can't tell when they're about to attack or use a special, so you can't really react to them. The dodge system is HORRIBLE. You can't animation cancel with a dodge, so if you're mid swing you're out of luck. And even if you do see an attack coming and dodge, it's still going to hit you. So the dodge mechanic is just completely useless. The game is less of a skill check and more of a stat check. Only redeeming quality is the easy achievements, ill get my quick 1000g and never touch this again.

Your card/build choices matter to the point it can ruin entire runs if you didn't pick wisely, but all of that is based on other RNG beyond your control. title: 9 Years of Shadows
review_text: The best thing about this game is the presentation. There are some memorable music tracks and the graphics are created very competently, even if I found most of the character and enemy designs to be uninteresting. The gameplay leaves much to be desired, with boring combat that does not evolve at all throughout the game and movement abilities that are restrictive and limit player expression. Bosses feel unpolished and rarely have more than 2-3 attacks. For example there is an early boss that has a total of 2 attacks both of which it takes long enough to recover from that you can heal fully every time, making the boss almost impossible to die to. The level designs are usually a straight path to the boss with a few dead end paths with items and optional encounters which would be fine in a level based game but feels counter-intuitive in a Metroidvania. The game also is buggy, for example pop in and unwanted text being added to descriptions. Play The Last Faith or Blasphemous first.

review_text: I got this for it's survivorslike mode, and it is alright. I don't care for the main mode much, you fight a couple waves of enemies in a room then go up to another room with more waves and so on. Anyway, the upgrades and attack systems are very interesting and there seem to be a lot of variety and ways you can make builds. It is a bit on the complicated side, so if you are looking for a chill survivors game, this isn't it. You will also need to dash, and dash a lot. You have a spell that auto fires, and then spell disks that generate mana to lauch the attached spell. Spell discs have a specific element(s) that you need to cast to charge them. It essentially creates links of spells. Like I said, its complicated, but if theory-crafting is your jam, check this out.

title: Maiden Cops
review_title: Indie Devs dispelling the Gaming Dark Ages...
review_text: ...one bouncy bodacious beatdown at a time.  Maiden Cops draws its inspiration from legendary titles like Streets of Rage and Final Fight.  The gameplay really feels like SOR3 with the dodge roll and the rechargeable special meter amongst other things.  Visually the game is excellent, with modern tech giving polish to retro inspired pixel art.  Combat is fun and rewarding with each character having their own unique stats and play style.  Meiga Holstaur is slow, yet strong, Priscilla Salamander is the balanced option of the three, and Nina Usagi is quick and agile.  Each of them has three special moves which you'll want to mix in with basic attacks and wall bounces to get those gold tier combo scores.  The writing was also very enjoyable with dialogue full of humor and charm.  I did not encounter any glitches through my playthroughs, and with unlockables and gold scores to aim for, there's still much to do.  Thank you devsðŸ‘

title: Tales of the Shire: A The Lord of The Ringsâ„¢ Game
review_text: I had this cozy game on my wish list for months.So, it's safe to assume I was excited for this release. The game has a lot of potential to be great, but there needs to be some improvements. The camera zoom in and out as you move around in your house is nauseating for anyone who is sensitive to that. Moving around the village by guide of birds that seemingly blend in with the world will have you running in circles and constantly checking your map, breaking game immersion. review_text: Killingfloor 2 was an amazing game. Ive spent days playing it with friends over the last 10 years. Ive talked 2 friends into buying whom also loved. title: Killing Floor 3
review_text: After many days on KF2, this game had me hyped up to launch, despite the delay. However, after 3 rounds of survival i've got some gripes with KF3. The QoL additions are great, mantling, mid-round restock, and dashing are awesome. But, the gunplay is a bit stiff and aim assist on controller is wonky with no options for it. The game itself is VERY barebones for the development time and the upgrading system for the few guns you do have is a crappy trade off system that disuades you from trying to be a strong as possible. But my biggest problem, very disappointing soundtrack atm. KF2's music brought so much adrenaline and excitement to the typical hoard shooter genre, and that's without even including Demon Hunter. The few tracks KF3 has just feel so lacking and weak. Even the reuse of the KF2 menu music in game has lost a lot of the grit and excitement it had. This is a launch day post so changes are expected, but as of now, this game does nothing for me but make me wanna play KF2 instead

review_text: Ive played all Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Nioh 1 and 2, Lies of P, Wo Long, Lords of The Fallen, Another Crab, Ninja Gaiden, Khazan, etc. This game is actually really good. Admittedly, I think they do a very poor job of explaining the mechanics. They use so many words to explain very simple things, which makes it confusing. There's is a bit of censorship concerning the historical figures, but it's in a way that you probably won't care as much or notice if you know much about late Ming history. The story is pretty interesting, albeit short on details like a darksouls game. Pretty good concept imo.

title: WUCHANG: Fallen Feathers Deluxe Edition
review_text: Game started to get fun but issues compound and makes it kinda just a chore to play. Good: Skills tree is fun albeit some skills feel useless, world and atmosphere are pretty good, map design its cool taking path and finding these areas are connected. Armor is pretty varied and I like the designs from bare minimum to armored. Bad: Did every major boss fight as far as I know, a few fun ones, some forgettable, and some cheap but nothing really stood out as a great fight. Recovery is slow, this game has the most punishable perfect parry I've seen to the point you parry and are hit by a second hit because the enemy ignores it, there is a certain lag to actions its not terrible but repeated its noticeable. Boss movesets aren't great they either do a 30 hit combo(where if you miss a dodge you die), every attack is a gap closer or knock down giving you no time to heal or create distance, or just extremely easy. This game could be better with some tuning but as of now 1 playthrough is enough.

title: WUCHANG: Fallen Feathers Deluxe Edition
review_text: Played every FROM soulslike, all the major soulslikes, this one's a bit on the easier side, but it's a fun romp. The good: Exploration is phenomenal in this one. Art direction HDR implementation Variety of builds OST SFX Lore and world building Questlines Good bosses Enemy design Armor design Character design Voice acting (CN, never tried ENG as dubs suck) The bad: Game runs like dookie. It just does. With a 5090 and 9800X3D, I had to play with so many settings in my BIOS, windows, afterburner, RTSS lock, NVCP, and in game settings to get it mostly smooth at 160fps lock with framegen. There's something wrong inherently with the frame pacing and how it's programmed, delivering from CPU. -1 for this. Bosses can be a little too easy, and some hitboxes sorely need re-working Runbacks, lord do I hate those runbacks. No ladder or elevator should be put before a boss imo, this is one of the things that should be left behind in the past from old level design artificially upping playtime

title: WUCHANG: Fallen Feathers Deluxe Edition
review_text: It's a rally good game. The level design is well put together kind of like Dark Souls 1 where you create shortcuts and give you a sense of where things are. Combat is also pretty fun, though can get annoying with hyper armor with some enemies. Moves can also get clunky with the details. The map and environmental design is top tier. Lots of nice details that tells a narrative. Character designs are also top tier. The game is also not grindy at all and pretty forgiving in letting you retry the boss more or less instantly. You'd think the narrative would be soft given that it's a Chinese game, but it'll surprise you with how gruesome it gets, though this is the international version. There's is a bit of censorship concerning the historical figures, but it's in a way that you probably won't care as much or notice if you know much about late Ming history. The story is pretty interesting, albeit short on details like a darksouls game. Pretty good concept imo.

title: Killing Floor 3 Deluxe Edition
review_text: After many days on KF2, this game had me hyped up to launch, despite the delay. However, after 3 rounds of survival i've got some gripes with KF3. The QoL additions are great, mantling, mid-round restock, and dashing are awesome. But, the gunplay is a bit stiff and aim assist on controller is wonky with no options for it. The game itself is VERY barebones for the development time and the upgrading system for the few guns you do have is a crappy trade off system that disuades you from trying to be a strong as possible. But my biggest problem, very disappointing soundtrack atm. KF2's music brought so much adrenaline and excitement to the typical hoard shooter genre, and that's without even including Demon Hunter. The few tracks KF3 has just feel so lacking and weak. Even the reuse of the KF2 menu music in game has lost a lot of the grit and excitement it had. This is a launch day post so changes are expected, but as of now, this game does nothing for me but make me wanna play KF2 instead

title: Hatsune Miku Logic Paint S+
review_text: So, is this a bulked up Logic Paint S? No! Not at all. This is it's own thing, most things vary between the two. First up, the illustrations. After each puzzel in the original, you got an illustration with the thing you made in the image. Here, that's not the case. Instead, you get costumes to put on the vocaloids, along with room items. Illustrations are now completion rewards for special puzzels and completing a characters set of puzzels. Speaking of... No reused puzzels (besides the hairpin lol). Everything is new. You get 5 10x10's, 30 15x15's, and 25 20x20's for the 6 vocaloids. Each one has 5 special puzzles 75x75 in length. You get 3 "other" 100x 100's as well. Stars also work different... ...Kinda. Clear the puzzel, use no hints, and clear with less than 3 mistakes. Those are the goals to hit. Use em' to get songs. And those are all new too! No oldies! Oh, and theres a hard mode if you turn puzzle assist off. That's all. Glory to Miku. I will endure for her.

review_text: More of 3.5/5 than 4/5, at ToR I'm in the 1% that maxxed all 22 character trees so hear me out: Something you need to know about SS is it has an artificial soft-cap to progression, as well as a hard cap. Each char can be leveled infinitely but the skill trees (22) cap at 170 skill points each, with each 3-4 tiers offering a minor global char stat buff - that's not the issue though. REGARDLESS of you having 0% bonus XP, or + 400%, you will generally be between lvl 50-60 by end of area 1, and 200-230 at Overlord (the 2nd endless mode) zone 6 - this is because, frankly, the game is poorly optimized. The devs confirmed this soft progression cap on steam 1yr ago. This make each run of SS feel VERY monotonous and repetitive. It takes roughly 1hr30min to get each char to 170 with the 50% bonus rune - huge time sink. Follow these tips though: Disarray>Shattered>Brittle>Fragile Doom>Bleed>Poison>Fire Overall SS has amazing features, but poor execution. It's evoled Army of Ruin, NOT Vamp Surv.

review_title: FPS is not a review of the game.
review_text: Played this game for quite a while on Steam and am very glad to finally see it's console release. This is a city builder/town management type game with light survival mechanics. You'll be building a settlement and starting a new life for yourself after escaping war. It'll include raising crops, livestock, and ultimately a family. You are the overseer of your settlement and will have farmers, blacksmiths, tailors and such living and working within your village. This game is one of those types of games that many people find relaxing, as you hunt, gather resources, and tend to your village. I hope this proves to be a positive experience for Toplitz and they bring Wild West Dynasty over here as well. Medieval Dynasty is a well loved game on PC with a great community. Let's hope it continues here.

title: Medieval Dynasty - Echoes Edition
review_text: This is a slow-build up type of game. You will be hungry, you will be thirsty, you will be poor. After the first year, you may have a few people in your town, but not many. They wont be skilled, and they have their own needs. Taxes suck, but not really. You have ample ability to make money by hunting, crafting, and prioritizing what your people do. Build 3 woodsheds, and 2 excavation sites. Build 10 houses and the worker areas. Know that this will skyrocket your taxes, which are due in the spring. When you notice how prices work, you notice that meat and simple crafted tools are easily produced and sell well. Also hunting bandits for coin and loot is not hard at all. You can change the difficulty and game options mid-play, which means you can turn off stamina, or get infinite carry weight. Really, if you set up your villagers well, you can sell firewood for a living, and slowly go from hunting to having a merchant empire. Clunky in a survival sandbox way, but fun and replayable too. GG

review_title: LAYERS OF FEAR Meets SILENT HILLS P.T.!
review_text: This game likes to mess with you hard.  Not just in the typical "Got Ya!" way, either, like some other horror games do...but in a more psychologically TROLLING kind of way.  The scares feel more proper & earned instead of repetitive or cheap. The experience will feed on your anxieties, making you wary due not knowing what to expect from one moment to the next. As far as visuals, gameplay, audio & performance are concerned...so far, there really is nothing that concerns addressing.  The game is 9/10 overall on flawlessness. Bonus Tip:  Once you're finally able to enter your room for the first time, you can watch the original Night Of The Living Dead.  However, you only need to watch up until Johnnie says "They're coming for you, Barbara" to unlock the Achievement of the same name.  Also...if you complete the "puzzle" for that room, the movie will end & the tv will just say "no signal".

That is just awesome for adeveloper to do in this day and age.

review_text: With 50+ hours total spend on Thomas and Bob, I can positively say this game is a hidden gem for turn-base RPG gamers. The inmates and setting are filled with entertainment pop culture and classic prison movies references, which put a nostagic smile on my face. The minigames can be confusing at first, but you can surpass them with enough practice for extra money. The time-passing and deadline essence of the game haven't given me issues since I'm experienced in time management games from games like "Frostpunk" and the "Persona" series; this mechanic may frustrate to some, but it's not impossible if you plan ahead. There is also action-based dice rolling elements like in Disco Elysium, but sadly you can't save scum manual saves if you fail a check. The combat itself is challenging at the beginning and end segments of the game, so train, make inmate friends, and prep your gear. Lastly, the soundtrack is banger and I can't wait to come back to this game as the upcoming third protagonist!

Contrary to the good, "bosses" each had a gimmick and some were less clear than others on how to "defeat" them. I keep this vague as to not spoil anything as it is truly an enjoyable experience but because of this design it caused the pacing to feel off. review_text: If you have ever been to a bar you have probably seen one or all of these games. I on the other hand, am a degenerate, who spent every second that I wasn't working or sleeping, hustling GoldenTee golf games at the local sports bar in the late 9o's early 2000's. Doesn't matter because there are no leaderboards or online play, which is extremely disappointing. I will be the first to admit this game is far from perfect but that won't keep me from giving it five stars for Atari having the ******* to bring a 25 yo game to console, just for some old heads to relive the past for a moment. title: Kinki Spiritual Affairs Bureau
review_text: Hilarious concept with genuinely fun gunplay and a surprisingly competent story. Has the loveably janky feel of something like Oneechanbara, just a great game that doesn't take itself overly seriously but is clearly made with care and passion. I can't overstate this: the game is absolutely hilarious and competently written. Especially if you know your J-horror and Shinto tropes, you will instantly fall in love with this game. And most shocking of all is the depth of the worldbuilding and story. There are near Metal Gear levels of care given to cutscenes and storytelling, and just one mission in, you will actually start understanding the rules and consistency of a world where ghosts can DM each other and a smoking girl dressed in a school uniform can kill them with the impunity and skill of Leon Kennedy meets Doomguy. It actually works so well, and the level of depth given to this world will sneak past the mild jank and genuinely charm you, like Deadly Premonition.

title: Neon Noodles
review_text: Very happy this came to console.  I think the game is well priced for its content and polish.  I highly recommend it.  However, the controls are more than odd in several spots.  What would be a 9/10 game gets bumped down to a solid 8.  You get used to the quirks, and I've yet to encounter a bug, but it begs the question; was there not a single console / controller using gamer in the office to play test this?  Using the "B" button as it normally is, but then also as a way of backing out of the current level is a baffling choice.  Why not assign the completely unused "View" button?  Also, the text menus between levels are easy to read and fit the game's aesthetics, but I have no clue which text window I'm currently in.  Fortunately the actual gameplay control mapping works very well, but also highlights the minor odd choices I'm quibbling about.  This is a difficult qenre to get working well on a gamepad.  Again, minor gripes aside, strongly recommended, and happy to see it ported.

title: Eriksholm: The Stolen Dream
review_text: It's a shame that this game isn't getting the attention it unquestionably deserves. Eriksholm is the best stealth game I have ever played. Period. The amount of player freedom is mind blowing. You can handle scenarios with an incredible degree of flexibility & creativity. You can play with the agility of your unbridled imagination, within the limits of the game's ultra smooth, dynamic coding. The AI is realistic, & the world feels genuine, from the reactions of the human NPCs to their response, I've never seen such confident programming in any other stealth game. Eriksholm is a massive paradigm shift, opening up totally new levels of possibility for the genre. The game also has some of the most remarkable graphics I've ever seen - especially in the cinematic cutscenes. The expressions convey emotional depths in digital characters that haven't been expressed in gaming before.  I believe the only appropriate word for a game as revolutionary as Eriksholm is a Singularity. Bravo!!!

title: System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster
review_text: System Shock 2 is one of, if not the best, immersive sims in existence alongside Deus Ex and Thief. Until now, though, it wasn't available on console. As expected, Nightdive has done a fantastic job bringing this classic to console for the first time. They've touched up the graphics while still maintaining its original look. This isn't a remake, it's a remaster, so it looks like a 1999 game with very minor graphical improvements. Additionally, they included scans of the cover art, disc, manual, strategy guide, interviews, reviews, etc.  The only minor complaint is that the UI could be enlarged.

title: System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster
review_text: Played this back in 99' on PC and it was one of the best games I have ever played. If they can add options to adjust the HUD, a more clear controller layout and make using the controller more "efficient", then I'll give this game 5 stars.

review_title: One of the Best TMNT Games - Hades but Turtles
review_text: If you're new to rougelikes this game will probably feel brutal at first but it's very fun as you get better and gain an appreciation for the grind. I went from being skeptical about the concept to 100%'ing it. Crossplay online co-op and great voice cast. Important tip: Don't mash the dash button, time it. During a dash you're invulnerable so rather than frantically trying to escape an enemy's attack zone, time your dash to precisely avoid the frames you would have taken damage. That efficient use of dashing keeps you on cooldown less often and will help with survival.

review_text: Plays like a simple, old arcade racer but without the timer and no doing laps. There's nothing complex about this, quick and easy to jump into. Handles good, quite forgiving if you aren't good at arcade style racers. Instead of beating a clock or trying to finish first, you just gotta survive to the end.  Choose your vehicle (once you unlock some), same for weapon. If you select to do a pursuit, just hunt down the target cars then go to the finish line which is easy if you don't deplete your health bar. If you select to do a delivery, just have to survive to the finish but if you blow up, have to do a pursuit again to get your tapes back. Not too much of a grind to get money. Can bribe the "haters" for R$5K before a race to lower difficulty. Has a pixelated filter option. Music plays a big roll in making the racing fun so if you like the tunes, you'll have fun. Easily worth the price. Not much to the game, plays like a simple arcade racer and I like it.

title: Strike Mission XS
review_text: An enemy force threatens thousands of innocent lives with its army and It's your job to take them down before that happens. In your ready for battle hellicopter, you'll use a machine gun, missles and strafing maneuvers across seven missions to take down the enemy. Every mission does take place on the same map but it's different areas each time. If you fly by an area that gives you an on screen danger warning, you're not meant to be there yet. Just fly by because those enemies are extra strong on purpose until it's time to go there. You'll have three lives across all seven missions so engage the enemies carefully. You do get full health, fuel and ammo upon respawning. Be sure to double check those stats when starting new missions because they sometimes auto replenish. Even so, if you manage resources well enough, there's plenty for all the missions. Albeit short, Strike Mission is fun to play. It has easy achievements and a few missions that do offer a good challenge.

review_text: The story was absolutely amazing, the voice acting was better than many of the triple A games out today, and I actually grew attatched to some of the main characters. It's simply a good game, the gameplay is smooth,it has a metric **** ton of replayability, and each kill i made gave me a little dopeamine hit, the game just feels that good. I honestly have no negative feedback for this game, sure, it might be a bit on the shorter side (~4 hour long story), but thats all you need to enjoy it. This is the perfect game if you're looking for a short, freakin awesome game to finish during the weekend or inbetween other larger games. Overall, just buy the game, you will not regret it

I completed all story missions (including support group) on the day of purchase, while length may be a concern it has a bunch of challenges and is a blast to replay. The game wants you to master each level and I love it. Check out the other games mentioned for a similar experience ( Primarily just Severed Steel and Trepang 2, the others are still amazing but raw gameplay is what I felt these two titles shared with this game.) I this experiance honestly makes me want to check out the other titles made by the devs and try them. I don't want to spoil any gameplay, but I will say it can be difficult at times, in a fun way since the levels are short. It is in no means impossible to beat, definitely easier than Super Hot. All you need is time and mapping skills to beat the levels. Each level usually lasts less than two minutes since their all time based which makes them easy to retry. The art style reminds me of Risk of Rain 2, which is beautiful. Seriously, play this game, it's literally on Game Pass!  I beat it... Almost cried. Would love a sequel, or a spin off. I cannot get enough of this game.

title: Mainframent
review_text: *Edit: Now 4,000 gamerscore Like an early 1980's home computer platforming game. Has the aesthetic, gameplay, original ideas & fun simplicity of the era but runs way better. Starts easy, gets decently harder at level 10 unless using cheats in options (like invincible) but that robs the fun. Sweep dirt & jump/broom hang to climb your way to finding all level punch cards & deposit them, 1 at a time (unless unlimited cheat is on), to restore power. When power is on, grab all batteries in the level that just had it's hazards go live then get to the exit.  A perfect level run (includes no damage) will turn on & combine all 3 progress lights above level door to one green light. This is extra challenge for replay value, affects nothing. Only collecting enough batteries to power end game elevator matters for progress. 16 levels & hub area shows a corridor at top blocked by red gates, not sure if this means anything, I don't see a way to drop them. Same is true for some of the levels.

title: Volcano Princess
review_text: Let us dispense with the pleasantries. I, your humble yet discerning narrator, have subjected myself to the digital crucible of Volcano Princess. One might be tempted to dismiss it as mere child's play, but to do so would be a grave error, a testament to one's own intellectual improverishment. The graphics, initially charming in their simplistic way, soon become a source of creeping dread. The blank, soulless eyes of the digital princess stare into your soul, judging your every failure. The soundtrack, a cacophony of gurgles, whimpers, and high-pitched screams, burrows its way into your subconscious, never truely leaving you. The true horror lies not in the gameplay, but the atmosphere. The game creates a pervasive sense of dread, a feeling that you are being watched, judged, and slowly consumed by something melevolent. Volcano Princess is not for tHe faint of hEart. it's a game that wiLl test your limits. if you dare Play, do so at your own risk. you May never be the samE...

A lot of visual novel nowadays always have the main character as a female who have male love interests, its really nice to have a male`s perspective for a change it makes the story much more immersive being a guy playing this game. If only there were more stories out there like this. i definitely recommend this game be given a chance

title: Flower Shop: The Complete Story
review_text: From what I experienced, Flower Shop is a cute, colorful, charming, and romantic VN. It has fun characters, cheesy yet heartwarming writing, and nice looking art. But it does have its flaws. The music is extremely generic, the gameplay and getting the good endings for the 4 routes may be confusing for some new players, and the story is really bland. The VN is also very short, you can beat this in like 2-3 hours. Even with its flaws, I still enjoyed Flower Shop, mostly because it delivered what I wanted from this VN, good romance. Is it worth the full price, No. I much rather y'all pick this up when its on sale. So if Flower Shop still interests you, then get it when it's on sale.

title: Architect Life: A House Design Simulator
review_title: The bones are there,but no meat
review_text: The actual designing of the floor plan is good. However, the lack of variety in objects holds the design element back. Placing objects is frustrating due to angle of camera doesn't give good reference for height. Hard to tell which ways doors will open. When using Snap turned off it is almost impossible to rotate items parallel to anything. Graphics aren't great when touring site, everything lacks detail and depth. Also the fov is odd and while you seem to be average in height compared to the house you tower over items. Lighting is dim from lights. Its a good start, but needs improvement to reach its price tag (ie free updates and dlc to fill the voids)

title: Robots at Midnight
review_text: I didnt know it was a souls-lite going into it. While they are fun they typically aren't to my liking for combat purposes. I played this game on Master mode and it took me about 9.5hrs to beat it.   I like the aesthetic choice to include weapon and gear designs. It's not too grueling especially if you make use of your parry and M.I.T.T abilities. I didn't use the third ability at all. Punch and finger gun were good enough for me. Worth the price, no technical issues for me on Series x. There's a new game + mode with a harder difficulty if you want it. I hope they make a second game in this universe with more outfits and some neon ish weapons. Fun game

title: Robots at Midnight
review_text: For those who are struggling with"Souls like" games,this is for you. The battle engagement mechanics are similar but not as complicated. The gear & weapons that you find (You will find at least in 2 in your first 3-4 hrs) are interesting & upgrading them to see the stats increase to help you defeat the scrappers on your way to find your father & what happened to the planet of YOB. If you want a game where you can lay back & chill. This game is for you. If you want a semi open world with bits of exploration. This game is for you.I could go on... So why are still reading my review & not playing already? Can't wait to see what screenshots & videos you post. And remember... Gaming should be fun like Robots At Midnight.

title: Robots at Midnight
review_text: I'll admit up front that there are, of course, better examples of souls games on the market (Elden Ring, Dark Souls 3, Bloodbourne). There are also better non-fromsoft souls games (Wo Long, Lies of P, Khazan). Indeed, there are better sci-fi souls game too (The Surge 2, Hell is Us, Remnant 2). There are even better cutesouls, tho not very many (Kana, Little Witch Nobeta, Another Crab's Treasure). But there's something about this game. It feels...personal. Intimate. Non-derivative. Almost like it's someone's off-clock experiment. It's got charm, and even a little gravitas. And despite not being a huge game, the level design feels intentional in a way that makes it feel far bigger than it. And like the games listed above, and all good souls games, it does an excellent job of rewarding exploration in such a way that you want to look under every rock and behind every tree. It feels like the people who made enjoyed making it; as though they made the game because they enjoyed it.

title: Robots at Midnight
review_text: The game starts reasonably well, and the setting is interesting, but it leaves you wanting more. PROS: Art style, level design, boss fights, difficulty options. CONS: Repetitive combat, lacking enemy variety, half-baked story. OKAY: Crafting/upgrading, the MITT gameplay mechanic, lore. Worth mentioning that this game has a Hero mode (easy) and a Master mode (hard); one feels like a cakewalk, while the other feels like a souls game. The difference is based on how much damage enemies deal to you and how fast they attack, with parries being required on Master difficulty. When you learn why it's called "Robots at Midnight", don't think too highly of it; I initially got a Dying Light vibe only for it to leave me incredibly underwhelmed by it being scripted. This game took me about 8 hours to beat, which isn't great for $20. Definitely wait for a sale. Overall, it's fine. Just remember that this is an indie game though.

title: Chronicles of the Wolf
review_text: If you've played SotN then you'll feel right at home playing this. It's challenging to the point where it can be tough but is always fair. The atmosphere and feeling of dread are top notch. Plenty to find and do as well. Took me just about 20 hours to 100% the map and find all the equipment. It's also very well polished as I ran into zero bugs and the game also only crashed once. Two tips: It might be better to use the Dpad as the joystick is a little sensitive and you may find yourself sliding or throwing a sub weapon unintentionally. Also do not push RB during the boss rush mode, otherwise your game will freeze. Very solid game overall and worth the $20.

The caps on daily quests, riding lessons, transmute crystals, guilds, trader listings, and event tickets disincentivizes long-term play. Base classes are generally overshadowed by dlc classes despite the advent of subclassing now fostering homogeneity. Sets are plenty but many are useless. Server performance is rough.
