title: Police Simulator: Patrol Officers: Ultimate Duty Edition
review_text: If you've ever wanted a realistic police sim where you play as an everyday patrol officer doing mundane things like writing tickets, towing cars, responding to traffic collisions, DUI checkpoints, and on occasion intervening in crimes like robbery or drug dealing, then this game is for you. Keep in mind, this is NOT L.A. Noire, a True Crime game, or any action-oriented cop game. This is an accurate procedural law enforcement game where you are assigned tasks during your shift and are held accountable for any and all mistakes. Also, keep in mind this is a low budget indie game, so don't expect AAA quality. There is nothing else like this on console right now, and I'm glad the devs released this game. The devs confirmed they will keep updating and adding new content as well.

title: Police Simulator: Patrol Officers: Ultimate Duty Edition
review_text: I'm honestly not sure how this game has the rating it does, I was extremely disappointed. This game, like so many others in the modern day, is a great concept with poor execution. All of the actions take longer than they should, there is no ease of access and it all feels like a menu simulator. I understand this is a "realistic sim," I'm not complaining about doing the actual tasks, but the system for performing tasks is tedious. Beyond my nitpickings about the UI and bland/repetitive voice lines, the game is unbelievably buggy. Being a game from a small developer, I wouldn't criticize small bugs, but most are game breaking. Just one example, traffic jams. The games AI are morons. Cars will get randomly stuck on open road, causing traffic behind it to build up. If you get cars to do u-turns, they often get stuck doing that as well. Then because of the game rules, you can't command them to move anymore, so they just sit there, in the middle of the road, for eternity.

title: Soulstone Survivors
review_text: More of 3.5/5 than 4/5, at ToR I'm in the 1% that maxxed all 22 character trees so hear me out: Something you need to know about SS is it has an artificial soft-cap to progression, as well as a hard cap. Each char can be leveled infinitely but the skill trees (22) cap at 170 skill points each, with each 3-4 tiers offering a minor global char stat buff - that's not the issue though. REGARDLESS of you having 0% bonus XP, or + 400%, you will generally be between lvl 50-60 by end of area 1, and 200-230 at Overlord (the 2nd endless mode) zone 6 - this is because, frankly, the game is poorly optimized. The devs confirmed this soft progression cap on steam 1yr ago. This make each run of SS feel VERY monotonous and repetitive. It takes roughly 1hr30min to get each char to 170 with the 50% bonus rune - huge time sink. Follow these tips though: Disarray>Shattered>Brittle>Fragile Doom>Bleed>Poison>Fire Overall SS has amazing features, but poor execution. It's evoled Army of Ruin, NOT Vamp Surv.

title: Lost in Random: The Eternal Die
review_text: I can see how fans are disappointed with the direction this franchise took, but never having played the original, I had fun with this one. I see the comparison to Hades, but this felt easier to pick up and progress through.  Every run had something new to come back to at the main hub. New weapons, wardrobe changes, and permanent upgrades. Picking upgrades and fitting them into the right slots and color matching made every run something different. I started one run, gunning straight for attack damage. I found some good drops and was able to switch the build on the fly and still make it work. It's responsive and runs well. Never had any performance issues. The art style is wonderful. The dice mechanic is fun, and while I tend to ignore the random mechanics, it is fun when it plays in your favor. If you want to try a new roguelike that has the fundamentals of what we know and enjoy, I would give this one a try.

review_text: As a huge Tron fan since childhood, I was going to buy this anyway, but sad to say this is an unlikable entry.  The overall look is good and fits well with the aesthetic of the second movie.  The game itself is very shallow with boring missions, clumsy combat, and overall super repetitive gameplay.  The light cycle (which should be a high point of any Tron game) feels like an afterthought with light cycle combat being rare and absolutely terrible when it does happen.  Enemy cycles just bounce around the environment and can be defeated by driving in circles with your lightwall.  They head straight for it.  Shameful.  The light-jet was even worse.  Plot was ok.  Dialogue or interaction menus are super annoying with unneccessary extra 'clicks'.  Even die hard Tron fans are cautioned. Wait for $9.99 or less.  This is way too basic, amateurish, sloppy, annoying, and boring for $24.99.

review_text: Since my initial review, I've put more time into FBC and I'm enjoying myself. Also, the devs released a patch addressing a lot of the issues I had. They made onboarding a whole lot better by making CL3 available from the start. Progression has also been improved immensely. Not only did they lessen the grind, they separated cosmetics and equipment to make unlocking what you want easier. I still think there should be a proper tutorial and kit based items should be unlocked from the get go. However, this is a fantastic start! The gunplay could be more punchy, but it's serviceable. It looks/sounds good and runs well. Although, I've been noticing a lot of connection issues lately. I can't tell you how frustrating it was to take on Sticky Ricky solo. Overall, a fun game that's been improved fairly quickly but could still use refinement in areas.

There are a few neat things like special features, a CRT filter and cool screen borders to switch through. By and large though it's 30 bucks to conveniently play the old trilogy through your Xbox, it's up to you if you're down for that or not. As someone whose Gex 3 disc was badly scratched, lost and has no working N64 or original PlayStation to play this on, I am DEFINITELY not regretting this purchase. And I can't even rate it lower than a 5/5, because even if a newer, younger player doesn't dig the outdated graphics or sometimes wonky 90's gameplay then that doesn't mean there's actually anything wrong with this game. For what it is (a port) it checks every box. If you had complaints about Gex back then, then you'll still have those complaints now. If you loved Gex back then, then you'll love it now. title: Thief Simulator & Prison Simulator
review_text: This is a pure stealth, modern thief simulator. You must avoid detection, and cannot harm or kill your way in or out. You must drive janky cars, weave your way between people and cameras on foot, sometimes even run like hell and hide, and use that brain of yours to work out a viable sequence of actions to solve each puzzle.  I had no problem beating this game, there were no bugs big enough to break it for me, and the only reason I stopped playing is because of the pure stealth aspect. 35 hours, compared to the hundreds I have logged on Payday 2 while completing similar enough activities.  If you can meet it where it's at and accept it for what it is though, you just might be able to enjoy your time with this game, every bit as well as I have. Seriously, I still want to play it again some time. But I like stealth, janky driving, and reverse Santa Clausing everything that isn't nailed down. I'd suggest ignoring all the bad reviews, if this game has what you're looking for. Enjoy!

review_title: Save your money, $5 on Steam and not great
review_text: "Does not contain jump scare." Not plural, bad translations everywhere. This games feels slow, sluggish, boring, and not at all engaging. A novel idea, walking alone through an abandoned prison, but this game is not that. Theres a cheesy bunch of "jump scare" throughout, mid-century horror trope sound effects included! A monster shows up some, benign and not scary. There's kind of a story? It's very bad. The prison is not a convincing prison (maybe if you're a teenager that just watched 'The Rock' or some prison reality TV shows). There's details that make no sense (BTC transactions but the tech involved in the prison is 90"s at best?) The "story" there is goes in too many directions with no personal involvement. Each letter interacted with only lends to further convolte other details. There is no challenge, either. Given a door that needs a 4 digit code, you find the code in a note. Instead of challenging the gamer to remember the code, it is then prominently displayed on the screen.

title: Star Trucker - Deluxe Bundle
review_text: Idk, I was really excited for this game. Loved the demo and was hoping it would be expanded on a lot up to release. The visuals are nice and I really like the tactile sense of having a lot of switches and buttons to press in your cab.  Unfortunately, the novelty wears thin pretty quickly. There isn't much Trucking. You get a job, pick up trailer, drive to warp gate, go to next hub. There isn't a lot in the sense of "Hauling". No 6DoF. This was genuinely baffling. The true game is managing your truck. Power cells. They run all your trucks systems, drain relatively fast, are expensive, and are just a pain to deal with. It really takes away from the open road, trucking experience when you're near constantly worrying about managing power in your truck. The truck itself is also made of Aluminum foil. One hit will turn your rig into Swiss cheese. And honestly not a big deal, but irked me, is there is only one radio station that cycles the same 5 or 6 songs. The game just isn't there yet.

review_title: Defence is key, grind to earn try to learn
review_text: The game will award you health if you attack after you deflect, yes that is correct. Train yourself to fight back after deflecting, dodge Charged attacks or parry them. If you get hit you lose health, but if you deflect you have a certain amount of time to get it back by landing hits, I just beat the Scrapped Watchman boss like a cake walk with this trick with help.  Try Grinding a little, yes that's right, you need to level up, whatever your preference is, just look up some good Level up tutorials, you'll soon find out with the Deflect technique, that health isn't everything.  Finally learn the enemies combos, deflecting is good and everything, but you have legs, and can outrun most of the enemies without worry, so take your time. The game maybe hard, but loot really comes in handy, use it to your advantage. And enjoy the game even when you die, because you will die, a lot. But, if you use the deflect technique and regain your health you will do better. Good Luck.

review_text: This is the kind of horror experience I like to play. Very violent, very intense, and very realistic and disturbing. Things that can actually happen to you scare me more than ghost, vampires, and monsters. If you like the Outlast games, you'll definitely need to check this one out.  The game has a extremely bold and dark storyline. Definitely not for the faint of heart or the really young crowd. The gameplay is very much like Outlast, but with its own style and unique take on genre. It's designed to be challenging and keep you on edge the whole experience. This is not a easy game at first and it does take some practice. The graphics are great, and stylized to fit the dark tone perfectly. It runs good with no real bugs that I've seen. Plus, the price is a steal for this great horror experience.  We need more games like this in the horror genre. Check this one out...If you dare.

title: The Talos Principle Ultimate Collection
review_text: Gameplay is in the style of Portal 2, The Turing Test and older Sherlock Holmes games by Frogwares. Also a bit like The Witness, but with abilities and more varied puzzles. Story is deeply philosophical. Existentialism, rationalism, empiricism and transhumanism. Also theology, mythology and artificial intelligence. Do you do what you are told? Or blindly follow those before you? Or rather do whatever you want instead? Graphics are decent and has quality or performance option. There are some frame drops when inside the elevators, but I assume this is due to loading/buffering. Music is very fitting for the atmosphere and changes with each hub/nexus. There are quite a few mutually exclusive achievements which will require multiple playthroughs or reloading. I completed the story and collected all sigils (not including stars) without any in-game hints or outside guide in 17 hours (in-game save, not Xbox time). YMMV depending on your outside the box thinking. I used a guide for stars.

title: The Talos Principle Ultimate Collection
review_text: If you love first person puzzle games, this is for you. It also looks gorgeous and has a greatly customizable photo mode. I see another review complaining about frame rate, and while I suppose that's fair, I ask myself how much I care about good frame rates in a non physics based puzzle game. The answer is not much. Especially not enough to drop a 1-star bomb like they did. If you enjoy puzzle games, I recommend trying this game for yourself. This version also comes with the DLC and a brand new chapter so there's plenty of value. If you really enjoy this there's also a sequel and a free prequel (only on PC) named Sigils of Elohim.

review_text: First, ignore the reviews that bash on any portion of this game.  The price was worth the risk just to see how accurate the other reviews were, so I gave it a go.. After reading reviews about the cursor usage I had some doubts going in, but that faded within the first hour; it's actually pretty good, and there's hot keys to quickly move items if you read the button actions on the screen ðŸ¤£.   Overall, if you're on the fence like I was: It's fun, and if not- the price lessens the regret.  Enjoy! Common sense helps too.

title: Pacify and Emily Horror Bundle
review_title: Intriging. Scary. But has its flaws.
review_text: It is rare that a game can grab my attention the way this one has. It usually takes a deep story, strong voice acting and solid gameplay. Emily Wants to Play is missing the first two and it does not matter. The game is all about survival.  I did jump quite a bit. The scares were successful. Sometimes the anticipation of something happening was enough to keep me from even blinking. Of course in fear of being greeted by one of the house's inhabitants. My favorite aspect was figuring out what I had to do to survive until the next hour. This element was appreciated. Where the game fell a bit short was AI difficulty and load times.  The game can be unforgiving at times when it starts to stack different rules. This is where load times come in. You can fail in seconds and have to wait close to 1 min for it to load. Rinse and repeat. It in no way hurt the experience too bad. But it can feel like a lot of waiting.  For $5 this game is a steal. I recommend this game to anyone.

title: Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon
review_text: Knew it was indie. But felt that, given the demo and footage, this game at least had potential. It really is much better than the standards I'd set for it. It does just a little bit of everything; fishing, scavenging, blacksmithing/gear crafting, cooking, has a great variety of play-styles to toy with thanks to all the dual-wielding possibilities and weapon types. Music, atmosphere and art direction are all above-average. There are slow-mo kill animations, varying landscapes and enemy types. And on that note I want to mention there's a cool feature involving a sketch book that you can take out pretty much whenever, and draw a sketch of whatever is in front of you. Overall there's a fairly large amount of content as well. This is a game I'd so far put on the same level as Oblivion (for the first time playing it), in terms of "a really cool, new dark fantasy RPG I can actually sink my teeth into." It's not perfect; there is some jank here. But what a breath of fresh air.

title: Steel Seed - Deluxe Edition
review_text: An absolutely beautiful game with some nice world building and wonderful scenery, but marred by stiff combat and a variety of glitches that are hard to overlook. A major glitch that frequently cropped up was climbable ledges simply not registering, which for a platforming game is rough, forcing the player to reload a save only to have another ledge rendered unfunctional (Beyond Good and Evil from 20 years ago plays better). Combat and movement never mesh well and are incredibly clunky, seeming slow and disjointed. Most of the game is in love with its ideas, doting on specifics like the drone companion, but it really struggles with their implementation, level situations that should be challenging are lessons in unnecessary frustration (some of the forced combat sections are just tripe even knowing the mechanics).   TLDR: It looks beautiful, feels like a classic title, but the techinical aspects of the game leave something to be desired; not really fun.

title: Steel Seed - Deluxe Edition
review_text: I loved the vibe, the locations, the lore, the stealth, and the platforming. The game is gorgeous with compelling underground biomes, but marred by bugs and the bewildering decision to wrest control of the camera at key moments... ENRAGING. When the game transforms into a fixed-camera isometric brawler or a 2D platformer, it suffers HARD. I'm also not a huge fan of forced combat sections in a stealth game and there are like four or so of them. I wanted to five star this game, but after nearly putting my controller through the TV after numerous arbitrary deaths, I just couldn't do it. Is the game good? Yes. Is it GREAT? Sadly, owing to some frustrating design choices, no. If you like stealth and 3D platforming get this game, but be prepared for some rough spots. My girl kept asking if I was OK, and I kept yelling, "this is going in my report!!!" Well, this is my report.

review_text: Deserves a bigger budget, that's for sure. It borrows from a lot of the same games and media as the recent jedi series, albeit a bit less soulsy. They both work fine, but the dodge is more predictive that reflexive, while the enemy attack animations feel like they're the other way around. review_text: I just want to say don't pay attention to the negative people reviewing this. They made this an "official release" in the store because it seems like they plan to just update this until they get to the full release version (1.0). But I will admit that it plays slightly worse than Splitgate 1. Think if Halo skipped from Halo 2 to Infinite. Its still Halo, but that much of a change all at once would definitely throw people off at first. That's the best way to describe the change from Splitgate 1 to 2. Its still Splitgate, but now with bigger maps, bigger lobbies, loadouts, perks, attachments, equipment, and sliding. But the core gameplay loop is still there

There's a heavy emphasis on making every weapon yourself (barring your first sword of course) and really tailoring your gameplay to your play style as you earn better metals and woods to work with and gather materials to fit those moulds. I really like the whole "kill each enemy type enough to earn their weapon blueprint" bit. I've just reached the Doyen Graves after a few hours of play and one particularly fun boss fight in a fortress, and while I wouldn't say the story is communicated in the clearest way from the start, I would say the characters are all interesting and funny in different ways! Don't sleep on this, it's worth the price of admission.

review_text: Firstly, the destruction is AMAZING, you could use this engine to make a great top-down shooter, military vehicle game (helicopters and tanks), large monsters destroying a city game, a spiritual successor to Red Faction (as the people with that license have just been sitting on it), or something else totally new. It's not difficult, the few times there were timers were pretty reasonable, but that sewer section was needlessly hard and frustrating. I took away a star due to the sewer section, not keeping the very long story concise, and there were too many tasks like, "Go upstairs and talk to some guy, for another cutscene after the cutscene you just watched," and too much traveling to the office or to the house in story mode, just put me there or give me a good immediate fast-travel option. Overall 4-stars, mostly fun, awesome destruction!

title: Deliver At All Costs

review_text: I chose correctly. This is a 9.0 game, and one which I don't have sufficient room to type the reasons why the various "complaints" you'll see in the other reviews here are unfounded; based on expectations of games catering to every single individual's preferences, like camera and car handling, the earliest part of a very deep and complex story (with a film-style script, outside of certain gameplay scenarios where it's the typical NPC barks & Quest-giver instructions), or just whatever didn't immediately feel like some other game that person is intimately familiar with. This is the vision of a team of experts, punching way above their weight class. The destruction of the environment being SO well-executed, completely uncompromising, and all-encompassing while ALSO being intrinsically tied to the gameplay experience, but without being MANDATORY; this is such a massive achievement in & of itself, but there's so much more to it than speeding thru buildings as they collapse. Amazing, 9/10.

The story is not good, because of poor voice acting and writing, so why are we required to travel across the map to drag on a boring conversation? Why can't missions take place on one map, rather than multiple zones interrupting flow? Why, for a game with unparalleled destruction are we often penalized for smashing into something? review_text: The game is like the first game on 3DS, but with so many new features, and improved graphics, improved combat, and crafting. The world is huge with beautiful environments to explore and collect items, harvest resources, and fight a variety of creatures, and enemies. The main storyline is good with time travel and the writing for npc is well done and funnny. Once you start playing you will be hooked, the game has that great game play loop of reward, collecting, crafting and leveling up as you explore the huge world with time travel. There are a lot of variety of mounts to ride, and also fast travel. There is a limited co-op, and 4 player multiplayer with it's different modes, also the developers have add new patches to multiplayer mode, and continue to make upgrades, and plan to support the game, hopefully with DLC. review_text: After 12 hours, smashing my head against the corruption-version of Seraph has drained the drive to continue. I've tried combinations of each faction and attempting unconventional strategies, but to get walled at the end after steamrolling through every previous fight, how does corruption feel anything but unfair?  20 strike damage, plus two corruption, plus doubling that corruption every turn is just too much. If the game's calculations were concrete and presented more information with each move, it would be less of an issue, but higher Covenant runs demand you rely on the rewind button, slowing pace to a crawl. Everything before the final boss feels euphoric. There are challenge runs to try (separate from community runs), there's more story, twice as many factions, and mutators are back for you to create the ideal challenge run. Other may feel conflicted on the art, but the developers give each artist credit when you zoom in on a card, which I applaud.

title: Monster Train Collection
review_text: On the artifact/card/resource/roguelike stuff it's basically a copy-paste of Slay the Spire, but that's fine because Slay the Spire is polished. The only difference is it changed Slay the Spire into a tower defense game (enemies advance several stages, only your towers (cards) at each stage can attack those enemies, enemies that make it to the end remove HP from your base which has to be kept alive. Main downside is it feels very short. A run might be 8-9 fights, but the first 2-3 fights are basically so simplified/basic that they don't really count. A run feels like maybe 3 actual fights that are a little significant. A Slay the Spire run feels 2-4x longer to me. Basically, by the time I've actually upgraded one or two units, gotten one or two sweet artifacts that are worth building a deck around and maxed one or two spells, the campaign is over before it feels like I really use them.

Finding the perfect swing angle and power level seems like a **** shoot. The game has no consistency with ball movement and momentum. While im sure some will find the radio station aesthetic interesting (the story), it became annoying after about the 10th hole. This seems trivial but i found it quite annoying. Restarting a hole isn't done quickly due to having to pause the game to the menu which is done through a graphical transition rather than instant. title: Hunt and Fight: Action RPG
review_text: Game has too many flaws at this moment. Combat is simple, yet ineffective because medium sized creatures block 20/20 attacks, then counterattack you to open you into a combo. Your counterattack is bugged and doesnt work. Often, youll get stuck on the environment while attacking or retreating and your ambush just reversed. Running is sooooo slow and boring. Furthermore, you can only carry 10 things and constantly have to run for x3 minutes back to town AT LEAST x5 times per mission OR leave all the treasure you found on the floor. Game autosaves once an hour, but you WILL die once every x2 minutes against opponents who block EVERY attack(85%). Very few secret areas. All underwhelming :/ Dont waste your time with this flop.

review_text: The Precinct is one of the best games I've played in years. It doesn't try to reinvent the wheel or milk the player, it just delivers exactly what a game should be: Finished, Affordable. The loop is smooth and satisfying, the city feels alive, and the visuals hit that perfect blend of nostalgic and modern. It hits the same itch as the classic GTA top-downs while adding its own police SIM flavor that makes every shift feel unique--You can also make custom shifts. I haven't been this happy about a game purchase in a long time --''no regerts''. It's the first game in years I've found myself thinking about even when I'm not playing. I truly hope the devs stick with this formula. This game deserves DLC. Equals into real future. You're on the fence. Buy it. Support this kind of game development. It's what the industry needs.

title: Palia
review_title: Honest review for people wanting to know about gameplay
review_text: First off, it is NOT pay-to-win. All microtransactions are cosmetic except one that gives your pet the ability to ship items every 10 mins. Some are gotten via Twitch or seasonal events for free. Game plays like Animal Crossing but anime humanoids, focusing on building and designing your own fantasy home and furniture. You hunt, catch bugs, fish, mine, and cut trees for materials to use or sell, buy upgrades and recipes, and garden and cook food for an exp boost to your skills. Everything can be done in groups except story quests. You also can date the NPCs to get more stat boosts. I personally don't have issues with the community in game, but I also am not in the Discord chats. Played on Switch 2 years ago and was glad to see my entire account and home ported over. That said, climbing can still be a chore and has needed tweeking since day 1, the map opens the shop if you try to use the same button to close it, and the fact you can't help people do quests you completed does stink.

review_text: Everspace 2 is a fun, fast paced, shipbased looter-shooter with a good story. It's a direct sequel to the first game but you don't need to play the first one to understand the second. The game play is more arcade than sim and the controls seem FPS inspired but you can customize them to be more sim like. The game is very combat focused. There's a ton to explore and find but be prepared to fight rather often. There's 3 ship classes each with 3 subclasses, for 9 ships total. They each have their own play style and abilities. My only complaint is that once you obtain a tier 4 ship the game gets very easy because of how OP you become. The only challenge are rifts with bullet sponge enemies and a hidden timer. Farming rifts are how you get legendary equipment which gets boring.  I overall really enjoyed the game and am excited for the free expansion coming spring 2024.

review_text: It's cool, but much harder than Hotline Miami.  There's no target-lock, and there's so many bright particle effects and also areas with bright lights (which there is no option to dim) it's hard to tell if a bullet is coming at you.  You also have way more enemies to kill before each checkpoint (even in the 3rd level there's like 15 to 20 guys to kill in one life), less useful cover and a hard time telling what is cover and what isn't, no way to scroll the screen a bit (there's just red arrows to indicate enemy presence, but if you can't see if they're behind cover you don't know how to enter the room).  Enemies also instantly sense you once you have line of sight of them, even if they have their back turned and are in a different room.  The only way to get a drop on enemies is the dodge and slow-mo. It's cool someone decided to make a prettier Hotline Miami, but why did they think it had to be much harder too?  The cheap needless deaths get annoying.

title: Operation: Polygon Storm + The Hong Kong Massacre Bundle
review_text: Welcome to the dark side of Hong Kong. Nice shooting action that demands quick thinking and trigger reflexes in order to survive. Twin stick shooter with some destructional environments, ragdoll physics, bullets, blood, and a dark mood electronic retro soundtrack. Graphics and sounds are nice, but when putting holes in enemies or being detected by them they seem to lack voice, which kinda takes away a sense of realism. Controlling your guy and shooting and dodging is challenging, as you will die...alot!! Your enemies are damn near perfect when shooting at you, and 1-hit kills are what they're good at. review_title: It does exactly what it sets out to do
review_text: This is not a bad game by any means. For me, I found the humor a little...young, and the combat a bit imprecise, but it all works fine, and the devs clearly had a vision, and they achieved that vision. If you like goofy, punny humor, and don't care about razor's edge precision in your arpg combat, then pick it up. I think i was hoping for more of an insider's lampooning of souls games, but it really has nothing to do with that. It's more about euro-style arpg tropes turned up to 11. In fact, you'll prolly enjoy the game more if you're not familiar with souls games, cuz you won't be comparing it to the flawlessly accurate melee combat and deep, organic exploration that you get from fromsoft. Which, to be clear, is a really unfair comparison to make. This is not a bad game by any means, and it's not trying to live up to dark souls. I'll prolly play some more when i'm in a goofy, childlike mood. And if you like goofy, frivolous humor, you'll probably love this. Just be aware what it is.

title: MotoGPâ„¢25 - Xbox One
review_text: Last Moto GP game I liked was 17. I've tried every year since and could only play a few races and I was done with them. GP 25 has pulled me back in. The introduction of pro and arcade will open this game up to new players while keeping the hardcore satisfied as well. I've mashed the breaks in mid turn completly overshooting the turn and not wipeout, very forgiving. Vets just play on pro and crank up the Ai. Supermoto, flat track are a nice add on and a whole new set of skills to learn. Flat and supermoto does feel a bit floaty but not awful. Mini bikes are hilarous fun. Downside is only 2 tracks for the 3 extra modes. Hopefully they add more tracks for these modes. Graphics are the best yet. Customization and animations outside of races mostly remain the same. Overall if you're looking to get back into MotoGP this is the game to do it. When I get off the game I find myself wanting to get back and I haven't felt that in a long time. Oh yeah, split screen racing. Buy it!!!

review_title: Reminded me of why I love video games
review_text: Clair Obscur reminded me that video games are at their best when they are treated as art pieces, not products, being passionately worked on by a group of creative people, and not a board room full of executives that will throttle all the true joy and life out of a game for the sake of reaching a wider audience. Its not afraid to have real heart and emotion, it assumes its players are adults with actual attention spans, and man, all the artists absolutely went off. From the world to the music, the cut scene direction, the sound design, all of it is the glorious end result of people bringing their passion and drive into something they truly wanted to do. To me, the unexpected popularity of this game also shows solidification of a trend in the gaming industry; that AA and indie can now not only compete directly with AAA games but also clearly surpass them with fewer resources, due to the passion and drive that propels these smaller studios like Sandfall Interactive.

title: Sunderfolk
review_text: Do you enjoy tactical RPGs? How about couch co-op games? If you do, and you have a couple of friends who feel the same, you might enjoy this game! Sunderfolk plays like a simplified TRPG, where each turn you play a card that lets you move and attack with your character (1 of 6, each one with different abilities). You control your character using a mobile device with the goal of your party completing the mission objectives (kill monsters, save victims, interact with objects, etc.) After each mission, your party returns to town to level up, improve your character, talk to townsfolk, and other typical actions in a TRPG. The mobile device controller allows you to scan a QR code in order to resume progress between play sessions, and to edit your Fate/Action decks as you get new cards to improve your character. So far, we have been enjoying the game, and are looking forward to finishing the story!

title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
review_text: I remember playing the original game on the xbox 360. I didn't really play again after skyrim came out. The one thing keeping me from playing oblivion again was the horrible leveling system. The remaster has simplified the stat system and now you can just play casually without being forced to micromanage your skill leveling to get the correct stats when leveling up. In the original, you needed 10 levels in a strength related skill to get 5 points in the strength attribute when you sleep to level up. If you didn't maximize to get 4-5 points in strength and endurance as a melee build each level, then you wouldn't be able to keep up with the difficulty increases as you reached higher levels. That forced you either power game, or just stay low level forever to keep the game from getting too hard. The remaster has made this into a more simple and relaxed leveling experience.

review_title: Best Silent Hill tribute in a long time.
review_text: I have been an obsessive Silent Hill fan since I was a child with 1-4 on PSX/PS2. Those games defined my taste in horror and surreal cinematic atmosphere, so let me be clear: This game gets it so right. The subway/mannequins/hospital vibe will be immediately familiar to SH fans, and it looks so good in UE5. The stilted voice acting and weird posters perfectly captures the dreamlike atmosphere of the originals, and the creators really use the fixed camera angles for maximum cinematic effect. Even the soundtrack sounds like golden age Yamaoka. As others have stated, combat is sporadic and the biggest focus is on the environmental storytelling and the classic horror puzzles, so if you prefer more of a slow-burn atmospheric surreal horror to nonstop action, this is right up your alley. If this was released as an official Silent Hill game I wouldn't have ever suspected otherwise. If you're as much of a fan as I am, you've seen these tropes many times before, but this one does them justice.

This game is very much rooted in the oldschool survival horror tradition. The most obvious influence being the old PS1/PS2 Silent Hill games, but with UE5 graphics, which mainly look very good. The game was made by a very small indie team on a budget, so there are some shortcomings and jagged edges here and there, graphically, technically and design wise. review_text: An absolutely beautiful game with some nice world building and wonderful scenery, but marred by stiff combat and a variety of glitches that are hard to overlook. A major glitch that frequently cropped up was climbable ledges simply not registering, which for a platforming game is rough, forcing the player to reload a save only to have another ledge rendered unfunctional (Beyond Good and Evil from 20 years ago plays better). Combat and movement never mesh well and are incredibly clunky, seeming slow and disjointed. Most of the game is in love with its ideas, doting on specifics like the drone companion, but it really struggles with their implementation, level situations that should be challenging are lessons in unnecessary frustration (some of the forced combat sections are just tripe even knowing the mechanics).   TLDR: It looks beautiful, feels like a classic title, but the techinical aspects of the game leave something to be desired; not really fun.

review_text: Just happen to spot this game on a compilation of "must plays" and also saw that IGN only gave it 6 so I knew this was going to be an awesome game. What I didn't expect was a total banger! Like so many, I love Metriodvania and Soulslike games and Mandragora mixes it with style and class, totally exceeding my expectations. The AMAZING art style, game direction/storylines, gameplay and a insane depth of upgrades and abilities is top notch! All that I can recommend is if you love the aforementioned game styles you will most likely love this game. I'll be hoping for a sequel...and if Primal Game Studios can top this bad boy then take my money!

title: Mandragora: Whispers of the Witch Tree
review_title: (Save Bug Fixed) Ridiculously Amazing TRUE Metroidvania
review_text: EDIT:  The Save bug seems to be fully fixed. This game would deserve a 5/5 easily, but due to launching the way it did (in testing this glitch WOULD have come up) makes it lose a star.  But yeah, this game is the perfect mix of Castlevania Symphony of the Night and something like Dark Souls. Combat is tough but fair, learnable, you won't die 14 times to learn a pattern, and there's enough RPG stuff to make this really meat-y with secrets, loot, crafting, interesting NPCs, etc.  The opening works well with keeping things controlled at first, opening up to let you explore at your own pace in multiple pathways as the first act gets closer to ending. The boss of Act 1 is tough, too! But you can win a boss that you lost on without grinding, but a different approach and well-timed item use will get you the success. The level tree is fun too! With Cross-classing at level 25. So much to do and I'm just at the end of Act 1 so far.

title: Leila
review_text: This game is like life: short, sweet, and full of lessons. Despite this game being quite short (about 1 hour and 15 minutes), you learn years-worth of information about the character through fitting and fulfilling puzzles that both symbolize what is happening and drive home each part of this endearing glimpse into the ups and downs of life. This is a developer with a vision and a determination to share an experience, not just take your money. Leila is a game you can enjoy regardless of who you are or where you're from. By covering real world topics without over-extending itself or becoming dull, Leila very modestly proves the journey is more important than the destination.

title: HexaScape: Cyber Defense
review_text: Basic info: Campaign - Endless - Player Maps - Map Editor PC Port (noticeable) Global leaderboard (PC & Xbox) Zero guides online H:CD is bad at being amazing, and amazing at being bad. The core concept SEEMS cool:You start on a preset or procedural map, and build the course baring some obstacles. Pipes connected to towers make them stronger. Green data nodes give you a skill point. Pieces are randomly generated. Here's the issue: You can only spend the skill points you earn on ONE tower of your choosing. Pipes give you a core tower point but the more towers connected, the slower you earn them. Enemies get stronger not just from the spawn nodes, but as the match goes on. Even if you play near perfectly, the odds are consistently ramping against you. I've placed in the single or low double digits globally on the maps, and it just wasn't fun or worth the effort. The map editor barely works on console as controller inputs will sometimes flicker the PC controls. 2 bugged achievements.

title: VENARI - Escape Room Adventure
review_text: These are my initial impressions. Will update after playing more. PROS: The Old School feel is nice. Pleasing environment to look at. Some puzzles are easy, some take solid thought so it's a good mix. I'm curious about the story. CONS: There are not even basic settings. Controllers NEED sensitivity options as moving puzzles is aggravatingly slow. There needs to be better contrast on the menu buttons. It's very difficult to see what's selected. Basic settings needed in a QOL update: invert 'Y' axis, turn off motion blur, controller sensitivity. Could also benefit from optional captions for the documents for accessibility. OVERALL: 2 stars removed for lack of any settings. Seems like it has good bones and I'm looking forward to seeing what it has to offer. Devs, please give us a QOL update with settings.

title: Mayhem Mail
review_text: This is a blast to play. Try the Steam demo, it gives a whole world to play. Fans of early home computer plaformer games like Miner 49'er, Sammy Lightfoot, Jumpman, and Hard Hat Mack (for some examples) should love this. It's a gem of a game and if those names are unfamiliar, also in the same genre as Arabian, Donkey Kong, Donkey Kong Jr., and the more recent game Donut Dodo.  If you are colorblind you can swap out the color of the mail & boxes for numbers or letters to match. It takes away their colors but I suppose that's to help avoid confusion. Just for fun and challenge, you can set this to random so sometimes it's colors but other times numbers or letters. The color/numbers/letters are randomly changed for each time you die & start the stage.  If a stage is too difficult and you need a hand, pause the game and you can access 3 cheats to assist, which can be turned off/on at any point of play, same for the color/number/letter theme but you will need to reset stage.

title: Promise Mascot Agency
review_text: Not everyone will "get" this game, but for those who do, it is pure bliss. The same studio that brought you Paradise Killer has now used their amazing worldbuilding skills to bring you a story where humans exist alongside cartoonish and bizarre mascots, basically their own species, and you play as a disgraced Yakuza ace voiced by the legendary actor behind Kazuma Kiryu himself. In the first ten minutes a guy gets shot, another cuts off his own pinky, and you meet an anthromorphic finger running a love hotel, and that is just the world this game exists in. So, you're getting an open-world Yakuza style management sim with the amazing creativity of Kaizen behind it, with a dash of Deadly Premonition and the original No More Heroes thrown in. If that's your taste in games like it is for me, don't hesitate. This is your game.

title: Blue Prince
review_text: Over 30 hours in,opened room 46 at hour 22 and i dont want to stop. Pure fun and addicting brain stimulation. If you like Myst,or Outer Wilds..this simply is a must play. The puzzles are challenging,unique,thought provoking and just fun. The progression loop feels rewarding and engaging. Music is top tier,zero bugs or performance issues. Its just a dang great,one of a kind experience. DO NOT LOOK UP THE GUIDES UNLESS YOURE ABSOLUTELY STUCK. The self discovery from exploring and documenting your findings is the entire purpose. Just explore/record/remember. And have fun in the mansion :) Also,i played on gamepass for over 25 hours,then bought the game. 30 bucks is a perfect price for this,well worth it. There are dozens of hours to be played in Blue Prince. Well done devs,you made a masterpiece!!

review_title: Very Fun Roguelite Puzzler; Emphasis on the Puzzler
review_text: Essentially a roguelite puzzler. Permanent progress is made indirectly (via learning mechanics, room layouts, west/east side differences}, and directly (passscodes for locks/computers, upgrades to your camp that give bonus resorces on day start}. Played about 10 days. On luck: While you can't always control â€¢whichâ€¢ puzzle you're capable of solving on any given day, there is almost always â€¢aâ€¢ puzzle you can solve. Layers and layers of mystery--make no mistake, the rooms are a pretense for the real game, which is played in your journal and in between your ears.   Not reccomended for anyone looking for a casual experience, or new to puzzle games. (Which means most gamepass players, who have a tendency to be both). Very happy to see this game on gamepass; I was initially going to buy it on Steam, but the game is platform-agnostic.  Highly recommended for puzzle lovers and real-life escape room enthusists (not digital escape rooms; this isn't a point-and-click game)

review_text: I would encourage you to jump right in.  This game was a rare gem - creative, supportive, frustrating, enchanting. review_title: Fun rougelike upfront. 1%er puzzle game afterward
review_text: This game on the surface is about using the roguelike room/drafting to find an entrance to "Room 46." That takes people a 24-36 hours on average. That is the first 1/3 of the game and when it moves into "most difficult puzzle game of all time" territory.  By the time you reach room 46 you should have pages and pages of notes. That is the easier part of the puzzles. Many after that require understanding of foreign language, uncommon english words, understanding of chess, learning an in game language. For myself I just give up, I'm looking up solution after solution and saying: "I would never figure that out ever", because I don't understand somthing from outside the game. I love puzzle games and never have played a game anywhere near as cryptic as this. It should be a fun ride for most but once you hit "room 46" best of luck because the game ceases to be accessable to 99.9% of the population after that.

review_text: Everyone buckle in, because i just saw the "time to beat" recommended is like 48 hours. I have been on some reddit posts and everyone talks about having 100+ hours in this game. If they were being honest they would probably say 300 hours for an average person. DO NOT feel discouraged if it takes you a long time and you will seemingly not make any progress for a few irl days. The graphics, mechanics, progression style all make this feel like the best puzzle game ever. I have played Myst, Full throttle remastered, and return to monkey island so i saw blue prince and thought "hey that'll be fun" yeah it'd be fun if i was sherlock holmes. For normal people you really have to be okay with failure and seemingly impossible puzzles. I would strongly recommend not playing this game if you just want to use walkthroughs to try beat it because that is just not how this game is supposed to be made and it might be a waste of time. Please just put 100 hours in and see what happens!

title: South of Midnight
review_text: Played through to the end and looking foreward to going through it again for the collectables. The environments are on par with Psychonauts 2. Very vivid and imaginative. The protagonist makes some questionable choices, but she's young with a chip on her shoulder so I managed to suspend disbelief. Combat fell a bit flat for me personally. Target lock negatively impacts your movement and it didn't feel right from start to finish. Platforming is a bit off as well at times. I had trouble getting onto certain ledges and sometimes Hazel would float on surfaces if I came in at a weird angle. What really kept me playing was the atmosphere and art direction. Especially the swamp towards the end of the game. Overall it's visually stunning but played it safe with combat/platforming mechanics. I still enjoyed my time with it though.

title: South of Midnight
review_text: I grew up playing story games on Playstation, PS2, etc. and feel like that genre of game has been left in the past. This game, brings it back in spectacular fashion. The visuals, characters, models, bosses, and art are stunning, the music accompanying boss fights is fantastic, and the acting and story are phenomenal. The UI is clean and easy to navigate and the traits/upgrades system is simple in a good way (shorter story-focused game). The only [sensible] complaints are regarding the combat, which I admit is fairly simplistic at its core but you can get a bit creative with it (but don't use target locking). Overall a fantastic story game, like playing through a unique and captivating movie. 5/5, make more games like this.

title: South of Midnight
review_text: This is a game with real heart and soul. Take Alice in Wonderland and add a bit of southern comfort and you've got South of Midnight. The environment is incredible, with each level featuring rich and vibrant designs. The story is heart-warming and endearing, showcasing the love and bond between mother and daughter. The game itself isn't too dense, featuring somewhat challenging combat and platforming without too much frustration. It's a game I would recommend for anyone wanting to engage more with the story. Definitely one you can throw on to sit back and relax with. The combat, however, gets repetitive over time and is isolated to mainly small arenas. There also isn't too much variety in enemy types. That being said the fights are fun and fast paced while still giving you and the character plenty of mobility. The ending felt a bit rushed but I will admit it's more about the journey than the destination. Still recommend as a simple and entertaining adventure game!

I was a little confused at first with CB, which made me a little disinterested, too. But by two hours in, I realized the game had real potential. Just beat it at nearly 100% achievements (can't get a few due to bugs), and I would strongly recommend it to anyone who is a fan of this genre. review_text: Cassette Beasts feels like a Metroidvania had a love child with Temtem. Amazing idea that was executed nicely. Sound design is great (vine ball seems a little loud, but that's a minor nitpick lol) and the music is absolutely amazing. Especially when they add the vocals to the mix under certain conditions. Gameplay is straightforward: Metroidvania style monster catcher. All creatures are viable, and can be used to great effect if you plan out the moves and make a strategy. The sticker system is a nice refreshing idea. You don't lose moves, you peel them off your monsters and can stick them back on to another if they are compatible. For a game that's being light-hearted, focusing on fun and laughs, it has a few surprisingly darker areas. I won't give anything away, but I will say it'll keep you hooked to the end. Battles are super fun and engaging too. They encourage you to find your own playstyle! Overall a definite 10/10 in my opinion. Like PokÃ©mon and Metroidvanias? Play this.

review_title: Somber Story. Satisfying Gameplay. Great Game.
review_text: This roguelike has gameplay like Warm Snow, but mechanics like Hades. Despite having an art style like Ashen, the vibe is more in line with Life Is Strange. In the real world you build relationships with characters, giving them gifts and chatting with them to learn more about them, as so they can provide buffs in the dream world. The dream world is the rogue loop: several layers/bosses deep, and about an hour long run to the end. Tons of weapons and boons to unlock as you progress. There is an easier difficulty option in settings, but enemies are no pushover in later zones. My only real complaint is that, playing this on my series s, it was causing my console fan to run a bit hard (comparably to something like a massive AAA game, such as Witcher 3). To my achievement hunters, be warned... This game is serious grind to unlock and do everything. Not as easy as other roguelikes, but still worthwhile. Also, this game is on sale regularly, so picking it up for around $5 is well worth it imo

review_text: Played through to the end and looking foreward to going through it again for the collectables. The environments are on par with Psychonauts 2. Very vivid and imaginative. The protagonist makes some questionable choices, but she's young with a chip on her shoulder so I managed to suspend disbelief. Combat fell a bit flat for me personally. Target lock negatively impacts your movement and it didn't feel right from start to finish. Platforming is a bit off as well at times. I had trouble getting onto certain ledges and sometimes Hazel would float on surfaces if I came in at a weird angle. What really kept me playing was the atmosphere and art direction. Especially the swamp towards the end of the game. Overall it's visually stunning but played it safe with combat/platforming mechanics. I still enjoyed my time with it though.

title: South of Midnight Weaver's Edition
review_text: I grew up playing story games on Playstation, PS2, etc. and feel like that genre of game has been left in the past. This game, brings it back in spectacular fashion. The visuals, characters, models, bosses, and art are stunning, the music accompanying boss fights is fantastic, and the acting and story are phenomenal. The UI is clean and easy to navigate and the traits/upgrades system is simple in a good way (shorter story-focused game). The only [sensible] complaints are regarding the combat, which I admit is fairly simplistic at its core but you can get a bit creative with it (but don't use target locking). Overall a fantastic story game, like playing through a unique and captivating movie. 5/5, make more games like this.

title: South of Midnight Weaver's Edition
review_text: This is a game with real heart and soul. Take Alice in Wonderland and add a bit of southern comfort and you've got South of Midnight. The environment is incredible, with each level featuring rich and vibrant designs. The story is heart-warming and endearing, showcasing the love and bond between mother and daughter. The game itself isn't too dense, featuring somewhat challenging combat and platforming without too much frustration. It's a game I would recommend for anyone wanting to engage more with the story. Definitely one you can throw on to sit back and relax with. The combat, however, gets repetitive over time and is isolated to mainly small arenas. There also isn't too much variety in enemy types. That being said the fights are fun and fast paced while still giving you and the character plenty of mobility. The ending felt a bit rushed but I will admit it's more about the journey than the destination. Still recommend as a simple and entertaining adventure game!

review_text: While not too graphically "hardcore", this game may not be for those with slightly weaker stomachs.  Organs(and what you may find inside) are realistically detailed & have jiggly physics.  The gameplay mechanics are pretty simple & quite intuitive. review_text: After finishing the first few worlds, I am beyond impressed with the work Argonaut Games put into both preserving the style of the original while adding modern elements to make the game more accessible. Specifically, the controls are a massive improvement over the original. On the flip side, the textures and rugged geometry keeps the vibes of the original intact. With that being said, know that it is still a fairly short game that can be completed within a week. Definitely worth picking up.

title: Vagrus - The Riven Realms
review_title: Sunless sea/bannerlord/and kenshi had a baby
review_text: Yeah im not kidding you explore a vast world via a comitatus(caravan) as a Vargus(Nomad leader) you are trader/transport/adventurer/mercenary all wrapped into one. You travel via a node system that has distance via paths for how much movement it takes to traverse you must prepare for the desert otherwise it and your comes(crew) will eat you alive. It does have a reputation system with factions and a hidden criminal system. Lots of lore and reading tons of decision making. You will feel like one vargus among many people in the world you have some importance but not much. You must live in the desert by acquring coin. You will be mostly a tradr and taxi. However its fun and you never know what is instore.

title: Dollhouse: Behind the Broken Mirror
review_text: Dollhouse has surprisingly been an IP for years, the first title going through some sort of developmental hell ages ago. I remember waiting what felt like a decade for the original to drop, and being quite disappointed when it did. I honestly wasn't expecting a sequel to even happen. The first was pretty bad, likely due to multiple factors including the split focus between single and multiplayer, though it had some good ideas. This follow up is a strictly solo affair and does manage to exceed the original in many ways, though not enough to really stand out unfortunately. I would advise against a full price purchase. In a world with the likes of Madison, Tormented Souls and Still Wakes The Deep, this simply doesn't rise to a standard worthy of its asking price. The controls are stilted, combat equal parts boring and frustrating, graphics are fine, occasionally nice but mostly by-the-numbers 'indie-horror'. If you really are curious, wait for a sale.

review_text: I'll preface with an opinion; I have not beaten The First Berserker: Khazan yet, but this will most likely be my personal GOTY. This game [so far] has been a tour de force of game development. At it's core, it is a satisfying blend of punchy, frenetic combat, looping linear exploration, an interesting world, and light rpg mechanics. Sound familiar? For fans of the genre, it will be, and yet it's not entirely derivative for a genre so full of hits. Gameplay is a mix of parries, dodges, stance breaking, and special skills. The skill tree features a path for each of the 3 weapon types, one for shared skills, and one more, but that's a spoiler.  The setting is very much dark fantasy. high castles, jagged peaks, dank caves, bandits and deadly monsters. Think of Kentaro Miuras work. The visual design is unique and beautiful, the music is tense and somber, and the voice acting is fantastic, especially from our duo protagonists. If you like this genre, play the demo, see what I mean.

title: The First Berserker: Khazan
review_text: Yes, best, I said BEST! The First Berzerker: Khazan, offers a both unique but also familiar experience. The art style is completely unique, but I guess the best way to explain it is BOTW meets Sekiro with a manga feel. The games combat is reminiscent of Sekiro, Lies of P, and Bloodborne. The games other features, mainly item progression, is similar to nioh, with lots of variations of the games same 3 weapon types.  The games map, while not open world, is also not entirely linear, offering different locations to chose to explore. The games progression of attributes is similar to classic fromsoft souls games, just at a slower place. It also uses lacrima (souls) as both currency and a method of leveling up, which you drop and can retrieve upon death. It has a skill tree similar to recent Assasins creed games, with unique abilities for each weapon type.  Khazan has issues, no hard difficulty, gang fights, to much loot, etc. But overall, it's nearly perfect. A true 10/10 experience.

title: The First Berserker: Khazan Deluxe Edition
review_text: Yes, best, I said BEST! The First Berzerker: Khazan, offers a both unique but also familiar experience. The art style is completely unique, but I guess the best way to explain it is BOTW meets Sekiro with a manga feel. The games combat is reminiscent of Sekiro, Lies of P, and Bloodborne. The games other features, mainly item progression, is similar to nioh, with lots of variations of the games same 3 weapon types.  The games map, while not open world, is also not entirely linear, offering different locations to chose to explore. The games progression of attributes is similar to classic fromsoft souls games, just at a slower place. It also uses lacrima (souls) as both currency and a method of leveling up, which you drop and can retrieve upon death. It has a skill tree similar to recent Assasins creed games, with unique abilities for each weapon type.  Khazan has issues, no hard difficulty, gang fights, to much loot, etc. But overall, it's nearly perfect. A true 10/10 experience.

title: BLEACH Rebirth of Souls
review_title: Not worth the price of admission
review_text: A 20-30$ game that charges AAA prices and should only be bought on discount.  A good fighting game with fun mechanics that are easy to pick up over time, but is severely dragged down by its low production costs. The cutscenes show little to no animation, bad pacing and editing choices lead to a stale boring experince. Instead of a comprehensive cinematic experience that retells the best parts of Bleach, we're given characters standing around expositioning cliffnotes around action but show nothing with. This is not a game that'll make new Bleach fans or completely satisfy old ones. It is a good fighting game, but not worth its price. -No og Bleach music ops ends or osts from the anime. -You can NOT play Orihime Inoue or Vizords other than Shinji. :( +og voice actors make a return but not all. Voice direction is poor. Orihime is not strong and abilities are limited but she can still be used in a fighting game with unique mechanics.  6/10 recommend for Bleach fans who want a fighting game

title: Atelier Yumia: The Alchemist of Memories & the Envisioned Land (Xbox One)
review_text: Firstly the Game is great, haven't had fun for years. Secondly the final boss is hard as h3ll. You have to be lvl 100 with good *** weapons, armor and rings for each character. The boss has 3 stages, each time you get its health half way it goes to a new boss stage. My first attempt i thought i was ready, i wasn't. Each regions as it's own boss to move to the next region and there's 4 regions. There's a building function that i like but with the camp sites you can't build a lot. And the game may crash every few hours. During my first play through some of the functions didn't work because it was using the demo save, so there was a lot that didn't work. There's NG+ so make S Tier weapons and stuff before going to NG+. To get NG+ you have to kill the final boss. NG+ will let you keep the weapons, armor and rings in a new save. So rekt those bosses with ease now in NG+. This game reminds me of far cry or just cause. The characters, you'll love them. Oh yeah there's also the jiggle physics.

Mod menu where people can import their own creations into the game (similar to snowrunner or farming sim)

review_title: The problem with being a game people want to hate
review_text: I am currently 22 hours into the game and I do have some thoughts. This is an e early review. Most of this game I love, as a die hard fan of the Assassin's Creed series who has played all the games. The combat is satisfying, the graphics are stunning. Most characters are great, the story is interesting. Though the facial animations are awful. The cut scenes are terrible. But that's to be expected at this point. At the end of the day, I don't know why I'm writing this review. Because no matter how hard I try to tell people about all the good this game has, they will never listen. Because Assassin's Creed Shadows is a game people want to hate, because of the publisher Ubisoft. This game will never get the praise it deserves because it is clouded in controversy.

Additionally, I really like that they added some online play to the game because that was one of the things that the original game needed and that made it really convenient for people who can't really find other friends around to play the game with. Overall, I'm very pleased with what I recieved with RCG2 and would recommend this game to anyone looking for a new game to play or any og fans who want some more River City Action! title: Storyblocks + Cat Games + Soko Games (BUNDLE)
review_text: Doctor Cat is, at its heart, a jigsaw puzzle game.  There are 12 images, with square pieces instead of cut shapes already set on the board.  You swap pairs anywhere, not just next to one another.  Difficulty determines how many square pieces are used.  Wrapped around each puzzle is a small story -a patient kitty who has an issue, a high level description of their issue, the picture matching the theme (bill stress, unhealthy eating, gambling, etc.), and then the Doc saying a short platitude about working together to fix the issue. The game's issues, however, need analysis. In the Office, you can change the difficulty.  Scrolling the text interacts with them by default.  Also, you are stuck in the office; you need to start a puzzle for Menu to work. The menu is also confusing.  Hard mode is hidden in the gallery, but Easy mode isn't. The painful part is the puzzle UI.  PC/mouse may be good, but Xbox controller gave me RSI.  No quick moves, except from just the left/right border.

title: One Lonely Outpost

The player character is scripted, games like these are better off with a strong silent type character who has minimal dialogue but, but in this game they get full paragraphs with minimal player input, so it's a lot of your character talking. The pet companion needs spacing, you start off with a talking cat that constantly hovers over your character that blocks interaction, which is problem when farming. The map in this game is very vague, each region image looks the surface of mars but blurry, no indication on what is there only a short name.

That way we would know better what we are buying before spending our hard earned currency on an item we dont really need yet.  Controlls could be refined, perhaps allow a deadzone to be defined by players on controllers to prevent snap back that spins the directional orientation of the character away for the intended target when the player releases the annolog stick during farming tasks. review_text: Full playthrough done in co-op with my spouse. CB:TtR is pretty well put together for a kids game. There's a little challenge present throughout with little frustration. The zones are unique enough to keep it interesting, and they even introduce new platforming mechanics and tighter or quicker jumps as you progress. Basic info: 5 biomes 7 levels per biome -5 platform levels (1-5) -1 Schmup boss level (6) -1 minigame level (7) 3 stickers to collect per level w/1 guaranteed on the 7th 5 base characters w/dif buffs and 2 unlocked at end biome 4 Chapter & level select No VA, only written dialogue We didn't encounter any bugs while playing, and checkpoints were forgiving but not too frequent. Overall, we had a ton of laughs voice acting the written dialogue and blundering about. If you're playing solo, it may be less enjoyable. 15 USD is fair MSRP but since there's little replay value after the stickerbook, 5-10 on sale is a good target, especially if you're a Bear enthusiast.

review_title: For the price you can't go wrong
review_text: Solid chill maze / puzzle game. My only complaint is I think there is a decent amount of wasted potential with the content. Most of the mazes are singular paths with no puzzle solving really required. With 50 levels it doesn't feel like the game really starts until after level 30, and really only reaches its full potential in the last 5 levels. Way too many levels were spent on introducing the basics. I think if the pacing was changed so that the content of level 31+ was introduced around level 11 and we got more mazes that played like the last 5 levels this would be perfect. With all that said, the last 20 levels are good enough to be worth getting through the first 30 and a 5 star review.

It's perfect for what it is supposed to be, a co-operative horde shooter where every battle is dynamic and different from the last. The weapons feel right, Classes are on point, yet customizable and Combat is relentless & satisfying (including things like bullet drop and armor penetration). To me, ST:E is awesome.

review_title: We need to talk about level 54.
review_text: Level 54 is entirely RNG based.  As a completionist with a score of 275k+ at the time of writing this, I have faced some diabolical challenges. This is the first time I've ever played a level with such poor design, it requires using a metronome and resetting it twice. You included three elevations, each set with fire traps that alternate. Each elevation has a different amount of space between the ground and the next elevation. This changes how high the fox can jump to clear the traps in time. Let's talk about clearing the traps in time. They do not run at a consistent pattern. And for each elevation cleared, the game is thrown off by just a few frames, requiring you to reset the metronome. Why a metronome? To make up for the lack of any sound cues. "It's OK, just use the code to unlock the levels" like another reviewer mentioned, the code just starts the game at the first press of A. 54 is IMPRESSIVELY bad level design.

review_text: I'm putting this here to help out any console players still on the fence about this RPG. Now I'm not going to beat aroung the bush stating the obvious, leaving out major spoilers, of course. Here's a summary: It's 1872 at the time of your death in what is assumed to be late 18th century Russia. It is here that you assume the role of eternally 22 year old Lizaveta Morozov, the star of this wonderful story driven RPG.                                                                                                                                 The demo lets you have an idea of what it will be like to navigate your way through undeath via a multiple choice morality system to shape how you will interact with the world around you. Be mindful of the consequences, though, as your actions will also influence the people you know; as well as pave the way you affect the world in further detailed interactions that account for past decisions. There's multiple endings, so enjoy it!

review_text: They work fine,you just have to understand how Lara works. When you want to do a running jump make her walk to the edge then draw her guns then she'll do the hop back and hold jump right after she starts moving forward and she'll jump like shes supposed to,she needs at least two steps before she can do a long jump. You can also do her back and side flips with guns drawn, its easiest to reset the camera behind her while doing the flips. And for the camera remap the look button from RS to RB and double click it to reset it behind her when it gets funky. RT gets her out of the water and will make her grab ledges while stepping off of an edge, you have to slightly step off instead of full force running off. I hope this helps those wanting to use modern controls, it took a lil bit to figure this out but i have absolutely no issues with them after learning this myself.

review_text: You can make it if you run. No. You can't. Why not? Because what hunts you is faster. Blood Hunting has many issues to be aware of before playing. Walking is too slow and running is clicking the left joystick and uncomfortably holding it down. I did discover while running, if you crouch and stop, running stays locked in. Interior layouts are oddly designed. Do not stay by the yellow running car, it will overheat your Xbox. Grab the needed key and leave the area ASAP. Also, do not pause and select retry, it will restart the whole game over, no matter how far you are. However, retrying after dying is ok. There are checkpoints but more are needed. title: Snezhinka
review_text: I LOVED Marfusha and never played anything like it. I was sad when i finished it thinking i would never play anything similar... Now we got the perfect sequel. I am so passionate about this series. It needs to be bigger and continue. This game changed how i view the gaming industry. In a greedy, toxic and corrupt world this flawless gem managed to be polished with love and care. This game is a gift to the player, a reward. You can feel the love that went into the experience, the love that was meant for the player. There has never been a better mix of dark and wholesome. The story is so bleak yet each character is filled with life. This series is a hopeless struggle against tyrannical governments where everything is shrouded in misery, everything except the relationships built upon survival. Marfusha and her allies fought for their own reasons and now so will Snezhinka!

review_title: Great game but needs a bit more content.
review_text: Warriors abyss is an interesting take on the orochi series,blending the traditional 1 vs 1000 gameplay with rougelite elements. And it works for the most part,I'm having a ridiculous amount of fun using my favorite characters from both the dynasty/samurai warriors games while making some interesting builds. But at the same time warriors abyss feels like it doesn't take full advantage of the rougelite mechanics. To me there just isn't enough random encounters and it feels like I'm doing the same thing over and over again with little variation. Plus the game has a big problem with boss variety. There's only 5 major bosses in total,that's pretty small compared to other rougelikes like dead cells or hades. The game is genuinely good and I'm having fun but having more bosses and some more unique zones with crazier Rng would make the game immensly better.

review_text: Warriors abyss is an interesting take on the orochi series,blending the traditional 1 vs 1000 gameplay with rougelite elements. And it works for the most part,I'm having a ridiculous amount of fun using my favorite characters from both the dynasty/samurai warriors games while making some interesting builds. But at the same time warriors abyss feels like it doesn't take full advantage of the rougelite mechanics. To me there just isn't enough random encounters and it feels like I'm doing the same thing over and over again with little variation. Plus the game has a big problem with boss variety. There's only 5 major bosses in total,that's pretty small compared to other rougelikes like dead cells or hades. The game is genuinely good and I'm having fun but having more bosses and some more unique zones with crazier Rng would make the game immensly better.

title: Sid Meier's CivilizationÂ® VII
review_title: The Good The Bad And The Ugly.
review_text: As a Civ 5, and Civ 6 lover Civ 7 just leaves me asking "why". So first things first the Good on the Game. The Graphics are an upgrade from Civ 6. The new animations are a nice touch. One thing I am really enjoying is the new Army Commander system. The ability to control your armys in a new and unique way brings a nice twist to domination focused players, and expands the strategy aspect of the game. Now onto the bad stuff. The age changes in my opinion are aweful to the game since its more of you play 3 mini civ matches instead of 1, because every time the age changes you borderline get set back to having nothing. you keep your cities and SOME of your military units, but your economy and science get reset and you start over. Go back to the normal trading and Sc sytem. The Ugly of the game is that there are so few civilizations and NO TRUE START EARTH MAP. Which I imagine will be set behind a pay wall later. So in conclusion WHY change so much from civ 6 which was perfect and trash it.

review_text: The Fear of being a "one trick pony" has caused one of the saddest letdowns for the playerbase. An incredible amount of money has been made off of Civ6 alone, so why change it? If "passion" is no longer the motivation for developers anymore then i will talk logically in terms of making money. Why release a title that belongs to a different game entirely, and come to expect success? Call of Duty is still alive because of this one money-hungry rule. Civ7 is not worth the money. Absolutely no passion or business sense. I have no malice for Firaxis, but they need to be the "one trick pony" everyone loved. I genuinely feel for everyone that waited years for something they didnt want, and feel worse for the die hard fans that want their overpriced pre-order refunded. Civ7 will probably not be fixed in the eyes of 90% of the fans, but Civ8 has so much to live up to now.

review_title: Wow, okay.. this game is actually rather good!
review_text: What a surprise! I almost overlooked this title, and one could easily shrug it off after seeing the letters 'FMV'. However the execution here can be called perfect! Sharp HD visuals with excellent production values makes you feel like you're watching a recent modern film release. But the real draw here is the authentic Choose Your Own Adventure style gameplay which makes this both refreshingly casual, yet remarkably exciting! Its a gem that sufficiently scratches a major itch you never even knew you had! It's not perfect, as the video seems to pause on rare occasion, consequently having to briefly accelerate just to catch up (in my experiences). The only other quibble is that being a British game, some non-native players may have trouble following the heavily accented dialogue. There are subtitles, but they take something away from the overall cinematic presentation, in my opinion. Otherwise, the game is a very nice diversion, especially if you're looking for something somewhat unique!

review_text: I played this back when it was on GP and I thought it was okay for the strategy boardgame genre.  I was not impressed. I gave it another try.  My original assessment was right. It's much better as a group rogue style game and played that way. You are NOT going to win.  It's not a strategy rpg board game.   Your goal should be to grind out books BEFORE you lose.  Books are used to unlock classes, better gear, and POSITIVE events.  Use everything you have to finish a dungeon or kill a chaos boss to get lore books. Tips Focus on books!   Ignore the chaos meter.  At lvl 3 towers will pop that you destroy to lower to 2. Make sure you have 1 toon with high STR, SPD, and INT to destroy towers. Do "easy" town quests. Make sure you have 1+ high physical DAM and 1+ magic DAM to bypass resists. Avoid Herbalist.  Heal skill only works when using an herb.  Prices escalate quickly.  You NEED all money for gear, not herbs. Tinder pouch(camp) is your heal.  Lasts many turns, just go back.
