title: Sid Meier's CivilizationÂ® VII Deluxe Edition
review_title: The Good The Bad And The Ugly.
review_text: As a Civ 5, and Civ 6 lover Civ 7 just leaves me asking "why". So first things first the Good on the Game. The Graphics are an upgrade from Civ 6. The new animations are a nice touch. One thing I am really enjoying is the new Army Commander system. The ability to control your armys in a new and unique way brings a nice twist to domination focused players, and expands the strategy aspect of the game. Now onto the bad stuff. The age changes in my opinion are aweful to the game since its more of you play 3 mini civ matches instead of 1, because every time the age changes you borderline get set back to having nothing. you keep your cities and SOME of your military units, but your economy and science get reset and you start over. Go back to the normal trading and Sc sytem. The Ugly of the game is that there are so few civilizations and NO TRUE START EARTH MAP. Which I imagine will be set behind a pay wall later. So in conclusion WHY change so much from civ 6 which was perfect and trash it.

title: Sid Meier's CivilizationÂ® VII Deluxe Edition
review_text: The Fear of being a "one trick pony" has caused one of the saddest letdowns for the playerbase. An incredible amount of money has been made off of Civ6 alone, so why change it? If "passion" is no longer the motivation for developers anymore then i will talk logically in terms of making money. Why release a title that belongs to a different game entirely, and come to expect success? Call of Duty is still alive because of this one money-hungry rule. Civ7 is not worth the money. Absolutely no passion or business sense. I have no malice for Firaxis, but they need to be the "one trick pony" everyone loved. I genuinely feel for everyone that waited years for something they didnt want, and feel worse for the die hard fans that want their overpriced pre-order refunded. review_title: Triple A game developers should be ashamed.
review_text: Just goes to show we are living in a topsy-turvy world when games like this are not considered triple A, but starfield is? This game does not insult the player by being laughably easy, instead it challenges you to actually put your feet in Henrys shoes. I also love the armor system, reminds me of morrowind until bethesda took a arrow to the knee and got casual with weapons and armor in their newer titles. This game harkens to a age when games were unapologetically Hard, unique, and in general just not complete slop for the masses. You will get your moneys worth at full price i guarantee, I can not say the same for many "triple A" games in the last 5 years. So have you got what it takes to be hardcore or are you a milk drinker?

title: Rogue Waters
review_text: There are a number of little things that could be better, but this game is good because it gets most of the important things right.  The pacing is spot on.  Battles are fast but involved enough to not feel trivial.  The way ship fights impact the unit vs. unit combat is unique and works rather well.  Compared to most roguelites, I really liked that success was less dependent on what upgrades the RNG gives.  The combat mechanic of of forcing opponents backwards totally fits the swashbuckling theme. The biggest flaw is that this game is below average (but far from the worst) when it comes to feeling like you are getting stronger with each run.  There are other small things that could be better, but nothing that significantly impacted my enjoyment.

review_text: Lots of cool mechanics, addictive core loop, all the good stuff you want in a roguetac. Nicely presented too. Only negative i seen is that early game balance on either the boss fight or broadside battle could use some adjusting, imo. The boss fights early on aren't just hard, hard is good, but they're apparently impossible. The fort cannons can take out all your good fighters before the battle starts if you don't focus on them, but doing that means ignoring their buffs, so the enemy has bonus health, armor, and per turn healing, which means your normal crew cant damage them by just attacking. And they have 2 or 3 times as many fighters as you. I'm all for the grind, but you get strong enough to snooze thru normal fights WAY before you have any shot at the first boss, so you get to the boss fight and you try to die because it's faster that way.  But if you don't mind grinding all day early on, great game. Just be prepared.

title: Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector
review_text: ...it were a dead tree novel. High praise indeed. This game takes an already magical world brimming with cyberpunk, desperate stellar frontier drama, political intrigue, and no small amount of heart and digs deeper in every way. I didn't think I'd vibe w/the dice roll mechanic when I started the first one, but they improved it and made it deeper. Amos Roddy's soundtrack evoked both Brian Eno and early Moby in equal measure, giving the story an extra cybernetic oomph and emotional resonance. I spent 27 hours in a single playthrough, I wanted to savor every moment and was reluctant to let it end. Hell, if they can sustain the polished level of writing and plot development, I'd play a 100+ hour third entry with an even more complicated spider web of directions and interwoven subplots. I desperately want to get badk out to the Helion System and beyond to live amon its' denizens explore. Ad astra, ad aspera. And beyond the infinite.

title: Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector
review_text: i really enjoyed this game until i came across a situation where i found out that you can not voluntarily fail a contract even if it means continuing would "kill" you, so instead of abandoning the mission and accepting the consequences of the failure, you end up in a stress, dice break loop. After dying i completed the mission, but afterwards i uninstalled the game as i find this design just awful. I would have been fine failing the contract and all of the ramifications that entailed , but FORCING me to keep going until all of my dice break and getting a permanent glitch (or Game Over in hardcore) isn't interesting game design with the amount of contracts in the game that have a large number of steps in them. Failing the mission is fine, but when im 4/5th of the way through, and i know i cant continue without dying, LET MY VOLENTARILY FAIL and not force me to kill my character.

review_title: Pretty unique but far from explored idea.
review_text: Techno Banter is largely a text driven game with several mini games throughout, mainly the bouncer game. It's kind of limited on the game end but it has a great look, unique quirky characters and a great soundtrack. It's short and you can probably 100% the game in a few hours but I went through almost all the possible dialogue and beat the game 3x to get all achievments for about 14 hours of play. In the end it comes down to if you like odd characters and interactions in games. If you do this one should be good for you. I really hope they take this game and make a bigger and better sequel because it is a great foundation.

review_text: If you like French games and you like block pushing puzzles, you will almost certainly like this game. Sort of a "choose your own difficulty" type thing. The color palate and environment are tolerable for exactly as long as this game is. Like many French games its form over function, art over mechanics. The story is also a little...um obvious I guess? But by the same token its one relatively rare in video games. title: Eternal Strands
review_text: Enjoyed this game & the magic more than Avowed & Immortals of Aveum. Mainly for the gameplay. Story was solid, easy to follow with some interesting lore/codexes. Only complaint is it's too easy to start climbing. Kinetic fire & frost magic. 10 unique spells. Two of which can be used to traverse the map super fast late game & collect everything to get 100%, which took me 38 hours without a guide (can do Spellbound on dead Great Ark). Plus 9 weapon spells across 3 weapon types. Enemies can be weakened by fire or frost magic, & that magic can make it easier to get certain resources from enemies & rocks/trees. You upgrade your gear by increasing the amount of resources & the type of resources which, increases the stats & changes the look. Later in the game you can dye your gear, salvage & exchange resources. Defeat mini bosses to learn new spells & harvest them to Max out each unique spell. Weather can make some of the flights easier or harder. Adds some flavor to exploring areas again.

title: Eternal Strands
review_text: Eternal Strands was a refreshing mix of an open world, action and feel good game. Loved the characters, style, world building, story, and honestly everything about this game. Just finish playing through and will be playing it again soon. This is amazing for being this stuio's first game and I would be sooooooo excited if they made a sequel!

title: Eternal Strands
review_text: Not far in yet, but it's already promising. Combat's a bit loose. I'm glad they brought back Dragon Age's original magic wheel function. The magic interacting with enemis and environment is nice. Like, altering loot drops, cooling fires, creating bridges. No character creation, sadly, but altering dialogue choices seems to give the illusion that we craft our character's personality...which is nice. Very similar gameplay styles to Breath of the Wild and Fenyx Rising. So if ya like those games, I recommend this. If ya think that makes it a knockoff...you're an idiot and should feel bad. Get an education.

title: Eternal Strands
review_title: Very fun, very underated, A hidden jewel.
review_text: For what it is, this game is fun to play. It is a refreshing break from Undisputed, COD and Madden, 2K and other games that take a more realistic approach. This is a game of magic, enchantment and exploration. I enjoyed the fairytale, cartoonish world this game takes place in and the imaginative style of it's gameplay. The fanbase for this game would increase if more people gave it a chance, and saw how fun n engaging it is. The learning curve about aquiring strands and upgrading armore and weapons, etc. is worth it, once you see all the game has to offer.

title: Eternal Strands
review_text: Mom: We have Zelda at home Zelda at home: Okay, that's harsh. The game is really quite good, though it certainly wears its influences on its chest. It controls well, the weapon and armor upgrade system is fun to play around with, and the fights against the giant enemies are really quite fun, especially figuring out how to extract strands from them to upgrade your magic spells. Combat feels a lot of fun, tough the controls took me a bit of getting used to. They sit somewhere between a classic action RPG and a Soulslike, so I keep accidentally hitting the wrong button to attack. Not a big deal, though. It runs well, the voice acting is superb, and the story is good enough to keep me motivated to keep playing. I do think that some of the conversations can get a little long, but that might just be my impatience speaking there.

title: The Stone of Madness
review_text: My interest was piqued when I heard the talent and minds behind the Blasphemous franchise made this, after completing it, I can say it's definitely worth playing. It's an Isometric Real-Time Stealth/Tactics Game where you control a group of characters with different strengths and weaknesses, and work together to complete objectives. You have a Day and Night cycle, where you make preparations, and then move forward with your plan within the time given. Pretty solid, with a quick narrative, and intersting mechanics. Only complaint I have is the Bugs regarding NPC pathing. it can make or break a scenario depending on what you're trying to accomplish. I highly reccommend this one!

review_text: This game has significantly more polish than it's predecessor, and a lot of the clunckier systems have been streamlined, gutted, or completely reworked. I have only one complaint having completed my first playthrough on "tails of iron" difficulty, that being that the combat feels slower than he first game. Maybe its that im just coming off of bloody wiskers mode in the first game, but I never felt the same type of adrenaline ruch playing ToI 2 that I got playing ToI 1, I just felt so tanky that I never had to really get a feel for any of the bosses, most of them being defeated on the first few tries. However, this is not a negative for everyone, as the wombo-combos some of the bosses gave you in the first game can be a little... bullcrappy, but that was part of the charm. Overall, the game is good, and you should play it. Highly recommend.

title: Orcs Must Die! Deathtrap
review_text: I want to enjoy Deathtrap - the co-op chaos is fun, the trap system still feels good, and when everything clicks, it absolutely has tha classic OMD energy. That's what makes this so disappointing. The way the game has been handled has completely drained my enthusiasm. I came back expecting at least a small anniversary celebration and maybe some long-requested QoL improvements, like trap loadouts. Instead, I found out the game is leaving Game Pass just three days after it's anniversary. Pulling it from Game Pass with no anniversary event, no acknowledgment, and no update feels like a huge misstep. It sends a message to the community that the game is being quietly dropped. Why would I pay to own this game if I'm made to believe there will be no future content or updates? Buy it on sale for a couple hours of enjoyment, but don't expect it to be worth full price. Deathtrap is fun with friends, but the lack of care shown around it's anniversary seriously hurts how I'll remember this game.

title: Dreamcore
review_text: 4 stars bc the game is exactly what youd expect. Non linear, simple walking sim through liminal space. The VHS aesthetic layered over clean graphics works well. The sound design is good, use headphones. That being said, if you are like me and have never understood the hype around liminal spaces, this game wont help you understand. This is considered a psych horror game, and not once did I feel anything other than boredom. Not trapped, or claustrophobic, or anxious. Just felt like I was wasting my time. I was hoping the immersion in a game like this would help me 'get it,' and I guess this has proved Im just not the target audience for this sort of thing. Im only saying all this to make it clear that this is not a game for everyone, but if you really enjoy the aesthetics of liminal spaces this game does it well.

title: SYNDUALITY Echo of Ada
review_text: When in the thick of a fight with and a lone bounty sniper picks you off,losing the potenially 2 million credit priced equipment, the game shows its player driven economy at its lowest.  On the other hand when meeting up and teaming up with complete strangers all for a rare item, the comaraderie is well received. There is alot left to chance, which makes going out to complete missions a slog and unrewarding in most cases. Your cost to build equipment is completely imbalanced with anything above green tier. Anti cradle weaponry is only available to the "evil" faction which makes encounters with bounty targets heavily weighted towards the opponent and makes daily missions requiring munition weapon impossible unless a bp weapon is given, though with such a stringent bp for free it is unlikely.

title: SYNDUALITY Echo of Ada
review_title: Killed by forced PVP and easy deaths
review_text: I really wanted to like this game. Suffered hours of playing careful as possible and still too punishing. Relentless griefers scared off players. For playing as giant metal robots, everything kills in 1-5 hits. Better gear doesn't feel better since unlocking it forces you to play crushingly harder zones. Insurance abusers forced an update were you can no longer recover lost gear in time. Losing gear that takes hours to aquire to 2-hit kill monsters is draining. The robots are so much slower and weaker than their anime counterparts. Can't even choose unique melee and drills like the show. Android cosmetics are mostly real cash, and nobody else will see it at this point. Equipment controls are not smooth or quick to navigate for a game where you need to react quickly to not die so fast. Story Missions don't let you use custom mech; preset only. Just watch the anime and avoid this game.

title: SYNDUALITY Echo of Ada

Very consumer unfriendly practices.

review_text: Ender Lilies was excellent, but Ender Magnolia is masterful; this is what a Metroidvania SHOULD be.  Nearly everything has been improved over the 1st game:  the map is more detailed & pinpoints your positioning, you can use 4 abilities instead of 3 & they allow for vastly different play styles, equipment is far more versatile w/ more capacity for relics, etc.  I could go on & on, but you should see for yourself! Don't be fooled, though.  The game can be harsh difficulty-wise (especially the final boss when going for the good ending), but there are options available to lessen the burden of surviving in this bleak, yet beautifully detailed land... it's haunting seeing the parallels & possible consequences from how Lilies ended.  This land has it's own story to tell.  It's far better fleshed-out, yet just as engrossing & bittersweet by the end.  They clearly put a LOT of heart into this sophomore effort, & it shows everywhere! This developer is one to keep your eyes on. ðŸ‘

title: ENDER MAGNOLIA: Bloom in the Mist
review_text: I am a big fan of this subgenre of games; however, the opening hours of many games in the subgenre leave players stuck in the mire of bad maps, gated mechanics, & general drudgery. Ender Magnolias is the exception. The player starts with many movement & combat mechanic, but the true star of the show is the map: differentiating between unmapped, mapped but unexplored, and fully mapped is discernable at a glance. If that weren't enough, as you acquire mechanics, the previously locked areas gates on the map show a different color, AND show the applicable mechanic to open the area!                                                            Most metroidvanias get in their own (and the player's) wayof the "fun". Not Ender Magnolias.                                                                                                                        This has been my first ever game review, written with controller. Support these good people. -K

title: DYNASTY WARRIORS: ORIGINS
review_title: A pleasant blend of new and old
review_text: Every time a new DW game releases I am excited to play and come with the expectation that the combat and story will remain the same... and that's fine because I like warriors games. But they really mixed things up with a new original protagonist; the story is rewritten around this mysterious character and the voicelines (JP) and cutscenes feel so much more personal and cinematic than previous games. The combat is a blend of older mechanics and newer, action RPG mechanics that require a little more effort than mashing X or Y on enemies. I only a have a couple hours in but I'll say that this game gives the DW franchise a refreishing feel that it desperately needed. Good job developer team!

review_text: I like it for what it is. Just not liking that I can't create my own character or play as another character instead. This is why 4 was better. Overall the combat was fine. Maybe too many cinematics that you need to go through and conversations in between the main quest battles. Again DW4 did that better. Weapon RNG I'm not really a fan because of luck vs skill in obtaining upgrades. DW4 did it better with experience being the only way. Overall the game is entertaining so far but I can't imagine much for endgame after I beat the main campaign. DW4 offered numerous campaigns told through the perspective of different families giving more replay value. Would also be more fun to play co-op with a friend like older titles. Not hating, just fair criticism of what could've been improved or done different.

title: Hexa River
review_text: In Hexa River, you are tasked with connecting hex pieces by moving and rotating them around to form a river. There are only four different types of river pieces to use but with 40 levels to clear, it will get challenging. The controls work fine except at times, it feels like you're fighting the cursor to get it to move where you want it. The only other complaint I have is there are several levels where you can connect the start and end of the river without using every river piece available but the game won't let you move on. Every river piece has to be used for it to count. The reason why that gets annoying is because it discourages players from finding shorter, better solutions. Otherwise, all of the achievements unlock just fine and if you enjoy these types of puzzle games, you'll get along well with this one.

title: Star Wars Outlaws Deluxe Edition

review_text: Sure, it's got a LITTLE of that ol' Ubisoft checklist bloat, but I've been staying away from Ubi games for a while, so it's not the drag it could be. But most of the bugs and the other complaints seem to have been worked out for the most part - I've been having quite a lot of fun being as sneaky as I want to be, but not having my buzz harshed if I'm found out because I'm still able to fight my way out of a scrape and find some cover if I need it. And it manages a great, authentic SW feel that gets me right in the "'member? berries" w/o squeezing too hard. Idunno, maybe if I played the game at launch, I would've been a lot harsher, but as it is, I am enjoying myself quite a bit. It's the game I keep coming back to. It's the game I keep missing when I'm doing something else. I didn't expect that. Not from Ubisoft. Does it have issues? Sure, but who cares? It still manages to fulfill my lifelong wish of being a scoundrel in the SW universe since the 70s, and it does it pretty well.

title: Star Wars Outlaws Deluxe Edition
review_text: I wanted to like this game so badly, but the sheer volume of stealth in this game is absolutely exhausting. Every failed attempt results in a reloaded save from 30 minutes ago. From a studio that has given us some magnificent stealth games, this one plays like a 2000 splinter cell entry. The only marks Ican give this game is: Nix is cute, Sabacc is fun, and as always, Ubi knows how to immerse you in a world and make it feel alive.
